    // compileEntityCard lowers a portrait and its optional entity caption. The
    // image preset owns the portrait geometry and motion; position_x/position_y
    // can move the portrait so caption_layout can use the opposite side.
    func compileEntityCard(ri resolvedItem, src *semanticPlan, registry *assetRegistry) ([]Layer, error) {
        var currentStyle entityStyleVariant
        var hasStyle bool
        if ri.Item.EntityStyleID != "" {
            imageMotionOverride := ri.Item.MotionID
            captionMotionOverride := ri.Item.CaptionMotionID
            captionMotionParams := ri.Item.CaptionMotionParams
            style, ok := ResolveEntityStyle(ri.Item.EntityStyleID, src.entityStyleSampleKey(), src.VideoID, ri.Item.ID)
            if !ok {
                style = entityStyleRegistry.sample(entityStyleRegistry.query(nil), "", src.entityStyleSampleKey(), src.VideoID, ri.Item.ID)
            }
            // Layout, colour, image motion and caption motion all stay exactly as
            // the style (or the producer override) declares them. The selected
            // catalog motion reaches Chronon unchanged so GPU failures stay visible.
            currentStyle = style
            hasStyle = true
            ri.Item.MotionID = style.ImageMotionID
            if imageMotionOverride != "" {
                ri.Item.MotionID = imageMotionOverride
            }
            ri.Item.CaptionMotionID = style.CaptionMotionID
            if captionMotionOverride != "" {
                ri.Item.CaptionMotionID = captionMotionOverride
            }
            ri.Item.CaptionMotionParams = captionMotionParams
            ri.Item.CaptionLayout = style.CaptionLayout
            // SSOT typography (typography_ssot.go): the payload's explicit
            // typeface/color/layout always win over the preset default — same
            // precedence as the motion overrides above. The preset default only
            // fills in when the plan carries no choice, so selecting an entity
            // style can never silently retype or recolor a caption the
            // producer set (the old unconditional CaptionColor overwrite made
            // every render diverge per sampled style).
            if strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.CaptionColor) == "" {
                ri.Item.CaptionColor = style.CaptionColor
            }
            if strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.CaptionLayout) == "" {
                ri.Item.CaptionLayout = style.CaptionLayout
            }
            // Place the runtime portrait in one of two balanced columns, or center it
            // for below-caption layouts.
            x := 0.0
            switch style.ImageSide {
            case "left":
                x = -float64(src.Width) * 0.25
            case "right":
                x = float64(src.Width) * 0.25
            case "center", "below":
                x = 0.0
            default:
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("overlay: entity style %q has unsupported image side %q", style.Name, style.ImageSide)
            }
            // Entity style supplies the default editorial column, while an explicit
            // producer position (for example to clear a concurrent date card) wins.
            if _, explicit := numericValue(ri.Params["position_x"]); !explicit {
                ri.Params["position_x"] = x
            }
            if _, explicit := numericValue(ri.Params["position_y"]); !explicit {
                ri.Params["position_y"] = 0.0
            }
        }
        if ri.Item.MotionID == "" && ri.ImagePreset.ID != "" {
            ri.Item.MotionID = runtimeDefaultImageMotionID(src, ri.Item.ID)
        }
        resolvedImageMotion, err := resolveRegisteredMotion(ri.Item.MotionID)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("overlay: entity image motion %q: %w", ri.Item.MotionID, err)
        }
        img := imageLayer(ri, registry.Path(ri.Item.Assets[0].ID))
        if hasStyle && currentStyle.CameraMotionID != "" {
            img.Enable3D = true
        }
        if ri.ImagePreset.ID != "" {
            applyPresetDefinition(&img, ri.ImagePreset)
            var imgAnimation *LayerAnimation
            if ri.Item.MotionID != "" {
                imgAnimation, err = imageMotionAnimationResolved(ri.Item.MotionID, ri.Item.MotionParams, ri.End-ri.Start, ri.ImagePreset.Motion.Exit, ri.Item.ID, TargetImage, resolvedImageMotion)
            } else {
                imgAnimation, err = animationForPreset(ri.ImagePreset, "", ri.End-ri.Start)
            }
            if err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
            applyMotionRouting(&img, imgAnimation)
            // Keep the source portrait uncropped; an explicit position lets the
            // producer place it on either side while the preset retains its size.
            img.Position = []float64{0, 0}
            img.Fit = FitContain
        }
        defaultImageBox(&img)
        if x, ok := numericValue(ri.Params["position_x"]); ok {
            y, _ := numericValue(ri.Params["position_y"])
            img.Position = []float64{x, y}
        }
        // Entities with text own a portrait card: a non-vertical box is covered
        // into the supported portrait (same height and center), so the caption
        // compiled from its bounds follows automatically. Vertical images pass
        // through untouched.
        if strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.EntityCaption) != "" {
            autoFitEntityPortrait(&img)
        }
        if err := applyFrameTreatment(&img, ri.Item.Frame); err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("overlay: entity image item %q: %w", ri.Item.ID, err)
        }
        if ri.Item.MotionID != "" && ri.ImagePreset.ID == "" {

        }

        if resolvedImageMotion != nil {
            premium = premiumImageRecipeDefinition(resolvedImageMotion.definition)
        }
        layers, err := compilePremiumImageLayers(ri, src, img, premium)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        if caption := strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.EntityCaption); caption != "" {
            imageIndex := premiumImageLayerIndex(layers)
            captionItem := ri.Item
            captionLayer, err := compileEntityCaptionLayer(ri, src, captionItem, caption, &layers[imageIndex], "entity")
            if err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
            if premium != nil && len(premium.ImageRecipe.CaptionTracks) > 0 {
                premiumLayerActive(&captionLayer, premiumTracks(*premium, premium.ImageRecipe.CaptionTracks, captionLayer.DurationFrames))
            }
            layers = append(layers, captionLayer)
        }
        if premium != nil && premium.ImageRecipe.RequireCaption && strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.EntityCaption) == "" {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("overlay: motion %q requires entity_caption", premium.ID)
        }
    // semantic_image_caption.go owns the caption half of the image subsystem:

    func compileImageCaptionLayer(parent resolvedItem, src *semanticPlan, child semanticItem, caption string, image *Layer, childID string, role textRole) (Layer, error) {
        captionIdentity := parent.Item.ID + ":" + childID
        captionMotion := ""
        if child.CaptionMotionID != "" {

        }

            return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: item %q image caption has no positive image geometry", parent.Item.ID)
        }
        // The resolver owns the geometry: image bottom_center + margin anchor,
        // safe-area clamping and long-name font fitting all happen there. The
        // lowering below only writes the resolver's answer into the layer.
        layoutPosition := image.Position
        sequenceOffsetX, sequenceOffsetY := 0.0, 0.0
        if parent.Item.CameraMotionID != "" {
            // Resolve the label in the local viewport, then translate it back to the
            // portrait's world position so the camera carries the pair together.
            if len(image.Position) >= 2 {
                sequenceOffsetX, sequenceOffsetY = image.Position[0], image.Position[1]
            }
            layoutPosition = []float64{0, 0}
        }
        imageBounds := EntityCardImageBoundsFromCenter(src.Width, src.Height, layoutPosition, image.Size[0], image.Size[1])
        requestedFontSize := 0.0
        if parent.Item.CameraMotionID != "" {
            if value, ok := numericValue(parent.Params["font_size_px"]); ok {
                requestedFontSize = value
            }
        }
        layout, err := ResolveEntityCardLayoutAtSize(src.Width, src.Height, imageBounds, caption, child.CaptionLayout, requestedFontSize)
        if err != nil {
            return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: item %q entity caption layout: %w", parent.Item.ID, err)
        }
        // Vertical fallback: the resolver may shift the image up so the pair
        // image + margin + caption fits inside the safe area. Image layers are
        // positioned relative to the canvas center, so an upward canvas shift of
        // `shift` px converts to exactly minus `shift`; the caption's geometry
        // below is canvas-absolute.
        if shift := imageBounds.Y - layout.ImageBounds.Y; shift != 0 {
            if len(image.Position) < 2 {

            image.Position[1] -= shift
        }
        captionBounds := layout.CaptionBounds
        width := int(captionBounds.Width)
        if width < 1 {

        }
        captionLayerID := parent.Item.ID + ":" + childID + ":caption"

        // borrowing a phrase template, preset, or phrase-specific motion policy.
        if !motionAdmitsTarget(captionMotion, TargetCaption) {

        if !motionAdmitsTarget(captionMotion, TargetCaption) {

        }
        positionX := captionBounds.CenterX

            positionY += sequenceOffsetY - float64(src.Height)/2
        }

    // sequenceImageLayoutParams gives each image a portrait viewport. Cover crops
    // landscape padding so baked-in blurred side bands cannot dominate the photo.
    func sequenceImageLayoutParams(params map[string]any, src *semanticPlan, index int) map[string]any {
        if src == nil || src.Width <= 0 || src.Height <= 0 {
            return params
        }
        result := make(map[string]any, len(params)+5)
        for key, value := range params {
            result[key] = value
        }
        // Fill most of the frame so portraits remain the visual focus. The reserved
        // lower margin still gives the screen-space caption room beneath the image.
        portraitHeight := float64(src.Height) * sequencePortraitHeightRatio
        result["width"] = int(portraitHeight * 0.73)
        result["height"] = int(portraitHeight)
        result["position_x"] = float64(index * src.Width)
        result["position_y"] = 0.0
        result["fit"] = "cover"
        return result
    }
    
    // compileSingleImageLayer is shared by standalone images and composite
    // children; callers pass the correct animation controls for that semantic unit.
    func compileSingleImageLayer(ri resolvedItem, src *semanticPlan, assetPath string, preset PresetDefinition, motionID string, motionParams map[string]any, start, end int64, layerID string) (Layer, error) {
        var resolved *resolvedMotion
        var err error
        if motionID != "" {
            resolved, err = resolveRegisteredMotion(motionID)
            if err != nil {
                return Layer{}, err
            }
        }
        return compileSingleImageLayerResolved(ri, src, assetPath, preset, motionID, motionParams, start, end, layerID, resolved)
    }
    
    func compileSingleImageLayerResolved(ri resolvedItem, src *semanticPlan, assetPath string, preset PresetDefinition, motionID string, motionParams map[string]any, start, end int64, layerID string, resolved *resolvedMotion) (Layer, error) {
        layer := imageLayer(ri, assetPath)
        layer.ID = imageLayerID(layerID)
        layer.StartFrame, layer.DurationFrames = start, end-start
        applyPresetDefinition(&layer, preset)
        defaultImageBox(&layer)
        sequenceStatic := ri.Item.CameraMotionID != ""
        if sequenceStatic {
            motionID, motionParams, resolved = "", nil, nil
        }
        if motionID == "" && preset.ID != "" && !sequenceStatic {
            motionID = runtimeDefaultImageMotionID(src, layerID)
            if motionID != "" {
                var err error
                resolved, err = resolveRegisteredMotion(motionID)
                if err != nil {
                    return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: default image motion %q: %w", motionID, err)
                }
            }
        }
        if motionID != "" {
            var err error
            // Keep the selected motion ID intact. Replacing a failed GPU motion with
            // a different recipe concealed unsupported runtime behavior.
            animation, err := imageMotionAnimationResolved(motionID, motionParams, end-start, preset.Motion.Exit, layerID, TargetImage, resolved)
            if err != nil {
                return Layer{}, err
            }
            // Explicit image motion_id is authoritative for both entity and generic
            // images; 2.5D recipes are no longer silently discarded for portraits.
            applyMotionRouting(&layer, animation)
        } else if preset.ID != "" && !sequenceStatic {
            animation, err := animationForPreset(preset, "", end-start)
            if err != nil {
                return Layer{}, err
            }
            applyMotionRouting(&layer, animation)
        }
        if x, ok := numericValue(ri.Params["position_x"]); ok {
            y, _ := numericValue(ri.Params["position_y"])
            layer.Position = []float64{x, y}
        } else if layer.Position == nil {
            if ri.Kind == KindEntityImage {
                layer.Position = []float64{0, 0}
                layer.Fit = FitContain
            } else if position, ok := ri.Params["position"].(string); ok && strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(position), "center") {
                layer.Position = []float64{0, 0}
            } else {
                layer.Position = resolveImageLayout(preset.Layout, layer.BoxWidth, layer.BoxHeight, src.Width, src.Height)
            }
        }
        if y, ok := numericValue(ri.Params["position_y"]); ok {
            if layer.Position == nil {
                layer.Position = []float64{0, 0}
            }
            layer.Position[1] = y
        }
        if ri.Kind == KindEntityImage {
            layer.Fit = FitContain
            layer.EntityImage = true
        } else if fit, ok := ri.Params["fit"].(string); ok && (fit == "cover" || fit == "contain" || fit == "fill") {
            // Bounded payloads choose how pixels fill the authored box; the
            // default contain path is preserved when the key is absent.
            layer.Fit = fit
        }
        // Bounded clips the card inside its authored box (the renderer already
        // clips to Size/Radius); validation owns the contract, lowering only
        // keeps the authored fit instead of falling back to a preset default.
        if bounded, ok := ri.Params["bounded"].(bool); ok && bounded && layer.Fit == "" {
            layer.Fit = FitContain
        }
        frame := frameFromImageParams(ri.Params, ri.Item.Frame)
        if err := applyFrameTreatment(&layer, frame); err != nil {
            return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: image item %q: %w", ri.Item.ID, err)
        }
        return layer, nil

            img.Position = []float64{0, 0}
            img.Fit = FitContain
        }
        defaultImageBox(&img)
        if x, ok := numericValue(ri.Params["position_x"]); ok {
            y, _ := numericValue(ri.Params["position_y"])
            img.Position = []float64{x, y}
        }
        // Entities with text own a portrait card: a non-vertical box is covered
        // into the supported portrait (same height and center), so the caption
        // compiled from its bounds follows automatically. Vertical images pass
        // through untouched.
        if strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.EntityCaption) != "" {
            autoFitEntityPortrait(&img)
        }
        if err := applyFrameTreatment(&img, ri.Item.Frame); err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("overlay: entity image item %q: %w", ri.Item.ID, err)
        }
        if ri.Item.MotionID != "" && ri.ImagePreset.ID == "" {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("overlay: entity image item %q with motion_id requires image_preset_id", ri.Item.ID)
        }
        var premium *motion.MotionDefinition
        if resolvedImageMotion != nil {
            premium = premiumImageRecipeDefinition(resolvedImageMotion.definition)
        }
        layers, err := compilePremiumImageLayers(ri, src, img, premium)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        if caption := strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.EntityCaption); caption != "" {
            imageIndex := premiumImageLayerIndex(layers)
            captionItem := ri.Item
            captionLayer, err := compileEntityCaptionLayer(ri, src, captionItem, caption, &layers[imageIndex], "entity")
            if err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
            if premium != nil && len(premium.ImageRecipe.CaptionTracks) > 0 {
                premiumLayerActive(&captionLayer, premiumTracks(*premium, premium.ImageRecipe.CaptionTracks, captionLayer.DurationFrames))
            }
            layers = append(layers, captionLayer)
        }
        if premium != nil && premium.ImageRecipe.RequireCaption && strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.EntityCaption) == "" {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("overlay: motion %q requires entity_caption", premium.ID)
        }
        return layers, nil
    }
    // semantic_image_caption.go owns the caption half of the image subsystem:
    // linked-caption geometry and role-based lowering through the shared text
    // spec seam. Image layer lowering stays in
    // semantic_image_compile.go; composition validation in
    // semantic_image_validate.go.
    package overlay
    
    import (
        "fmt"
        "strings"
    )
    
    func compileImageCaptionLayer(parent resolvedItem, src *semanticPlan, child semanticItem, caption string, image *Layer, childID string, role textRole) (Layer, error) {
        captionIdentity := parent.Item.ID + ":" + childID
        captionMotion := ""
        if child.CaptionMotionID != "" {
            captionMotion = EntityCaptionMotionID(child.CaptionMotionID)
        } else {
            captionMotion = entityCaptionMotionIDForIdentity("", src.PlanID, src.VideoID, captionIdentity)
        }
        // A 3D caption motion is kept as declared: the text lowering derives
        // enable_3d from the animators it emits, so Chronon receives the camera-
        // backed caption exactly as the producer asked for it.
        if len(image.Size) < 2 || image.Size[0] <= 0 || image.Size[1] <= 0 {
            return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: item %q image caption has no positive image geometry", parent.Item.ID)
        }
        // The resolver owns the geometry: image bottom_center + margin anchor,
        // safe-area clamping and long-name font fitting all happen there. The
        // lowering below only writes the resolver's answer into the layer.
        layoutPosition := image.Position
        sequenceOffsetX, sequenceOffsetY := 0.0, 0.0
        if parent.Item.CameraMotionID != "" {
            // Resolve the label in the local viewport, then translate it back to the
            // portrait's world position so the camera carries the pair together.
            if len(image.Position) >= 2 {
                sequenceOffsetX, sequenceOffsetY = image.Position[0], image.Position[1]
            }
            layoutPosition = []float64{0, 0}
        }
        imageBounds := EntityCardImageBoundsFromCenter(src.Width, src.Height, layoutPosition, image.Size[0], image.Size[1])
        requestedFontSize := 0.0
        if parent.Item.CameraMotionID != "" {
            if value, ok := numericValue(parent.Params["font_size_px"]); ok {
                requestedFontSize = value
            }
        }
        layout, err := ResolveEntityCardLayoutAtSize(src.Width, src.Height, imageBounds, caption, child.CaptionLayout, requestedFontSize)
        if err != nil {
            return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: item %q entity caption layout: %w", parent.Item.ID, err)
        }
        // Vertical fallback: the resolver may shift the image up so the pair
        // image + margin + caption fits inside the safe area. Image layers are
        // positioned relative to the canvas center, so an upward canvas shift of
        // `shift` px converts to exactly minus `shift`; the caption's geometry
        // below is canvas-absolute.
        if shift := imageBounds.Y - layout.ImageBounds.Y; shift != 0 {
            if len(image.Position) < 2 {
                image.Position = []float64{0, 0}
            }
            image.Position[1] -= shift
        }
        captionBounds := layout.CaptionBounds
        width := int(captionBounds.Width)
        if width < 1 {
            width = 1
        }
        captionLayerID := parent.Item.ID + ":" + childID + ":caption"
        // Caption semantics resolve directly to a role-aware text spec, without
        // borrowing a phrase template, preset, or phrase-specific motion policy.
        if !motionAdmitsTarget(captionMotion, TargetCaption) {
            captionMotion = entityCaptionMotionIDForIdentity("", src.PlanID, src.VideoID, captionIdentity)
        }
        if !motionAdmitsTarget(captionMotion, TargetCaption) {
            return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: item %q caption motion %q is not supported for text captions", parent.Item.ID, captionMotion)
        }
        positionX := captionBounds.CenterX
        positionY := captionBounds.CenterY
        if parent.Item.CameraMotionID != "" {
            positionX += sequenceOffsetX - float64(src.Width)/2
            positionY += sequenceOffsetY - float64(src.Height)/2
        }
        styleParams := map[string]any{
            "position_x":   positionX,
            "position_y":   positionY,
            "font_size_px": captionBounds.FontSize,
        }
        // Run-level runtime text style is the explicit payload choice. Thread the
        // payload's look (font, glow, stroke, shadow) onto the caption layer so
        // entity captions render the same style as phrases; the caption's
        // geometry-resolved font_size_px stays untouched. Fall back to the
        // language-level fallback supplies the family when the caller did not
        // choose one. Entity composition presets never own a typeface.
        for _, key := range runtimeTextStyleKeys {
            if key == "font_size_px" {
                continue
            }
            if value, ok := child.Params[key]; ok {
                styleParams[key] = value
            }
            // Parent runtime style is the canonical payload choice for every
            // caption in the image recipe. Child animation/preset data supplies
            // defaults only; it cannot silently change typography between renders.
            if value, ok := parent.Params[key]; ok {
                styleParams[key] = value
            }
        }
        mergeStyle := func(value map[string]any) {
            if current, currentOK := styleParams["style"].(map[string]any); currentOK {
                merged := make(map[string]any, len(current)+len(value))
                for key, entry := range current {
                    merged[key] = entry
                }
                for key, entry := range value {
                    merged[key] = entry
                }
                styleParams["style"] = merged
            } else {
                styleParams["style"] = value
            }
        }
        if value, ok := child.Params["style"].(map[string]any); ok {
            mergeStyle(value)
        }
        if value, ok := parent.Params["style"].(map[string]any); ok {
            mergeStyle(value)
        }
        if family := strings.TrimSpace(child.CaptionFontFamily); family != "" {
            if parent.Item.CameraMotionID != "" {
                styleParams["font_family"] = family
            } else if _, parentChoice := parent.Params["font_family"]; !parentChoice {
                styleParams["font_family"] = family
            }
        }
        overrideFill := ""
        if style, ok := child.Params["style"].(map[string]any); ok {
            if fill, ok := style["fill"].(string); ok {
                overrideFill = strings.TrimSpace(fill)
            }
        }
        if style, ok := parent.Params["style"].(map[string]any); ok {
            if fill, ok := style["fill"].(string); ok {
                overrideFill = strings.TrimSpace(fill)
            }
        }
        if overrideFill == "" {
            overrideFill = strings.TrimSpace(child.CaptionColor)
        }
    
        if overrideFill != "" {
            if _, err := parseHexColor(overrideFill); err != nil {
                return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: item %q caption color: %w", parent.Item.ID, err)
            }
        }
        motionParams := child.CaptionMotionParams
        if motionParams == nil {
            motionParams = map[string]any{"enter_frames": 8}
        }
        captionSpec := resolvedTextSpec{
            Text: caption, BoxWidth: width, BoxHeight: int(captionBounds.Height),
            Size:     []float64{captionBounds.Width, captionBounds.Height},
            Position: []float64{positionX, positionY}, Style: &LayerStyle{Font: OfficialFontPathForLanguage(src.Language)},
            MotionID: captionMotion, MotionParams: motionParams,
            StyleParams: styleParams, MotionTarget: TargetCaption, StylePolicy: role,
            FontSize: captionBounds.FontSize, OverrideFill: overrideFill,
        }
        captionLayer, err := compileResolvedText(captionLayerID, image.StartFrame, image.StartFrame+image.DurationFrames, captionSpec)
        if err != nil {
            return Layer{}, fmt.Errorf("overlay: entity image caption %q: %w", captionLayerID, err)
        }
        captionLayer.CaptionForImageID = image.ID
        captionLayer.CaptionLayout = child.CaptionLayout
        return captionLayer, nil
    }
    
    // compileEntityCaptionLayer keeps entity-card call sites explicit while
    // sharing all geometry, role resolution, and lowering with image captions.
    func compileEntityCaptionLayer(parent resolvedItem, src *semanticPlan, child semanticItem, caption string, image *Layer, childID string) (Layer, error) {
        return compileImageCaptionLayer(parent, src, child, caption, image, childID, textRoleEntityCaption)
    }

    package overlay
    
    import (
        "math"
        "strconv"
        "testing"
    )
    
    // The render-plan `position` field carries TWO different meanings, one per
    // layer type, and the engine's decoder (render_plan_compiler_animation.cpp,
    // apply_layer_primitives) is the authority on which:
    //
    //   - text  — the value is the layer centre's ABSOLUTE canvas coordinate; the
    //     engine subtracts canvas/2 itself.
    //   - other — the value is an offset from the canvas centre.
    //
    // canvasBoxPosition is this repository's single owner of that conversion.
    // Emitting the wrong form for a text layer is not a cosmetic error: the engine
    // subtracts half a canvas a second time, so the layer lands half a canvas away
    // from the box it was positioned against. That is exactly what shipped — every
    // burned subtitle cue was authored at the bottom centre and rendered against
    // the top-left corner of the frame, clipped off the left edge.
    
    // TestCanvasBoxPositionMatchesEngineLayerSemantics pins both branches of the
    // conversion, and the fact that they differ by half a canvas — the discrepancy
    // that a single shared form used to hide.
    func TestCanvasBoxPositionMatchesEngineLayerSemantics(t *testing.T) {
        const canvasW, canvasH = 1920, 1080
        // A 320x80 box anchored at (1552,48): a top_right watermark with a 48px
        // margin, which is the shape the watermark test compiles.
        got := struct{ x, y, w, h float64 }{1552, 48, 320, 80}
    
        text := canvasBoxPosition("text", got.x, got.y, got.w, got.h, canvasW, canvasH)
        if len(text) != 2 || text[0] != 1712 || text[1] != 88 {
            t.Fatalf("text position = %v, want the box centre in absolute canvas coordinates [1712 88]", text)
        }
    
        image := canvasBoxPosition("image", got.x, got.y, got.w, got.h, canvasW, canvasH)
        if len(image) != 2 || image[0] != 752 || image[1] != -452 {
            t.Fatalf("image position = %v, want a canvas-centre offset [752 -452]", image)
        }
    
        if math.Abs(text[0]-image[0]) != canvasW/2 || math.Abs(text[1]-image[1]) != canvasH/2 {
            t.Fatalf("text and non-text forms must differ by exactly half a canvas, got %v vs %v", text, image)
        }
    }
    
    // TestBurnedCuePositionLandsBottomCenter is the regression guard for the shipped
    // P0, with the numbers taken from the plan that produced it: a bottom_center cue
    // on 1920x1080 with the standard 1800x70 safe-area box anchored at (60, 829).
    //
    // The emitted position must be the box centre in absolute canvas coordinates —
    // [960, 864] — because that is the form the engine reads for text layers and it
    // subtracts canvas/2 itself. The bug emitted the canvas-centre offset [0, 324]
    // instead, so the engine resolved the cue's centre to (0, 324): hard against the
    // left edge, a third of the way down, which is precisely where the rendered
    // frames showed it.
    func TestBurnedCuePositionLandsBottomCenter(t *testing.T) {
        const canvasW, canvasH = 1920, 1080
        // The safe-area box subtitleCueGeometry resolves for bottom_center.
        const boxX, boxY, boxW, boxH = 60.0, 829.0, 1800.0, 70.0
    
        position := canvasBoxPosition("text", boxX, boxY, boxW, boxH, canvasW, canvasH)
        if len(position) != 2 || position[0] != 960 || position[1] != 864 {
            t.Fatalf("burned cue position = %v, want absolute canvas centre [960 864]", position)
        }
    
        // Replay the engine's text branch: it subtracts canvas/2 and the resulting
        // offset is measured from the canvas centre, so it must reproduce the box
        // centre. This is the arithmetic that failed in production.
        resolvedX := position[0] - canvasW/2 + canvasW/2
        resolvedY := position[1] - canvasH/2 + canvasH/2
        if resolvedX != boxX+boxW/2 || resolvedY != boxY+boxH/2 {
            t.Fatalf("engine resolves cue centre to (%.0f,%.0f), want the box centre (%.0f,%.0f)",
                resolvedX, resolvedY, boxX+boxW/2, boxY+boxH/2)
        }
        // And the cue must sit in the bottom band, horizontally centred.
        if resolvedY < canvasH*0.7 {
            t.Fatalf("bottom_center cue centre y = %.0f is not in the bottom band of a %dpx canvas", resolvedY, canvasH)
        }
        if math.Abs(resolvedX-canvasW/2) > 1 {
            t.Fatalf("bottom_center cue centre x = %.0f is not horizontally centred", resolvedX)
        }
    }

    // canvasBoxPosition converts a box expressed in ABSOLUTE canvas coordinates
    // (top-left anchor + size) into the render-plan `position` field for a layer of
    // the given type.
    //
    // This function is the single owner of that conversion because the engine's
    // decoder (render_plan_compiler_animation.cpp:apply_layer_primitives) reads the
    // field with two different semantics:
    //
    //   - text  — the value IS the layer centre's absolute canvas coordinate; the
    //     engine subtracts canvas/2 itself.
    //   - other — the value is an offset from the canvas centre.
    //
    // Emitting one form for both types is what parked every burned cue in the
    // top-left corner: an absolute top-left anchor was handed to the text branch,
    // which subtracted canvas/2 a second time (960,540 on a 1920x1080 canvas), so a
    // bottom_center cue's centre landed at the anchor minus half a canvas.
    func canvasBoxPosition(layerType string, x, y, w, h float64, canvasW, canvasH int) []float64 {
        cx := x + w/2
        cy := y + h/2
        if layerType == "text" {
            return []float64{cx, cy}
        }
        return []float64{cx - float64(canvasW)/2, cy - float64(canvasH)/2}
    }

Ho controllato il render **r20a**. Il difetto è già dentro gli overlay prodotti dal nostro software di rendering: non sembra causato dagli stock ricevuti né dal Master che assembla il video.

- Nell’overlay grezzo, la foto è centrata, ma la didascalia “Alberto Stasi” è tagliata sul bordo sinistro: [frame overlay]( /tmp/r20a-overlay-1.png ).
- Nel video finale, a 20 secondi, compare una schermata bianca con il testo tagliato nell’angolo in alto a sinistra: [frame finale]( /tmp/r20a-final-20.png ).
- Gli overlay risultano video H.264 a pieno schermo, senza canale alpha. Quindi il problema riguarda il layout e la composizione in **RenderingGen/Chronon**: testo e immagini non vengono posizionati correttamente e, in quei punti, lo sfondo bianco copre il filmato.

Il worker remoto ha eseguito il job; la causa più probabile è la gestione delle coordinate nell’overlay renderer, non la macchina worker. Non ho modificato né ricodificato il video.

    // resolveTextSpecBase handles role-neutral text validation, wrapping, motion
    // inputs and preset typography. The role resolvers above then add their own
    // semantics before the shared geometry resolver finishes the spec.
    func resolveTextSpecBase(ri resolvedItem, src *semanticPlan) (resolvedTextSpec, int, error) {
        if strings.TrimSpace(ri.Item.Text) == "" {
            return resolvedTextSpec{}, 0, fmt.Errorf("overlay: item %q requires text (PipelineGen owns the displayed text)", ri.Item.ID)
        }
        wrapped, lines := wrapPhraseAt25(ri.Item.Text)
        spec := resolvedTextSpec{
            Text:         wrapped,
            MotionID:     ri.Item.MotionID,
            MotionParams: ri.Item.MotionParams,
            StyleParams:  ri.Params,
            MotionTarget: semanticTextMotionTarget(ri.Item, ri.Kind),
        }
        if fill, ok := ri.Params["fill"].(string); ok {
            spec.OverrideFill = strings.TrimSpace(fill)
        }
        // Preset style and family layout travel with the spec; the compiler never
        // re-derives them from a template lookup.
        if ri.Preset.ID != "" {
            style, err := resolvedTextPresetStyle(ri.Preset, src.Language)
            if err != nil {
                return resolvedTextSpec{}, 0, err
            }
            spec.Style = style
            spec.PresetID = ri.Preset.ID
            spec.PresetDef = ri.Preset
        }
        return spec, lines, nil
    }
    
    // resolveTextSpecGeometry resolves the common position and box after each role
    // has attached its fit policy. Explicit runtime geometry wins over preset
    // layout, then the canonical text canvas.
    func resolveTextSpecGeometry(ri resolvedItem, src *semanticPlan, spec resolvedTextSpec, lines int) resolvedTextSpec {
        posX, hasPosX := spec.StyleParams["position_x"].(float64)
        posY, hasPosY := spec.StyleParams["position_y"].(float64)
        if width, ok := numericValue(spec.StyleParams["width"]); ok && width > 0 {
            spec.BoxWidth = int(width)
        }
        if height, ok := numericValue(spec.StyleParams["height"]); ok && height > 0 {
            spec.BoxHeight = int(height)
        }
        if spec.BoxWidth <= 0 {
            spec.BoxWidth = src.Width
            if ri.Preset.Family == PresetText && ri.Preset.Layout.BoxWidth > 0 && ri.Preset.Layout.BoxWidth < spec.BoxWidth {
                spec.BoxWidth = ri.Preset.Layout.BoxWidth
            }
        }
        if spec.BoxHeight <= 0 {
            spec.BoxHeight = DefaultTextBoxHeight
            if ri.Preset.Family == PresetText && ri.Preset.Layout.BoxHeight > 0 {
                spec.BoxHeight = ri.Preset.Layout.BoxHeight
            }
        }
        if spec.FitPolicy == "none" {
            if requestedSize, ok := numericValue(spec.StyleParams["font_size_px"]); ok && requestedSize > 0 {
                minimumHeight := int(requestedSize*1.7) + 32
                if spec.BoxHeight < minimumHeight {
                    spec.BoxHeight = minimumHeight
                }
            }
        }
        if lines > 1 {
            needed := lines*phraseLineHeight + 16 // glow/shadow padding
            if needed > spec.BoxHeight {
                if needed > src.Height {
                    needed = src.Height
                }
                spec.BoxHeight = needed
            }
        }
        spec.Position = resolveTextLayout(src.Width, src.Height)
        if hasPosX {
            spec.Position[0] += posX
        }
        if hasPosY {
            spec.Position[1] += posY
        }
        return spec
    }

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -u -o pipefail
    DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd )"
    API="http://127.0.0.1:8000"
    RUN="r20b-overlay-fix"
    PAYLOAD="$DIR/r20minuti-overlay-fix-r20b.generate.json"
    TOKEN="${VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN:-}"
    if [[ -z "$TOKEN" ]]; then echo "no admin token" >&2; exit 3; fi
    RESP="$DIR/$RUN-submit-response.json"
    code="$(curl -sS -o "$RESP" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$API/api/script/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $RUN-20261103-r20b" --data-binary "@$PAYLOAD")"
    echo "submit http=$code"
    python3 - "$RESP" <<'PY'
    import json,sys
    x=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); print('job_id:',x.get('job_id'),'status:',x.get('status'))
    PY
    JOB="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("job_id",""))' "$RESP")"
    if [[ -z "$JOB" ]]; then echo "no job id" >&2; exit 4; fi
    LOG="$DIR/$RUN-submit-poll.log"
    : > "$LOG"
    for _ in $(seq 1 500); do
     ts="$(date -Iseconds)"
     body="$(curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/api/jobs/$JOB/full")"
     status="$(printf '%s' "$body" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d.get("status") or d.get("current_status") or "UNKNOWN")')"
     printf '%s %s\n' "$ts" "$status" >> "$LOG"
     case "$status" in
      SUCCEEDED|FAILED|CANCELED|COMPLETED|ERROR)
       printf '%s\n' "$body" > "$DIR/$RUN-job-full.json"
       echo "terminal=$status"
       exit 0;;
     esac
     sleep 5
    done
    echo 'poll budget exhausted' >&2
    exit 5

    void apply_layer_primitives(chronon3d::LayerBuilder& builder,
                                const LayerPlan& layer,
                                int canvas_width,
                                int canvas_height,
                                FrameRate fps,
                                const FollowPathEvaluators* precompiled_follow_path) {
        if (layer.transition_in) builder.transition_in(compile_transition(*layer.transition_in, fps));
        if (layer.transition_out) builder.transition_out(compile_transition(*layer.transition_out, fps));
        if (layer.parent) builder.parent(*layer.parent);
        if (layer.track_matte) {
            switch (layer.track_matte->type) {
                case TrackMatteTypePlan::Alpha:
                    builder.track_matte_alpha(layer.track_matte->source); break;
                case TrackMatteTypePlan::AlphaInverted:
                    builder.track_matte_alpha_inverted(layer.track_matte->source); break;
                case TrackMatteTypePlan::Luma:
                    builder.track_matte_luma(layer.track_matte->source); break;
                case TrackMatteTypePlan::LumaInverted:
                    builder.track_matte_luma_inverted(layer.track_matte->source); break;
            }
        }
        if (layer.time_remap) {
            if (layer.time_remap->speed)
                builder.speed(*layer.time_remap->speed);
            if (layer.time_remap->reverse)
                builder.reverse();
            if (layer.time_remap->freeze_frame)
                builder.freeze_frame(*layer.time_remap->freeze_frame);
            if (layer.time_remap->animation) {
                auto& remap = builder.time_remap_anim();
                for (const auto& key : layer.time_remap->animation->keyframes)
                    add_animation_keyframe(remap, *layer.time_remap->animation, key,
                                           scalar_value(key, "time_remap"));
                remap.compute_roving();
                remap.compute_auto_beziers();
            }
        }
        if (layer.enable_3d) builder.enable_3d();
        if (layer.screen_space) builder.screen_space();
        if (layer.depth_role) {
            builder.depth_role(depth_role_value(*layer.depth_role));
            builder.depth_offset(layer.depth_offset);
        }
        if (layer.start_frame) builder.from(*layer.start_frame);
        if (layer.duration_frames) builder.duration(*layer.duration_frames);
        if (layer.position_dimensions >= 2) {
            // Render-plan geometry (Text, Shape) is authored in canvas coordinates
            // with a top-left box origin, while LayerBuilder transforms are centred
            // on the canvas. Convert the box origin once; motion tracks remain
            // additive offsets from this resolved placement.
            if (layer.id.ends_with("__stroke")) {
                const float sw = layer.size_dimensions >= 2 ? layer.size[0] : 0.0f;
                const float sh = layer.size_dimensions >= 2 ? layer.size[1] : 0.0f;
                builder.position({
                    layer.position[0] + static_cast<float>(canvas_width) - sw * 0.5f,
                    layer.position[1] + static_cast<float>(canvas_height) - sh * 0.5f,
                    layer.position[2]});
            } else if (layer.type == LayerType::Text || layer.type == LayerType::Shape) {
                builder.position({
                    layer.position[0] - static_cast<float>(canvas_width) * 0.5f,
                    layer.position[1] - static_cast<float>(canvas_height) * 0.5f,
                    layer.position[2]});
            } else {
                builder.position({layer.position[0], layer.position[1], layer.position[2]});
            }
        }
        if (layer.scale_dimensions >= 2)
            builder.scale({layer.scale[0], layer.scale[1], layer.scale[2]});
        if (layer.rotation_dimensions > 0)
            builder.rotate({layer.rotation[0], layer.rotation[1], layer.rotation[2]});
        builder.skew({layer.skew_angle_deg, layer.skew_axis_deg});
        if (layer.blend_mode) builder.blend(*layer.blend_mode);
        if (layer.opacity) builder.opacity(*layer.opacity);
        apply_animation_tracks(builder, layer, canvas_width, canvas_height, fps,
                               precompiled_follow_path);
    }
    
    #include "../compiler_stages.hpp"
    
    namespace chronon3d::compiler::stages {
    void lower_text(const render_plan::RenderPlan& plan, CompiledProgramData& out) {
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < plan.layers.size(); ++i) {
            const auto& layer = plan.layers[i];
            if (layer.type != render_plan::LayerType::Text) continue;
            const auto text_index = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(out.text_values.size());
            out.text_values.push_back(layer.text);
            const auto program_index = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(out.texts.size());
            out.texts.push_back({
                i, text_index, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(layer.text_animators.size())});
            out.layers[i].text_program_index = program_index;
        }
    }

Il problema è nel **tipo e nella durata dell’animazione scelta nel nostro progetto**: le animazioni attuali sono brevi transizioni d’ingresso (per esempio fade o zoom), poi l’immagine resta ferma. Alcune finestre durano solo circa un secondo, quindi il movimento può essere quasi impercettibile e sembrare un PNG statico.

Quindi la causa probabile è **la configurazione/pianificazione degli overlay nel nostro PipelineGen/RenderingGen**, non il worker remoto né il file MP4 finale. Se vuoi un movimento visibile per tutta la permanenza dell’overlay, va modificata l’animazione o la sua durata.

    ## 3. Walls, in the order they saturate
    
    1. **W1 — Drive quota (today).** 750 GB/day/account. At 1k/h the account dies

    3. **W3 — Monolithic storage churn (~30k/h).** 1.78–5.3 TB/h of unique output

    - **LANDED** — singleflight dedupe per cache key. The 25-requests-for-12-assets
      waste is coalesced: 25 logical `Resolve()` calls collapse to 12 physical
      upstream transfers and 13 coalesced waiters, pinned by
      `TestManager_25Requests12AssetsSingleFlight`.
    - **Metric semantics (important):** `duplicate_download_bytes` is NOT a
      waste counter to drive to zero — it is the bytes the dedupe AVOIDED. The
      acceptance criterion is the PHYSICAL side:
    
      ```
      physical upstream transfers == number of unique assets (12)
      physical upstream bytes     == one copy of each unique asset
      coalesced waiters            == duplicate requests (13)
      coalesced_avoided_bytes      == waiters that did not hit upstream
      ```
    
      A non-zero `duplicate_download_bytes` is therefore expected and healthy
      whenever concurrent waiters exist; only physical replication of the same
      asset would be a regression.
    - **Evidence:** pinned test above (`-count=1` and under `-race`); canary
      inspection of `cache_miss_bytes=0` after warm.

    | Model | Egress volume/h | CDN-class cost @ $0.005–0.01/GB | Notes |

    | Manifest-first | ~0.43 TB (audio) | **$2–4/h** | 30–60× cheaper; chunks cached at edge |
    
    Zero-egress object storage (R2-class) shifts origin cost to ~0 either way,
    but the churn/limit walls remain — only the representation change removes them.

    # Velox — Target 100% and Definition of Done
    
    Status: canonical execution plan
    Owner: Velox architecture
    Last reconciliation: 2026-06-26
    
    > **Stato architetturale (Agosto 2026):** la separazione in tre repository è
    > completata — Velox è una render farm headless, InstaeditLogin è l'editor/BFF,
    > VeloxFrontend è la UI. Vedi [`ROADMAP.md`](../../ROADMAP.md) (stato per area),
    > [`FUTURE.md`](../../FUTURE.md) (migliorie future) e
    > [`DEPLOY-CHECKLIST.md`](../../DEPLOY-CHECKLIST.md) (playbook di deploy).
    
    This directory is the only completion roadmap for Velox. Historical audits, temporary PR plans and snapshot ticket lists must not be used as active implementation contracts.
    
    A checkbox may be marked complete only when the change is merged into `main`, the required tests pass and the evidence is reproducible. Code that merely compiles is not complete.
    
    ## What Velox must become
    
    Velox is a headless, deterministic, server-side distributed video generation and composition runtime.
    
    The completed system must:
    
    - accept a project or generation request and compile it into an immutable render contract;
    - expand one Job into a persistent Task DAG;
    - execute independent work in parallel on CPU-first remote workers;
    - select workers from canonical executor capabilities, current resources, measured cost and data locality;
    - reuse verified content-addressed artifacts and precompositions;
    - recover automatically from master restart, worker crash and network partition;
    - declare success only after the final artifact is present, verified and READY;
    - expose enough telemetry to explain every placement, retry, failure and performance result;
    - promote the same signed image digest from staging to production without rebuilding;
    - remain usable without a graphical editor, browser renderer or GPU dependency.
    
    ## Non-negotiable invariants
    
    - One state owner, one writer and one mutation path for every important responsibility.
    - The master plans, schedules and owns Task lifecycle state.
    - Workers execute assigned contracts and never invent graph edges or reinterpret projects.
    - Registries own executor, resolver, provider, compiler, estimator and sampler selection.
    - SQLite stores authoritative state and metadata; BlobStore stores binary payloads.
    - Memory structures are reconstructible and never authoritative.
    - Job `SUCCEEDED` is written only by verified artifact finalization.
    - Task execution identity is the tuple `task_id`, `attempt_id`, `worker_id`, `lease_id` and revision where applicable.
    - No silent fallback, dual-write, hidden retry path or parallel renderer implementation.
    - CPU-only workers are first-class; GPU support is an explicit capability, never an implicit requirement.
    - Production gRPC is mTLS fail-closed.
    - Every production release is traceable to commit, version, image digest, SBOM, provenance and signature.
    
    ## Completion policy
    
    For every item below, evidence must include the relevant combination of:
    
    - merged commit or pull request;
    - targeted unit and invariant tests;
    - integration or E2E output;
    - database assertions;
    - logs and metrics;
    - rendered fixture, `ffprobe` output and SHA-256;
    - image digest, SBOM, provenance and signature;
    - recovery or failure-injection report.
    
    Do not check an item based only on a document, mock or manual observation.
    
    ## Master gates
    
    ### Gate 1 — Runtime correctness and recovery
    
    Detailed checklist: [01-RUNTIME-CONSISTENCY-AND-RECOVERY.md](01-RUNTIME-CONSISTENCY-AND-RECOVERY.md)
    
    - [ ] `main` passes the canonical verification command from a clean checkout.
    - [ ] Job, Task, TaskAttempt, lease and artifact state cannot diverge after partial failure.
    - [ ] Expired leases always produce a durable retry or a durable terminal result.
    - [ ] Late or duplicate reports cannot replace the winning attempt.
    - [ ] Master restart, worker crash and network partition recover automatically.
    - [ ] Drain and shutdown leave no orphan process or READY partial artifact.
    - [ ] Final artifact verification remains the only success gate.
    
    ### Gate 2 — CI, E2E and release integrity
    
    Detailed checklist: [02-CI-TESTING-AND-RELEASE.md](02-CI-TESTING-AND-RELEASE.md)
    
    - [ ] Go, C++, architecture, migration and security checks run in the canonical CI path.
    - [ ] Native C++ tests are executed, not only compiled.
    - [ ] Real gRPC workload E2E is a required check.
    - [ ] Production-like mTLS E2E is a required release check.
    - [ ] Missing mandatory dependencies fail CI instead of skipping critical tests.
    - [ ] Master and worker images are reproducible, signed and promoted by digest.
    - [ ] Branch protection blocks merge without all required checks.
    
    ### Gate 3 — Production operations and security
    
    Detailed checklist: [03-PRODUCTION-OPERATIONS-AND-SECURITY.md](03-PRODUCTION-OPERATIONS-AND-SECURITY.md)
    
    - [ ] Every worker passes a machine-readable production doctor.
    - [ ] Worker identity, certificate and allowlist membership are unambiguous.
    - [ ] Liveness and readiness are separate and used correctly by containers and operators.
    - [ ] Capacity and admission control prevent CPU, memory and disk overcommit.
    - [ ] Metrics, alerts and correlated logs cover the complete runtime.
    - [ ] PKI monitoring, rotation, revocation, rollout and rollback are tested.
    - [ ] Every supported hardware class passes canary and soak certification.
    
    ### Gate 4 — Distributed rendering, performance and scale
    
    Detailed checklist: [04-DISTRIBUTED-RENDERING-PERFORMANCE-AND-SCALE.md](04-DISTRIBUTED-RENDERING-PERFORMANCE-AND-SCALE.md)
    
    - [ ] One Job expands into a real persistent multi-Task DAG.
    - [ ] Independent layers execute before unrelated slow inputs are available.
    - [ ] Verified precompositions are reused by deterministic content hash.
    - [ ] Placement uses capability, resources, cost and locality.
    - [ ] Safe work can be temporally sharded and recomposed without a full rerender.
    - [ ] Critical path, parallel efficiency, cache hit ratio and estimation accuracy are measured.
    - [ ] Representative workloads meet defined correctness and performance SLOs.
    
    ## Required execution order
    
    1. Restore and enforce a clean green baseline.
    2. Close runtime consistency and recovery gaps.
    3. Make real E2E and native tests required.
    4. Complete production doctor, security and operational certification.
    5. Complete distributed DAG, cache, scheduling, sharding and performance work.
    6. Run release candidate recovery suite and soak tests.
    7. Promote one canary worker by digest.
    8. Expand by hardware class only after the canary evidence is green.
    
    A later phase may be developed in parallel only when it does not change an owner, schema or contract required by an earlier phase.
    
    ## Pull request rules
    
    - Start from current `origin/main` after `git fetch origin`.
    - One responsibility and one focused set of files per PR.
    - Search for existing code before adding new code.
    - Extend canonical registries, resolvers, samplers and repositories; do not duplicate them.
    - Rebase frequently on `origin/main`.
    - Run targeted tests plus the canonical verification gate.
    - Do not commit generated videos, output directories, caches or build products.
    - After push, inspect `git log -n 5 --oneline` and the remote diff.
    - Do not merge a documentation claim unless the code and evidence agree with it.
    
    ## Final 100% verdict
    
    Velox reaches 100% only when every master gate is checked and the final release candidate demonstrates all of the following in one reproducible run:
    
    ```text
    Doctor = READY
    mTLS workload E2E = PASS
    Job = SUCCEEDED
    All required Tasks = SUCCEEDED
    Winning TaskAttempts = SUCCEEDED
    Final Artifact = READY
    Artifact SHA-256 = verified
    ✓ • 0ms

## Assistant

Sì, si può cambiare approccio, ma dai numeri di oggi il **10× sul job completo non si ottiene semplicemente rendendo più veloce il render**: il worker ha assemblato il video in circa **13 secondi**. Nel job più recente, `remote_final_job` ha occupato circa **115 secondi**; le metriche riportano anche 51 secondi di coda e circa 51 di handoff, ma sono misure che possono sovrapporsi.

Le strade più promettenti sono:

1. **Togliere l’attesa evitabile tra Master e worker.** Misurare e ridurre separatamente coda, preparazione e handoff degli asset. Per un job appena osservato sono il primo bersaglio: il lavoro di assemblaggio dura molto meno dell’attesa che lo precede.
2. **Preparare gli asset mentre il contenuto viene generato.** Il worker potrebbe ricevere e verificare in anticipo materiali già noti, riutilizzando la cache locale. Così il job non aspetta che tutti gli input vengano raccolti alla fine.
3. **Eseguire le scene in parallelo e comporre i risultati man mano.** Script, voce e overlay di scene indipendenti possono avanzare contemporaneamente; il compositore finale dovrebbe aspettare solo i pezzi mancanti. Il repository già indica DAG persistenti e riuso di precomposizioni come direzione architetturale in [00-TARGET-AND-DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md](/home/pierone/Projects/company/VeloxEditiingg/docs/100-percent-plan/00-TARGET-AND-DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md).
4. **Ridurre il lavoro da trasferire.** Cache condivisa e output a segmenti possono evitare di spedire e ricomporre ogni volta tutti i file. Il piano [SCALE-IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md](/home/pierone/Projects/company/VeloxEditiingg/docs/SCALE-IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md) descrive già streaming, cache anticipata e consegna basata su manifest.

Per arrivare davvero a **10×** sul tempo percepito, punterei prima a consegnare **scene o anteprime progressivamente**, mentre il video completo continua a finire in background. Un job completo in circa 17 secondi non è un obiettivo realistico con i tempi attuali di generazione: servirebbe anche riusare risultati già calcolati o ridurre il lavoro richiesto.

Il prossimo passo utile è misurare nel dettaglio quei ~51 secondi di handoff e i ~51 di coda sul worker, verificando se dipendono da trasferimento degli asset, polling o scheduler. Solo dopo possiamo stimare il guadagno e scegliere quale cambiamento implementare.

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    RUN="r29-20min-20261104"
    API="http://127.0.0.1:8000"
    PAYLOAD="$DIR/$RUN.generate.json"
    RESP="$DIR/$RUN-submit-response.json"
    LOG="$DIR/$RUN-submit-poll.log"
    FULL="$DIR/$RUN-job-full.json"
    DONE="$DIR/$RUN.done"
    P="$(systemctl show -p MainPID --value pipelinegen.service)"
    TOKEN="${VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN:-}"
    if [[ -z "$TOKEN" && -r "/proc/$P/environ" ]]; then TOKEN="$(tr '\0' '\n' < "/proc/$P/environ" | sed -n 's/^VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN=//p')"; fi
    [[ -n "$TOKEN" ]] || { echo 'admin token unavailable' >&2; exit 3; }
    rm -f "$DONE"
    started_epoch="$(date +%s)"
    printf '%s submitted_at payload=%s\n' "$(date -Iseconds)" "$PAYLOAD" | tee "$LOG"
    code="$(curl -sS -o "$RESP" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$API/api/script/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $RUN" --data-binary "@$PAYLOAD")"
    printf '%s submit_http=%s\n' "$(date -Iseconds)" "$code" | tee -a "$LOG"
    [[ "$code" == 202 ]] || { cat "$RESP"; echo 'submission failed' >&2; exit 4; }
    JOB="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("job_id",""))' "$RESP")"
    [[ -n "$JOB" ]] || { echo 'missing job id' >&2; exit 4; }
    printf '%s job=%s\n' "$(date -Iseconds)" "$JOB" | tee -a "$LOG"
    for i in $(seq 1 480); do
      ts="$(date -Iseconds)"
      body="$(curl -sS --max-time 15 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/api/jobs/$JOB" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      status="$(printf '%s' "$body" | python3 -c 'import json,sys
    try:
     d=json.load(sys.stdin);print((d.get("status") or d.get("current_status") or "UNKNOWN").upper())
    except Exception: print("UNKNOWN")')"
      printf '%s %s\n' "$ts" "$status" >> "$LOG"
      case "$status" in
        SUCCEEDED|FAILED|CANCELED|COMPLETED|ERROR)
          curl -sS --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/api/jobs/$JOB/full" > "$FULL"
          elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - started_epoch ))
          printf 'DONE status=%s job=%s elapsed_s=%s\n' "$status" "$JOB" "$elapsed" | tee "$DONE"
          exit $([[ "$status" == SUCCEEDED || "$status" == COMPLETED ]] && echo 0 || echo 1)
          ;;
      esac
      sleep 5
    done
    printf 'DONE timeout job=%s\n' "$JOB" | tee "$DONE"
    exit 5

    const defaultFinalJobMasterURL = "https://veloxmanager.duckdns.org"
    
    // defaultFinalJobAttachBudget keeps script.generate attached through the usual
    // remote composite render. The old 60s default marked the local job FAILED while
    // the Master was still rendering for 6-14 minutes; those renders continued, but
    // their completed result was never joined back to the parent job. Leave enough
    // room for the observed render times while remaining below the 60m script job
    // timeout. Operators can still override this with
    // VELOX_FINAL_JOB_ATTACH_SECONDS.
    const defaultFinalJobAttachBudget = 50 * time.Minute
    
    // deprecatedFinalJobWorker51ID is the pin this build used to apply when no
    // operator override was configured. Worker 51 was quarantined on 2026-11-02, so
    // a hardcoded default silently routed every handoff to an unhealthy worker: r9
    // sat PENDING for 43 minutes against it. The pin is now opt-in
    // (VELOX_FINAL_JOB_WORKER_ID); with no override, the Master places the job.
    const deprecatedFinalJobWorker51ID = "velox-worker-523925eb"
    
    // finalJobWorkerPin is the placement pin for a handoff, or "" when the Master
    // must place the job itself. There is deliberately no default: an operator pin
    // is a deployment fact (which worker is healthy), not something this binary can
    // know. The retired worker-51 default is rejected loudly instead of silently
    // resurrected by a stale environment file.
    func finalJobWorkerPin() (string, error) {
        pin := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_WORKER_ID"))
        if pin == "" {
            return "", nil
        }
        if pin == deprecatedFinalJobWorker51ID {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_WORKER_ID pins the retired worker %s; unset it to let the Master place the job", pin)
        }
        return pin, nil
    }
    
    // finalJobQueueBudget reads VELOX_FINAL_JOB_QUEUE_SECONDS: how long a handoff
    // may wait for the Master to lease and START the job before the wait is handed
    // back. It bounds the failure mode r9 exposed (46 minutes in PENDING, then a
    // cancellation): a queued job cannot finish, so holding the local worker for
    // the whole render budget buys nothing. 0 disables the queue budget. A
    // malformed value is a configuration error, not a silent default.
    func finalJobQueueBudget() (time.Duration, error) {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_QUEUE_SECONDS"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobQueueBudget, nil
        }
        seconds, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || seconds < 0 {
            return 0, fmt.Errorf("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_QUEUE_SECONDS must be a non-negative integer number of seconds, got %q", raw)
        }
        return time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second, nil
    }
    
    // defaultFinalJobQueueBudget is generous for a healthy Master (r101 leased in
    // 0 s, r103 in 58 s) and far below the 46-minute stall that motivated it.
    const defaultFinalJobQueueBudget = 3 * time.Minute
    
    // finalJobAttachBudget reads VELOX_FINAL_JOB_ATTACH_SECONDS. 0 disables the
    // hand-off (every wait runs to completion: the pre-split blocking contract).
    // A malformed value is a configuration error, not a silent default.
    func finalJobAttachBudget() (time.Duration, error) {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_ATTACH_SECONDS"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobAttachBudget, nil
        }
        seconds, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || seconds < 0 {
            return 0, fmt.Errorf("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_ATTACH_SECONDS must be a non-negative integer number of seconds, got %q", raw)
        }
        return time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second, nil
    }

        // attachBudget bounds a single attempt's wait on the Master render; see
        // defaultFinalJobAttachBudget and finalJobAttachBudget.
        attachBudget time.Duration
        // queueBudget bounds the NOT-STARTED portion of that wait; see
        // defaultFinalJobQueueBudget and finalJobQueueBudget. It is carried on the
        // transport client so the resume path shares the same rule.
        queueBudget time.Duration
        // resolverNS is the accumulated runtime-asset resolution time reported in

        resolverNS atomic.Int64
        // resolved caches one handoff's runtime-asset resolution by identity. The

        // signing those bytes again per window answers a question the identity has

        // runs, and only ever stores a reference to immutable content.
        resolvedMu sync.Mutex
        resolved   map[string]map[string]any
        hits       int

        // during the overlay render, so StartFinalJob of the SAME run must keep
        // what was already warmed; a different run (or a retry reusing this
        // adapter) must never inherit another run's identities.
        resolvedRunID string

        // and two folders may offer the same file; the second caller waits for the
        // first instead of downloading and publishing those bytes again. Entries
        // hold immutable content, so a waiter always receives the same answer the
        // builder produced.
        inflightMu sync.Mutex
        inflight   map[string]*finalJobResolveCall
    }
    
    // finalJobResolveCall is one in-progress resolution. `done` is closed exactly
    // once, after ref/err are written, so a waiter needs no further lock.
    type finalJobResolveCall struct {
        done chan struct{}
        ref  map[string]any
        err  error
    }
    
    func newRemoteFinalJobAdapter(root *ComposeRoot) (*remoteFinalJobAdapter, error) {
        if root == nil || root.MediaPostgres == nil || root.Drive == nil || root.Drive.Reader == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("remote final-job handoff requires the media SSOT and Drive stock reader")
        }
        if strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("OBJECTSTORE_PUBLIC_URL")) == "" {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("remote final-job HTTPS handoff requires OBJECTSTORE_PUBLIC_URL; only stock assets may use Drive")
        }
        token := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_M2M_SECRET"))
        if token == "" {
            path := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_CREDENTIALS_FILE"))
            if path == "" {
                home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
                path = filepath.Join(home, "creator-77-master.env")
            }
            var err error
            token, err = remotejob.ReadTokenFile(path)
            if err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
        }
        base := ""
        if v := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_MASTER_URL")); v != "" {
            base = v
        }
        if base == "" {
            base = defaultFinalJobMasterURL
        }
        masterURL, err := url.Parse(base)
        if err != nil || masterURL == nil || masterURL.Scheme != "https" || masterURL.Host == "" {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("remote final-job master URL must use HTTPS")
        }
        budget, err := finalJobAttachBudget()
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        queueBudget, err := finalJobQueueBudget()
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        client := remotejob.New(base, token)
        client.QueueTimeout = queueBudget
        return &remoteFinalJobAdapter{media: pgmedia.NewMediaSearcher(root.MediaPostgres), stock: root.Drive.Reader, client: client, attachBudget: budget, queueBudget: queueBudget}, nil
    }
    
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) SubmitFinalJob(ctx context.Context, runID string, req scriptgen.GenerateRequest, result *scriptgen.GenerateResult) (scriptgen.RemoteFinalJobResult, error) {
        started, err := a.StartFinalJob(ctx, runID, req, result)
        if err != nil {
            return started, err
        }
        remote, waitErr := a.client.Attach(ctx, started.JobID, a.attachBudget)
        receipt := finalJobResult(started.JobID, remote)
        // The attach result only knows Master-clock phases; the locally measured
        // handoff belongs to the receipt the submission produced.
        receipt.Timing = mergeFinalJobTiming(started.Timing, receipt.Timing)
        return receipt, finalJobWaitError(waitErr)
    }
    
    // StartFinalJob creates the Master job and returns its durable handle without
    // polling. The scripts runner checkpoints this receipt before it attaches.
    //
    // It never sends FINALIZE to an identity the Master reports as already leased
    // or canceled: a leased job is handed back as ErrFinalJobPending so the next
    // attempt ATTACHES to it, and a canceled one is handed back as a stale receipt
    // so the next attempt prepares a fresh identity instead of replaying a dead id.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) StartFinalJob(ctx context.Context, runID string, req scriptgen.GenerateRequest, result *scriptgen.GenerateResult) (scriptgen.RemoteFinalJobResult, error) {
        if a == nil || a.client == nil {
            return scriptgen.RemoteFinalJobResult{}, fmt.Errorf("remote final-job adapter is not configured")
        }
        if a.segments == nil {
            return scriptgen.RemoteFinalJobResult{}, fmt.Errorf("remote final-job local segment preparation is not configured; refusing to dispatch raw video sources")
        }
        handoffStarted := time.Now()
        // The segment preparation measured by THIS build, never the preparer's
        // process-wide total: a resumed or concurrent run must not inherit it.
        var segmentPrep *scriptgen.RemoteFinalJobSegmentPrepTiming
        var resolveMS, prepareMS int64
        var payloadBuiltAt time.Time
        handoffTiming := func() *scriptgen.RemoteFinalJobTiming {
            timing := &scriptgen.RemoteFinalJobTiming{
                HandoffMS:        time.Since(handoffStarted).Milliseconds(),
                HandoffResolveMS: resolveMS,
                PrepareMS:        prepareMS,
            }
            if !payloadBuiltAt.IsZero() {
                // The payload build is a SUBSET of handoff_ms that contains segment
                // preparation and resolve; measuring its end is what makes the
                // remainder attributable to FINALIZE instead of unknown.
                timing.PayloadMS = payloadBuiltAt.Sub(handoffStarted).Milliseconds()
            }
            if segmentPrep != nil && segmentPrep.Segments > 0 {
                timing.SegmentPrep = segmentPrep
            }
            return timing
        }
        a.beginHandoffCache(runID)

    // Runtime-asset resolution for the remote final job: the identity cache, the
    // stock staging and its receipts, and the prefetch lanes that keep handoff
    // from re-resolving one source per fragment.
    
    // resolverClock accumulates the runtime-asset resolution time of one handoff.
    // It answers the only question the receipt could not: how much of handoff_ms is
    // spent finding and publishing sources rather than encoding fragments.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolverClock() func() {
        started := time.Now()
        return func() {
            if a != nil {
                a.resolverNS.Add(time.Since(started).Nanoseconds())
            }
        }
    }
    
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) ResolveFinalJobAsset(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        return a.resolveOnce("objectstore:"+strings.TrimSpace(id), func() (map[string]any, error) {
            defer a.resolverClock()()
            started := time.Now()
            ref, err := a.ResolveFinalJobObjectStoreAsset(ctx, id)
            log.Printf("final_job resolve kind=objectstore id=%s bytes=%v ms=%d err=%v",
                id, ref["size_bytes"], time.Since(started).Milliseconds(), err != nil)
            return ref, err
        })
    }
    
    // resolveOnce answers a repeated resolution from the handoff's own cache. The
    // cached reference is copied on the way out so a caller cannot mutate the entry
    // (the payload builder stamps roles and durations onto the map it receives).
    //
    // Concurrent callers of the SAME identity share one resolution (single flight):
    // the prefetch warms a folder while the walk asks for the file it needs, and
    // without this the prefetch would be duplicated work instead of saved work.
    // An error is never cached — a failed warm-up must not poison the walk.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolveOnce(key string, build func() (map[string]any, error)) (map[string]any, error) {
        if a == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job adapter is not configured")

        // latency bound — so parallelising it multiplies work instead of hiding it.
        // The knob stays so a future stack fix can be measured against this table.
        defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency = 1
        // maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency bounds the operator knob: beyond this the

        // source while costing ceil(64/6)·190 ms ≈ 2 s of wall instead of 64·190 ms.

        // certificate nobody can honour. The registered video-only profile describes
        // these bytes exactly; plan.Output keeps V1 for the assembled FILM.
        // The assembler's copy gate binds a prepared fragment to the profile IT
        // certifies against (VELOX_ASSEMBLY_READY_V1). r90 proved the coupling: with
        // VELOX_OVERLAY_VIDEO_ONLY_V1 on the fragment, the remote rejected the plan
        // (`segment "segment-0000" manifest binding is not exact`) even though the
        // bytes were exact (86/86 frame counts, durations, zero start). The
        // video-only profile keeps describing the RENDER ARTIFACT (plan
        // output_profile_id); the fragment certificate stays V1 until the gate
        // learns the video-only profile.
        finalJobSegmentProfile = kernelmedia.AssemblyMediaContractID
        finalJobSegmentMaxSize = int64(2 << 30)
        // Four lanes keep the fragment encode inside the CPU budget the map
        // compositor and the GPU lanes already use on the same host while cutting
        // the serial handoff to roughly a quarter.
        defaultFinalJobFragmentLanes = 4
        maxFinalJobFragmentLanes     = 16
        // finalJobFragmentFormatVersion is part of every cache key. It changes when
        // the BYTES of a fragment can change for the same work — the container of a
        // tagged placement did (v2) — so a cache written by an older build can never
        // answer for the newer layout. Bumping it costs one re-encode of the corpus.
        // v4: a duplicate placement is now DERIVED from the certified object by a
        // packet-copy remux instead of being encoded a second time.
        // v5 distinguishes the actual encoder selected by the codec override.
        // v6 separates optional packet-copy windows from encoded fragments.
        // v7: the key no longer carries the producing path (copy vs encode), which
        // was a distinction without a difference for the certified bytes.
        // v8: copy and remux force a zero start timestamp, so the same window can
        // produce different container bytes than v7.
        // v9: distinguish a copy-enabled request from encode-only work so an A/B
        // cannot silently return a cached artifact produced by the other path.
        // v10: the canonical avcC (SPS/PPS) is part of the work identity, and the
        // encoder now pins ref=1, so bytes produced before this change cannot

        finalJobFragmentFormatVersion = 10

    // certificate that describes it drift apart.
    var finalJobDelivery = kernelmedia.DefaultAssemblyMediaContract()

    // moves the GOP grid and the microsecond conversion with it.
    var (

        finalJobSegmentGOP = int64(finalJobDelivery.KeyframeInterval)
    )

    // census and fragment probe share this ONE comparison, so the encoder cannot
    // "normalize" a source the reuse gate already accepted as conformant.
    // finalJobDeliveryLevelCode is the H.264 level as ffprobe reports it (40 for

    func finalJobDeliveryLevelCode() int {

        policy mediaexec.EncoderPolicy

        sourcesMu sync.Mutex

        // geometry memoizes whether a source already matches the delivery geometry
        // (1920x1080, 24 fps, yuv420p). Probing it once per source is what lets the
        // encoder skip rebuilding a picture that is already built.
        geometryMu      sync.Mutex
        geometry        map[string]bool
        geometryFlights singleflight.Group
        // certificates memoizes the source census by content hash. Every window of
        // one source asks the same question ("are these bytes really
        // VELOX_ASSEMBLY_READY_V1 with a closed fixed GOP?") and the answer cannot
        // change within a run: the source is content-addressed. Probing it once per
        // source is what makes a copied window cheaper than an encoded one.
        certificatesMu sync.Mutex
        certificates   map[string]finalJobSourceCensus
        // censusFlights makes the first probe for one content identity shared by
        // all lanes. The map above handles completed results; this group handles
        // callers that arrive while the same ffprobe is still running.
        censusFlights singleflight.Group
        // verifier is the shared digest policy applied to this preparer's
        // local artifacts. It avoids rereading an immutable cache hit for every
        // placement while invalidating whenever size or mtime changes.
        verifier *digest.Verifier
        // fragmentLocks coalesces identical cacheable work within this preparer.
        // Entries are removed when the last holder or waiter leaves.
        fragmentLocksMu sync.Mutex
        fragmentLocks   map[string]*finalJobFragmentLock
        // paths maps a certified fragment's SHA-256 to the local file that holds
        // its bytes in this process. A duplicate placement is normally derived
        // from a fragment produced seconds earlier by the same run, so the bytes
        // never have to cross the network a second time.
        pathsMu sync.Mutex
        paths   map[string]string

        // publishes cannot mix in another run's work when two handoffs share this
        // preparer.
        scopeSeq atomic.Uint64
        // scoped holds one accumulator per live handoff. The aggregate above stays a
        // log surface only: a receipt reads its own entry, never the difference of
        // two process-wide snapshots that a concurrent handoff can move in between.
        scoped map[uint64]finalJobSegmentStats
    }

    // they are constants instead of free strings.
    const (

        finalJobWindowCache   = "cache"
        finalJobWindowCopy    = "copy"
        finalJobWindowEncode  = "encode"
        finalJobWindowDerived = "derived"
    )

    // a silent default.
    func finalJobFragmentLanes() (int, error) {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_PREPARE_LANES"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobFragmentLanes, nil
        }
        lanes, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || lanes < 1 || lanes > maxFinalJobFragmentLanes {
            return 0, fmt.Errorf("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_PREPARE_LANES must be an integer between 1 and %d, got %q", maxFinalJobFragmentLanes, raw)

        return lanes, nil
    }

    // exists only to measure the two paths against each other in an A/B run.
    // A malformed value is not a silent enable: it falls back to the encoded path.
    func finalJobCopyWindowsEnabled() bool {
        switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_COPY_CERTIFIED_WINDOWS"))) {

            return true
        default:
            return false
        }
    }

            lanes = 1

            ffmpeg:   strings.TrimSpace(ffmpeg),
            policy:   policy,
            client:   &http.Client{Timeout: 20 * time.Minute},
            cacheDir: strings.TrimSpace(cacheDir),
            lanes:    lanes,
            verifier: digest.NewVerifier(nil),
        }
    }
    
    // Parallelism lets the plan builder prepare independent fragments concurrently;
    // it never changes WHICH fragments are prepared or in what order they bind.
    func (p *finalJobSegmentPreparer) Parallelism() int {
        if p == nil || p.lanes < 1 {
            return 1
        }
        return p.lanes
    }

        if p == nil || p.client == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("local fragment encoder is unavailable")

        if request.FrameCount <= 0 || request.SourceInUS < 0 || request.SourceDurationUS <= 0 || request.TimelineStartFrame < 0 || request.TimelineRevision <= 0 || len(request.TimelineSHA256) != 64 {

        }
