    // Package pipeline — canonical_request_projection.go owns the typed external intake facade.
    package pipeline
    
    import (
        "encoding/json"
        "strings"
    
        "velox-shared/contract/assembly"
        "velox-shared/contract/deliveryplan"
        "velox-shared/publication"
    )
    
    // ExternalAPISourceProvider is the stable source-provider identity for POST /api/v1/jobs.
    const ExternalAPISourceProvider = "external_api"
    
    // JobSubmitTargetExecutorID is the executor for copy-ready compiled V2 video
    // plans. Drive stock-pool plans use the slice executor because the worker must
    // resolve the pool and fill its timeline slots before packet-copy assembly.
    const JobSubmitTargetExecutorID = "video.assemble.copy.v1"
    const JobSubmitDriveStockPoolExecutorID = "video.assemble.slice.v1"
    
    func (h *Handlers) NormalizeExternalJobSubmission(req SubmitJobRequest) *CanonicalCompletedPayload {
        rawPayload := submitRequestToRawPayload(&req)
        workerPayload, err := projectWorkerPayload(&req)
        if err != nil {
            return nil
        }
    
        var assemblyJob *assembly.AssemblyJobV1
        if req.Assembly != nil {
            assemblyJob, _ = req.Assembly.Normalize(req.IdempotencyKey)
        }
        targetExecutorID := targetExecutorForRequest(req)
        deliveryEnvelope := deliveryplan.ExtractEnvelope(rawPayload)
        if req.RenderOnly {
            // Render-only jobs have no external delivery route. Keep only the
            // opt-out marker in the control-plane envelope, even if a legacy or
            // defaulted intake DTO carried an empty delivery-plan entry.
            deliveryEnvelope = map[string]interface{}{"render_only": true}
        }
        return &CanonicalCompletedPayload{
            SourceProvider:   ExternalAPISourceProvider,
            SourceJobID:      req.IdempotencyKey,
            TargetExecutorID: targetExecutorID,
            WorkerPayload:    workerPayload,
            DeliveryPlan:     deliveryEnvelope,
            PublicationSpecs: projectPublicationSpecs(req.Publications),
            Assembly:         assemblyJob,
            StatusDomains:    inputAssemblyStatusDomain(workerPayload),
        }
    }
    
    func targetExecutorForJobType(jobType string) string {
        // Recipe names are decoupled from worker executor IDs. Every admitted
        // video request is normalized to CompiledRenderPlanV2 before dispatch.
        _ = jobType
        return JobSubmitTargetExecutorID
    }
    
    func targetExecutorForRequest(req SubmitJobRequest) string {
        return targetExecutorForCompiledPlan(req.CompiledRenderPlanJSON, req.JobType)
    }
    
    func targetExecutorForCompiledPlan(raw string, jobType string) string {
        var plan struct {
            StockPool *struct {
                SourceKind    string `json:"source_kind"`
                DriveFolderID string `json:"drive_folder_id"`
                Selection     string `json:"selection"`
            } `json:"stock_pool"`
        }
        if json.Unmarshal([]byte(strings.TrimSpace(raw)), &plan) == nil &&
            plan.StockPool != nil &&
            strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(plan.StockPool.SourceKind), "drive") &&
            strings.TrimSpace(plan.StockPool.DriveFolderID) != "" &&
            strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(plan.StockPool.Selection), "shuffle") {
            return JobSubmitDriveStockPoolExecutorID
        }
        return targetExecutorForJobType(jobType)
    }
    
    // projectPublicationSpecs converts intake DTOs into the canonical control-plane
    // contract. These specs are retained on CanonicalCompletedPayload and are never
    // merged into WorkerPayload: the renderer only needs render inputs, while the
    // delivery pipeline owns publication metadata and destinations.
    func projectPublicationSpecs(publications []SubmitPublication) []publication.Spec {
        if len(publications) == 0 {
            return nil
        }
        specs := make([]publication.Spec, 0, len(publications))
        for _, input := range publications {
            spec := submitPublicationToSharedSpec(input)
            if normalized, err := spec.Normalize(); err == nil {
                spec = normalized
            }
    // Package enqueue — V2-only payload normalization and routing.
    package enqueue
    
    import (
        "context"
        "crypto/sha256"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "strings"
    
        "velox-server/internal/telemetry"
        "velox-shared/contract"
        "velox-shared/contract/deliveryplan"
    )
    
    const canonicalCompiledPlanExecutor = "video.assemble.copy.v1@1"
    const canonicalDriveSliceExecutor = "video.assemble.slice.v1@1"
    
    func normalizeSceneVideoPayload(payloadMap map[string]interface{}) (map[string]interface{}, error) {
        return normalizeSceneVideoPayloadContext(context.Background(), payloadMap)
    }
    
    // normalizeSceneVideoPayloadContext validates and wraps producer-owned V2
    // bytes. It deliberately has no scene, overlay, media, or manifest compiler.
    func normalizeSceneVideoPayloadContext(ctx context.Context, payloadMap map[string]interface{}) (map[string]interface{}, error) {
        if payloadMap == nil {
            return nil, errors.New("compiled_render_plan_v2: payload is required")
        }
        for _, key := range []string{"scenes", "scenes_json", "render_manifest", "manifest_ref", "layers", "overlays", "visual_replacements", "items", "clips", "images", "voiceover_paths", "voiceover_path", "audio_path"} {
            if _, exists := payloadMap[key]; exists {
                return nil, deliveryplan.NewValidationError(key, "is retired; submit the producer-compiled CompiledRenderPlanV2")
            }
        }
        base, err := contract.NewJobPayloadV2Checked(payloadMap)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        if err := contract.ValidateCompiledRenderPlanV2Payload(payloadMap); err != nil {
            return nil, deliveryplan.NewValidationErrorWrapped("compiled_render_plan_v2", "producer plan validation failed", err)
        }
        if !compiledRenderPlanV2Present(payloadMap) {
            return nil, deliveryplan.NewValidationError("compiled_render_plan_v2", "producer-compiled plan and SHA are required")
        }
        base.VideoName = strings.TrimSpace(base.VideoName)
        if base.VideoName == "" {
            return nil, deliveryplan.NewValidationError("video_name", "is required")
        }
        base.ScriptText = strings.TrimSpace(base.ScriptText)
        if base.ScriptText == "" {
            base.ScriptText = base.VideoName
        }
        base.SetIdentity(base.JobID, base.JobRunID, base.CorrelationID)
        base.Version = "v2"
        base.Status = contract.InputAssemblyPending
        base.JobFingerprint = sceneVideoFingerprintContext(ctx, base.JobID, base.VideoName, base.ScriptText, base.CompiledRenderPlanSHA256)
    
        out, err := base.ToMap()
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        // These fields are control-plane or runtime binding metadata. Preserve
        // them without interpreting or modifying the compiled timeline.
        for key, value := range payloadMap {
            if strings.HasPrefix(key, "runtime_") || key == "publications" || key == "assembly" ||
                key == "_internal_forwarding_key" || key == "_placement_pin_worker_id" ||
                key == "source_provider" || key == "source_job_id" || key == "target_executor_id" || key == "delivery_plan" || key == "render_only" {
                if key == "_placement_pin_worker_id" {
                    if pin, ok := value.(string); ok {
                        value = strings.TrimSpace(pin)
                    }
                }
                out[key] = value
            }
        }
        if err := contract.ValidateCompiledRenderPlanV2Payload(out); err != nil {
            return nil, deliveryplan.NewValidationErrorWrapped("compiled_render_plan_v2", "normalized plan validation failed", err)
        }
        return out, nil
    }
    
    func compiledRenderPlanV2Present(payloadMap map[string]interface{}) bool {
        if payloadMap == nil {
            return false
        }
        _, hasJSON := payloadMap[contract.PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanJSON]
        _, hasSHA := payloadMap[contract.PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanSHA]
        return hasJSON || hasSHA
    }
    
    func resolveInternalExecutorID(payloadMap map[string]interface{}) string {
        if !compiledRenderPlanV2Present(payloadMap) {
            return ""
        }
        // Final-job Producers may keep the immutable compiled plan free of
        // transport locators and attach Drive file IDs in runtime_assets instead.
        // Join those locators by the stable asset_id before selecting the executor;
        // otherwise stock-sha256-* assets are misrouted to the copy-only executor.
        runtimeDriveIDs := runtimeDriveFileIDs(payloadMap["runtime_assets"])
        if raw, ok := payloadMap[contract.PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanJSON].(string); ok {
            var plan struct {
                StockPool *contract.StockPoolV2 `json:"stock_pool"`
                Assets    []struct {
                    SourceKind  string `json:"source_kind"`
                    DriveFileID string `json:"drive_file_id"`
                    AssetID     string `json:"asset_id"`
                    AssetKey    string `json:"asset_key"`
                    Kind        string `json:"kind"`
                } `json:"assets"`
            }
            if json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &plan) == nil {
                if plan.StockPool != nil {
                    return canonicalDriveSliceExecutor
                }
                for _, asset := range plan.Assets {
                    driveFileID := strings.TrimSpace(asset.DriveFileID)
                    if driveFileID == "" {
                        driveFileID = runtimeDriveIDs[strings.TrimSpace(asset.AssetID)]
                    }
                    if driveFileID == "" {
                        driveFileID = runtimeDriveIDs[strings.TrimSpace(asset.AssetKey)]
                    }
                    if asset.Kind == "video" && (asset.SourceKind == "drive" || driveFileID != "" || strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(asset.AssetID)), "drive:")) {
                        return canonicalDriveSliceExecutor
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return canonicalCompiledPlanExecutor
    }
    
    func runtimeDriveFileIDs(raw interface{}) map[string]string {
        encoded, err := json.Marshal(raw)
        if err != nil || len(encoded) == 0 || string(encoded) == "null" {
            return nil
        }
        var assets []struct {
            AssetID     string `json:"asset_id"`
            AssetKey    string `json:"asset_key"`
            DriveFileID string `json:"drive_file_id"`
        }
        if err := json.Unmarshal(encoded, &assets); err != nil {
            return nil
        }
        byIdentity := make(map[string]string, len(assets)*2)

## Assistant

Ho corretto il percorso: **un’unica regola condivisa** decide l’executor dal piano; i job con `stock_pool` usano il folder Drive, il Master non pre-carica i video stock e il worker li verifica e concatena senza ricodificarli. La nuova immagine locale del worker è installata; Master e worker risultano sani. Le modifiche sono nel commit locale `b8204784`, non pubblicato su GitHub.

Il rilancio **non ha prodotto un MP4**: r4 (`job_45e249c111b3783b`) è fallito in 7 secondi, prima di FFmpeg, perché il folder contiene sorgenti non compatibili con il piano. Il piano richiede H.264 High, livello 4.0; ho trovato almeno un file a livello 4.1 e un altro a 4.0 con extradata H.264 diversa. Per rispettare il vincolo di non ricodifica, il worker ha rifiutato il pool. Perché il job riesca, **tutti i video nel folder devono essere compatibili tra loro e col profilo del piano**; anche un solo elemento divergente fa fallire il job.

L’assegnatario effettivo è `host_57_129_132_133`; `velox-worker-523925eb` è ancora disconnesso e in quarantena.     docs/API-JOBS.md:45:Unlike `POST /api/v1/creator/jobs` (which uses the operator-grade `VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN`), `POST /api/v1/jobs` uses **per-client M2M credentials**. This is intentional: the operator's admin bearer is too coarse to distribute to external systems, and a single leaked operator token would expose the entire admin surface (`/api/v1/admin/m2m/*` is the same adminAuth boundary).
    docs/API-JOBS.md:51:  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
    docs/API-JOBS.md:70:The smoke script `scripts/api/jobs_smoke.sh` does this provisioning inline: pass `VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN` and the script mints an ephemeral client, runs the smoke, and `DELETE`s the client on exit (best-effort cleanup).
    docs/API-JOBS.md:76:  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN}"
    docs/API-JOBS.md:88:Authorization: Bearer <plaintext_secret>      (M2M bearer — NOT VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN)
    docs/API-JOBS.md:210:Authorization: Bearer <VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN>
    docs/API-JOBS.md:246:Cross-client authorisation is **STRICT**: every M2M polling read and action resolves the requested job through `creator_forwardings` and requires `external_client_id == m2m_client_id`. This covers `GET /api/v1/jobs/:id` and `GET /api/v1/jobs/:id/asset-progress`. A job that does not exist AND a job owned by another client return the identical `404 job_not_found` envelope (`ok:false`, `error:"job_not_found"`, same `message`) — the boundary reveals no existence oracle. Artifact URLs, delivery rows, timeline events and asset-progress are surfaced only after the ownership-scoped lookup succeeds; the same rule applies to the artifact / delivery projections nested in the status response. Admin callers (operator `VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN`) bypass the M2M boundary by design and keep the unscoped admin surface.

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # scripts/operator/with-production-env.sh — Source the local production env.
    #
    # Canonical usage:
    #   source scripts/operator/with-production-env.sh
    #   <command>   # any command needing the canonical production env (curl,
    #               # fleetctl, ops scripts — the Ansible rollout is retired).
    #
    # Legacy direct-exec usage (still works, will be removed in a future release):
    #   scripts/operator/with-production-env.sh <command> [args...]
    #   scripts/operator/with-production-env.sh curl -sS "$VELOX_MASTER_URL/health/ready"
    #
    # Override the env file location:
    #   VELOX_PRODUCTION_ENV=/path/to/custom.env source scripts/operator/with-production-env.sh
    #
    # Agents MUST source this wrapper (or run via `make canonical-dry`) instead of
    # `source .velox/production.env` directly. The wrapper enforces:
    #   - file exists,
    #   - file permissions are 600 (refuses world/group-readable credentials),
    #   - the three REQUIRED variables are set after sourcing,
    #   - the secret values are never echoed back to the terminal.
    # Agents MUST NOT print VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN, PATs, vault passwords, or SSH keys.
    #
    # Foot-gun guarded: sourcing (not executing) is the only sanctioned path;
    # direct-exec is legacy back-compat and will be removed.
    
    set -euo pipefail
    
    ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
    ENV_FILE="${VELOX_PRODUCTION_ENV:-${ROOT}/.velox/production.env}"
    
    if [[ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
        echo "Missing production environment: $ENV_FILE" >&2
        echo "Create it:" >&2
        echo "  mkdir -p .velox" >&2
        echo "  cat > .velox/production.env <<'EOF'" >&2
        echo "  VELOX_MASTER_HOST=<inserire IP o dominio>" >&2
        echo "  VELOX_MASTER_URL=https://<inserire IP o dominio>" >&2
        echo "  VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN=<inserire token reale>" >&2
        echo "  GHCR_SERVER_REPOSITORY=ghcr.io/marcuss-ops/velox-server" >&2
        echo "  GHCR_WORKER_REPOSITORY=ghcr.io/marcuss-ops/velox-worker" >&2
        echo "  EOF" >&2
        echo "  chmod 600 .velox/production.env" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Validate file permissions: refuse to source world-readable credential files.
    if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]]; then
        PERMS=$(stat -c '%a' "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
        GROUP_READABLE=$(( (PERMS / 10) % 10 ))
        OTHER_READABLE=$(( PERMS % 10 ))
        if [[ $GROUP_READABLE -ge 4 || $OTHER_READABLE -ge 4 ]]; then
            echo "FATAL: $ENV_FILE has overly permissive permissions (${PERMS})." >&2
            echo "Run: chmod 600 $ENV_FILE" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    
    set -a
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    source "$ENV_FILE"
    set +a
    
    # Validate required variables.
    : "${VELOX_MASTER_URL:?missing VELOX_MASTER_URL in $ENV_FILE}"
    : "${VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN:?missing VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN in $ENV_FILE}"
    : "${GHCR_SERVER_REPOSITORY:?missing GHCR_SERVER_REPOSITORY in $ENV_FILE}"
    
    # ── LEGACY DIRECT-EXEC PATH (deprecated; will be removed) ────────────────────
    # Detect direct execution (not sourcing). When sourced via `source ...`, this
    # branch is skipped and the env vars above flow into the calling shell. When
    # invoked as `with-production-env.sh <cmd> [args...]`, the BASH_SOURCE/$0
    # identity check distinguishes and routes to `exec "$@"`.
    # New operators must use `source` (or `make canonical-dry`); direct-exec is
    # kept only for back-compat with cron-era scripts.
    if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" != "${0}" ]]; then
        # Sourced mode: vars exported, return control to caller.
        return 0
    fi
    
    # Direct-exec mode (legacy): print usage if no args, else exec the child.
    if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "Usage: $0 <command> [args...]" >&2
        echo "       (prefer: source $0 && <command>)" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    exec "$@"

    // Package pipeline — request DTOs for the external job intake contract.
    package pipeline
    
    import "velox-shared/contract/assembly"
    
    // MaxSubmitJobBatchItems bounds the number of independent jobs accepted by
    // POST /api/v1/jobs/batch. The limit protects request latency and keeps a
    // batch's per-item response bounded; each item still has its own idempotency
    // key and enqueue transaction.
    const MaxSubmitJobBatchItems = 50
    
    type SubmitJobRequest struct {
        // Canonical recipe envelope. Existing scene fields remain the typed
        // projection used by the renderer; spec is accepted only as the input
        // recipe body and is normalized before validation/enqueue.
        JobType         string                 `json:"job_type,omitempty"`
        TemplateID      string                 `json:"template_id,omitempty"`
        TemplateVersion int                    `json:"template_version,omitempty"`
        Spec            map[string]interface{} `json:"spec,omitempty"`
        Output          *SubmitOutput          `json:"output,omitempty"`
    
        // IdempotencyKey is required. 1..128 bytes after UTF-8 trim, valid
        // UTF-8, no control bytes, no ':' or '%' separators. See
        // ValidateIdempotencyKey in idempotency_validation.go for the
        // byte-level rules and rejection envelopes.
        IdempotencyKey string `json:"idempotency_key"`
    
        // VideoName is the display name for the resulting video. Capped
        // at MaxVideoNameBytes (300); empty allowed.
        VideoName string `json:"video_name,omitempty"`
    
        // ScriptText is the plain-text script used for TTS / overlay.
        // Content field — NOT trimmed. Empty allowed. No byte-length cap
        // here; matches the creator path's tolerance.
        ScriptText string `json:"script_text,omitempty"`
        AudioURL   string `json:"audio_url,omitempty"`
        CopyOnly   bool   `json:"copy_only,omitempty"`
        // RenderOnly marks a completed worker render with no external delivery target.
        RenderOnly bool `json:"render_only,omitempty"`
        // CompiledRenderPlanJSON/SHA256 are producer-owned V2 bytes. When present,
        // the Master passes them through byte-for-byte and routes the task to the
        // canonical packet-copy executor; it never recompiles or infers the plan.
        CompiledRenderPlanJSON   string `json:"compiled_render_plan_json,omitempty"`
        CompiledRenderPlanSHA256 string `json:"compiled_render_plan_sha256,omitempty"`
    
        // Scenes is accepted only as transitional intake metadata. V2 render
        // submissions must provide a producer-compiled plan or a strict manifest
        // with final audio; the Master never turns scenes into renderer work.
        Scenes []SubmitScene `json:"scenes"`
    
        // Layers are independent overlays: title, name, important phrase or
        // additional media. They are not folded into Scenes, so callers can
        // submit a video, images and any combination of overlays together.
        Layers []SubmitLayer `json:"layers,omitempty"`
    
        // Overlays are editorial replacement intent. They become video timeline
        // segments and preserve the independent final audio timeline. Composite
        // work must be completed upstream and submitted through VisualReplacements.
        Overlays []SubmitOverlay `json:"overlays,omitempty"`
    
        // RuntimeAssets and RuntimePayload make PRE single-stage when the
        // producer already knows the runtime assets at submit time. A nil
        // RuntimeAssets keeps the legacy two-stage PRE→FINALIZE contract; an
        // explicitly supplied array clears the pending gate immediately.
        RuntimeAssets  []map[string]interface{} `json:"runtime_assets,omitempty"`
        RuntimePayload map[string]interface{}   `json:"runtime_payload,omitempty"`
        // RuntimeAssetsComplete makes the PRE single-stage transition explicit.
        // It is required when the producer intentionally submits an empty asset
        // list; nil-vs-empty must not decide a business state accidentally.
        RuntimeAssetsComplete *bool `json:"runtime_assets_complete,omitempty"`
    
        // VisualReplacements are already-composited video segments that
        // replace the base visual timeline over an absolute interval. Each
        // entry is a FINISHED video-only MP4; the master swaps it into the
        // timeline as a normal VideoSource (no overlay/compositing) and the
        // audio timeline remains independent. Resolved master-side by
        // VisualTimelineResolver; requires render_manifest + final_audio.
        VisualReplacements []SubmitVisualReplacement `json:"visual_replacements,omitempty"`
    
        // DeliveryPlan is the ordered list of delivery targets. Empty is allowed.
        // It remains backward-compatible with legacy senders. When
        // PublishingTarget is present, the handler resolves that selector into
        // this concrete plan before enqueue and rejects a request that supplies
        // both fields.
        DeliveryPlan []SubmitDeliveryPlanEntry `json:"delivery_plan,omitempty"`
    
        // PublishingTarget is an optional server-side channel/group selector.
        // It is never serialized into the renderer payload: the resolver expands
        // it into concrete DeliveryPlan entries before the canonical projection.
        PublishingTarget *SubmitPublishingTarget `json:"publishing_target,omitempty"`
    
        // Publications are the canonical publication intents for the
        // rendered outputs. They are kept separate from the renderer
        // payload and are consumed by the publication/delivery pipeline.
        Publications []SubmitPublication `json:"publications,omitempty"`
    
        // ManifestRef is retained as a typed wire field so legacy clients get an
        // explicit rejection. The Master no longer downloads manifests or compiles
        // renderer input; producers submit CompiledRenderPlanV2 directly.
        ManifestRef *SubmitManifestRef `json:"manifest_ref,omitempty"`
    
        // Assembly is control-plane metadata for eager Velox preparation. It is
        // normalized and persisted on TaskSpec; it never enters renderer Payload.
        Assembly *assembly.ExternalAssemblyRequest `json:"assembly,omitempty"`
    
        // RuntimeAssetsPending is set only by POST /api/v1/jobs/pre. It is an
        // internal two-stage marker and is intentionally not accepted from the
        // ordinary submit wire shape.
        RuntimeAssetsPending bool `json:"-"`
    
        // PlacementPinWorkerID is an optional operator/admin field that
        // forces the job to be placed on a specific worker, skipping
        // the normal placement matcher. Used by benchmark harnesses

    // Package pipeline — request DTOs for the external job intake contract.
    package pipeline
    
    import "velox-shared/contract/assembly"
    
    // MaxSubmitJobBatchItems bounds the number of independent jobs accepted by
    // POST /api/v1/jobs/batch. The limit protects request latency and keeps a
    // batch's per-item response bounded; each item still has its own idempotency
    // key and enqueue transaction.
    const MaxSubmitJobBatchItems = 50
    
    type SubmitJobRequest struct {
        // Canonical recipe envelope. Existing scene fields remain the typed
        // projection used by the renderer; spec is accepted only as the input
        // recipe body and is normalized before validation/enqueue.
        JobType         string                 `json:"job_type,omitempty"`
        TemplateID      string                 `json:"template_id,omitempty"`
        TemplateVersion int                    `json:"template_version,omitempty"`
        Spec            map[string]interface{} `json:"spec,omitempty"`
        Output          *SubmitOutput          `json:"output,omitempty"`
    
        // IdempotencyKey is required. 1..128 bytes after UTF-8 trim, valid
        // UTF-8, no control bytes, no ':' or '%' separators. See
        // ValidateIdempotencyKey in idempotency_validation.go for the
        // byte-level rules and rejection envelopes.
        IdempotencyKey string `json:"idempotency_key"`
    
        // VideoName is the display name for the resulting video. Capped
        // at MaxVideoNameBytes (300); empty allowed.
        VideoName string `json:"video_name,omitempty"`
    
        // ScriptText is the plain-text script used for TTS / overlay.
        // Content field — NOT trimmed. Empty allowed. No byte-length cap
        // here; matches the creator path's tolerance.
        ScriptText string `json:"script_text,omitempty"`
        AudioURL   string `json:"audio_url,omitempty"`
        CopyOnly   bool   `json:"copy_only,omitempty"`
        // RenderOnly marks a completed worker render with no external delivery target.
        RenderOnly bool `json:"render_only,omitempty"`
        // CompiledRenderPlanJSON/SHA256 are producer-owned V2 bytes. When present,
        // the Master passes them through byte-for-byte and routes the task to the
        // canonical packet-copy executor; it never recompiles or infers the plan.
        CompiledRenderPlanJSON   string `json:"compiled_render_plan_json,omitempty"`
        CompiledRenderPlanSHA256 string `json:"compiled_render_plan_sha256,omitempty"`
    
        // Scenes is accepted only as transitional intake metadata. V2 render
        // submissions must provide a producer-compiled plan or a strict manifest
        // with final audio; the Master never turns scenes into renderer work.
        Scenes []SubmitScene `json:"scenes"`
    
        // Layers are independent overlays: title, name, important phrase or
        // additional media. They are not folded into Scenes, so callers can
        // submit a video, images and any combination of overlays together.
        Layers []SubmitLayer `json:"layers,omitempty"`
    
        // Overlays are editorial replacement intent. They become video timeline
        // segments and preserve the independent final audio timeline. Composite
        // work must be completed upstream and submitted through VisualReplacements.
        Overlays []SubmitOverlay `json:"overlays,omitempty"`
    
        // RuntimeAssets and RuntimePayload make PRE single-stage when the
        // producer already knows the runtime assets at submit time. A nil
        // RuntimeAssets keeps the legacy two-stage PRE→FINALIZE contract; an
        // explicitly supplied array clears the pending gate immediately.
        RuntimeAssets  []map[string]interface{} `json:"runtime_assets,omitempty"`
        RuntimePayload map[string]interface{}   `json:"runtime_payload,omitempty"`
        // RuntimeAssetsComplete makes the PRE single-stage transition explicit.
        // It is required when the producer intentionally submits an empty asset
        // list; nil-vs-empty must not decide a business state accidentally.
        RuntimeAssetsComplete *bool `json:"runtime_assets_complete,omitempty"`
    
        // VisualReplacements are already-composited video segments that
        // replace the base visual timeline over an absolute interval. Each
        // entry is a FINISHED video-only MP4; the master swaps it into the
        // timeline as a normal VideoSource (no overlay/compositing) and the
        // audio timeline remains independent. Resolved master-side by
        // VisualTimelineResolver; requires render_manifest + final_audio.
        VisualReplacements []SubmitVisualReplacement `json:"visual_replacements,omitempty"`
    
        // DeliveryPlan is the ordered list of delivery targets. Empty is allowed.
        // It remains backward-compatible with legacy senders. When
        // PublishingTarget is present, the handler resolves that selector into
        // this concrete plan before enqueue and rejects a request that supplies
        // both fields.
        DeliveryPlan []SubmitDeliveryPlanEntry `json:"delivery_plan,omitempty"`
    
        // PublishingTarget is an optional server-side channel/group selector.
        // It is never serialized into the renderer payload: the resolver expands
        // it into concrete DeliveryPlan entries before the canonical projection.
        PublishingTarget *SubmitPublishingTarget `json:"publishing_target,omitempty"`
    
        // Publications are the canonical publication intents for the
        // rendered outputs. They are kept separate from the renderer
        // payload and are consumed by the publication/delivery pipeline.
        Publications []SubmitPublication `json:"publications,omitempty"`
    
        // ManifestRef is retained as a typed wire field so legacy clients get an
        // explicit rejection. The Master no longer downloads manifests or compiles
        // renderer input; producers submit CompiledRenderPlanV2 directly.
        ManifestRef *SubmitManifestRef `json:"manifest_ref,omitempty"`

    package pipeline
    
    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
    
        "velox-shared/assetref"
        "velox-shared/contract"
    )
    
    // resolveStockPoolRuntimeAssets is the one V2 folder-resolution boundary.
    // It lists metadata only; media bytes remain worker-owned transfers.
    func (h *Handlers) resolveStockPoolRuntimeAssets(ctx context.Context, req *SubmitJobRequest) error {
        if req == nil || req.CompiledRenderPlanJSON == "" {
            return nil
        }
        plan, err := contract.DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2([]byte(req.CompiledRenderPlanJSON))
        if err != nil {
            return nil // Canonical plan validation returns the structured V2 error later.
        }
        if plan.StockPool == nil {
            return nil
        }
        if h.stockFolderLister == nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("stock_pool requires the Master Drive folder-listing capability")
        }
        folderURL := "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/" + plan.StockPool.DriveFolderID
        folderID, err := assetref.ParseDriveFolderID(folderURL)
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        files, err := listStockFolderVideos(ctx, h.stockFolderLister, folderID.String(), 0, make(map[string]struct{}))
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        if len(files) == 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("stock_pool Drive folder contains no video files")
        }
        runtimeAssets := append([]map[string]interface{}(nil), req.RuntimeAssets...)
        seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(runtimeAssets)+len(files))
        for _, asset := range runtimeAssets {
            if id, ok := asset["asset_id"].(string); ok {
                seen[id] = struct{}{}
            }
        }
        for _, file := range files {
            if _, exists := seen[file.ID]; exists {
                continue
            }
            asset := map[string]interface{}{
                "asset_id": file.ID, "asset_key": file.ID, "drive_file_id": file.ID,
                "url":        "velox-drive://" + file.ID,
                "source_uri": "https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=" + file.ID,
                "kind":       "video", "stock_pool_member": true,
            }
            if file.Size > 0 {
                asset["size_bytes"] = file.Size
            }
            if file.VideoMediaMetadata.DurationMillis > 0 {
                asset["duration_ms"] = file.VideoMediaMetadata.DurationMillis
            }
            runtimeAssets = append(runtimeAssets, asset)
            seen[file.ID] = struct{}{}
        }
        req.RuntimeAssets = runtimeAssets
        // Ensure downstream payload projection sees the stable snapshot. The plan
        // remains byte-for-byte hash-bound; retries reuse the accepted runtime list.
        return nil
    }

    type issueM2MKeyRequest struct {

        Description       string   `json:"description"`
        Scopes            []string `json:"scopes"`
        RateLimitRPS      *int     `json:"rate_limit_rps"`
        RateLimitBurst    *int     `json:"rate_limit_burst"`

    }
    
    // issueM2MKeyResponse is the JSON returned by POST on success.
    // PlaintextSecret is the ONLY time the plaintext exists outside the
    // admin's clipboard; the row in `m2m_api_keys` contains only its
    // SHA-256 hash.
    type issueM2MKeyResponse struct {
        ClientID        string    `json:"client_id"`
        PlaintextSecret string    `json:"plaintext_secret"` // returned ONCE
        SecretHash      string    `json:"secret_hash"`
        Scopes          []string  `json:"scopes"`
        IsActive        bool      `json:"is_active"`
        Description     string    `json:"description"`
        RateLimitRPS    *int      `json:"rate_limit_rps"`

    }
    
    // =====================================================================

    // validateIssueM2MKeyRequest vets the request before insertion.
    // Reject: empty ClientID, ClientID containing `:`, scopes list with
    // unknown scope. Known / accepted scopes: `jobs.submit` (the only
    // scope supported at v1).
    func validateIssueM2MKeyRequest(req *issueM2MKeyRequest) error {
        if req == nil {
            return errAdminBadRequest("request body is required")
        }
        if cid := strings.TrimSpace(req.ClientID); cid == "" {
            return errAdminBadRequest("client_id is required")
        } else if strings.Contains(cid, ":") || strings.Contains(cid, " ") {
            return errAdminBadRequest("client_id must not contain ':' or whitespace")
        }
        for _, s := range req.Scopes {
            s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
            if s != "" && s != "jobs.submit" {
                return errAdminBadRequest("unsupported scope: " + s + " (only jobs.submit is supported in v1)")
            }
        }
        // Range guards: RPS+Burst non-negative; quotas non-negative.
        if req.RateLimitRPS != nil && *req.RateLimitRPS < 0 {
            return errAdminBadRequest("rate_limit_rps must be >= 0 (0 → use cfg.M2M.DefaultRPS)")

    package contract
    
    import (
        "crypto/sha256"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "fmt"
        "sort"
    )
    
    // CompiledPlanVersionV2 identifies the producer-compiled execution-plan
    // contract. CompiledRenderPlanV2 intentionally lives beside, rather than
    // replacing, the existing V1 master/worker render-plan mirrors.
    const CompiledPlanVersionV2 = 2
    
    // AudioModeFinalAudioCopyV2 declares that the final audio asset is already
    // mixed and must be muxed without another audio mix or encode.
    const (
        // AudioModeFinalAudioCopy is the wire value for an already-finalized
        // audio asset that must be muxed without another mix or encode.
        AudioModeFinalAudioCopy = "FINAL_AUDIO_COPY"
    
        // AudioModeFinalAudioCopyV2 is retained as an explicit V2-named alias for
        // callers that prefer versioned constants; both names have one wire value.
        AudioModeFinalAudioCopyV2 = AudioModeFinalAudioCopy
    )
    
    // CompiledRenderPlanV2 is the canonical, producer-compiled execution plan.
    // It contains editorial decisions and verified asset identity only; job and
    // attempt identity remain in the surrounding TaskSpec so retries and workers
    // can consume the same plan bytes and plan hash.
    type CompiledRenderPlanV2 struct {
        PlanVersion      int              `json:"plan_version"`
        TimelineRevision int64            `json:"timeline_revision"`
        TimelineSHA256   string           `json:"timeline_sha256"`
        DurationUS       int64            `json:"duration_us"`
        Output           OutputContractV2 `json:"output"`
        FinalAudio       FinalAudioV2     `json:"final_audio"`
        VideoTracks      []VideoTrackV2   `json:"video_tracks"`
        // StockPool declares that the worker selects source videos from one Drive
        // folder at execution time. The folder is expanded by the Master into
        // runtime_assets; the producer never assigns individual files to scenes.
        StockPool *StockPoolV2 `json:"stock_pool,omitempty"`
        Assets    []AssetRefV2 `json:"assets"`
    }
    
    // StockPoolV2 is the single canonical stock selection rule for a job.
    // Selection is deterministic per job so retries reproduce the same edit.
    type StockPoolV2 struct {
        SourceKind    string `json:"source_kind"`
        DriveFolderID string `json:"drive_folder_id"`
        Selection     string `json:"selection"`
    }
    
    // OutputContractV2 describes the normalized output timeline and container.
    type OutputContractV2 struct {
        Container   string `json:"container"`
        VideoCodec  string `json:"video_codec"`
        Width       int    `json:"width"`
        Height      int    `json:"height"`
        FPSNum      int    `json:"fps_num"`
        FPSDen      int    `json:"fps_den"`
        PixelFormat string `json:"pixel_format,omitempty"`
    
        // Strengthened canonical-profile fields. The native packet-copy executor
        // validates the complete profile before execution.
        ProfileID    string `json:"profile_id,omitempty"`
        CodecProfile string `json:"codec_profile,omitempty"`
        CodecLevel   string `json:"codec_level,omitempty"`
        GOPSize      int    `json:"gop_size,omitempty"`
        // b_frames is required by the native canonical-profile parser even when
        // the canonical value is zero; omitting it would make Go's canonical JSON

        BFrames     int  `json:"b_frames"`
        ClosedGOP   bool `json:"closed_gop,omitempty"`
        TimeBaseNum int  `json:"time_base_num,omitempty"`
        TimeBaseDen int  `json:"time_base_den,omitempty"`
    }
    
    // FinalAudioV2 identifies the one already-finalized audio source for the

    type FinalAudioV2 struct {
        Mode string `json:"mode"`

    func TestCompiledRenderPlanV2_CanonicalizationSortsAssetsWithoutMutation(t *testing.T) {
        plan := testCompiledRenderPlanV2()
        if plan.Assets[0].AssetID != "video-a" {
            t.Fatalf("test fixture must start in non-canonical order")
        }
    
        canonical, err := plan.CanonicalJSON()
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("CanonicalJSON: %v", err)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(string(canonical), `"assets":[{"asset_id":"audio-master"`) {
            t.Fatalf("assets were not sorted by asset_id: %s", canonical)
        }
        if plan.Assets[0].AssetID != "video-a" {
            t.Fatalf("CanonicalJSON mutated caller assets: first asset = %q", plan.Assets[0].AssetID)
        }
    }
    
    func TestCompiledRenderPlanV2_PlanSHA256MatchesCanonicalBytes(t *testing.T) {
        plan := testCompiledRenderPlanV2()
        canonical, err := plan.CanonicalJSON()
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("CanonicalJSON: %v", err)
        }
        got, err := plan.PlanSHA256()
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("PlanSHA256: %v", err)
        }
        if want := HashCompiledPlanV2(canonical); got != want {
            t.Fatalf("PlanSHA256 = %q, HashCompiledPlanV2 = %q", got, want)
        }
        if len(got) != 64 {
            t.Fatalf("SHA256 length = %d, want 64", len(got))
        }
    }

    // DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2 strictly decodes, validates, and canonical-form
    // checks a V2 JSON document. Unknown fields, trailing JSON, semantic errors,
    // and non-canonical whitespace/order are all rejected.
    func DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2(data []byte) (*CompiledRenderPlanV2, error) {
        if len(bytes.TrimSpace(data)) == 0 {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: empty document")
        }
    
        decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
        decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
        var plan CompiledRenderPlanV2
        if err := decoder.Decode(&plan); err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: strict decode: %w", err)
        }
        var trailing any
        if err := decoder.Decode(&trailing); err != io.EOF {
            if err == nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: trailing JSON value")
            }
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: trailing data: %w", err)
        }
        if err := ValidateCompiledRenderPlanV2(&plan); err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
    
        canonical, err := plan.CanonicalJSON()
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        if !bytes.Equal(data, canonical) {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: document is not canonical JSON")
        }
        return &plan, nil
    }
    
    // ValidateCompiledRenderPlanV2JSON is the validation-oriented alias for the
    // strict decoder. It returns the decoded plan for callers that need it after
    // admission.
    func ValidateCompiledRenderPlanV2JSON(data []byte) (*CompiledRenderPlanV2, error) {
        return DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2(data)
    }
    
    // DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2Payload is the single TaskOffer-envelope boundary
    // for a V2 compiled plan. It verifies the exact wire SHA and delegates the
    // document checks to DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2. A payload without either V2
    // key returns (nil, nil) so legacy workers remain unaffected; a partial or
    // malformed envelope fails closed.
    func DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2Payload(raw map[string]interface{}) (*CompiledRenderPlanV2, error) {
        if raw == nil {
            return nil, nil
        }
        planJSON, hasJSON := raw[PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanJSON]
        planSHA, hasSHA := raw[PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanSHA]
        if !hasJSON && !hasSHA {
            return nil, nil
        }
        if !hasJSON {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: %q is required when %q is present", PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanJSON, PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanSHA)
        }
        if !hasSHA {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: %q is required when %q is present", PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanSHA, PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanJSON)
        }

    // CanonicalJSON returns the deterministic V2 document used for persistence
    // and hashing. Asset references are sorted by AssetID because their order is
    // set-like; track and segment order is preserved because it is semantic.
    // Nil slices are normalized to empty arrays so equivalent empty collections
    // never alternate between JSON null and [].
    func (p *CompiledRenderPlanV2) CanonicalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
        if p == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: nil plan")
        }
    
        canonical := *p
        canonical.VideoTracks = cloneVideoTracks(p.VideoTracks)
        canonical.Assets = append([]AssetRefV2(nil), p.Assets...)
        sort.SliceStable(canonical.Assets, func(i, j int) bool {
            left, right := canonical.Assets[i], canonical.Assets[j]
            if left.AssetID != right.AssetID {
                return left.AssetID < right.AssetID
            }
            // Asset IDs are expected to be unique, but deterministic tie-breaking
            // keeps canonicalization stable even before semantic validation runs.
            return assetRefV2SortKey(left) < assetRefV2SortKey(right)
        })

            canonical.VideoTracks = []VideoTrackV2{}

    func verifyFirstPacketKeyframe(ctx context.Context, path string) error {
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries", "packet=flags", "-read_intervals", "%+#1", "-of", "csv=p=0", path)
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("ffprobe first packet: %w", err)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(string(out), "K") {
            return errors.New("first video packet is not a keyframe")
        }
        return nil
    }

        n := plan.DurationUS * int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
        d := int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000
        return (n + d - 1) / d
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) verifyCopyInputs(ctx context.Context, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, bindings runtimeassets.Bindings) error {
        assets := make(map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, len(plan.Assets))
        for _, asset := range plan.Assets {

                return fmt.Errorf("source %q is not integrity-verified against the plan", asset.AssetID)
            }
            info, statErr := os.Stat(binding.Path)
            if statErr != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Size() != binding.Size {
                return fmt.Errorf("source %q local file identity is invalid", asset.AssetID)
            }
            probe, err := e.prober.ProbeMediaDetails(ctx, binding.Path)
            if err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("probe source %q: %w", asset.AssetID, err)
            }

            }
            if probe.VideoFrameCount <= 0 || probe.VideoFrameCount != asset.FrameCount {

            }
            wantLevel, _ := strconv.Atoi(strings.ReplaceAll(plan.Output.CodecLevel, ".", ""))
            if probe.VideoCodec != "h264" || !strings.EqualFold(probe.VideoProfile, plan.Output.CodecProfile) || probe.VideoLevel != wantLevel || probe.VideoBFrames != plan.Output.BFrames || probe.VideoExtradataHash == "" || probe.VideoTimeBaseNum <= 0 || probe.VideoTimeBaseDen <= 0 || probe.Width != plan.Output.Width || probe.Height != plan.Output.Height || probe.VideoFPSNum != plan.Output.FPSNum || probe.VideoFPSDen != plan.Output.FPSDen || probe.VideoPixelFormat != plan.Output.PixelFormat {
                return fmt.Errorf("source %q media profile differs from the output; refusing to transcode", asset.AssetID)
            }
            if baseline == nil {
                copy := probe
                baseline = &copy
            } else if !sameSliceCopySignature(*baseline, probe) {
                return fmt.Errorf("source %q codec parameters/time base differ from the other inputs; refusing to transcode", asset.AssetID)
            }
            probes[asset.AssetID] = probe
        }
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            probe := probes[segment.AssetID]
            actualUS := int64(probe.DurationSec * 1_000_000)
            windowEnd := segment.SourceInUS + segment.SourceDurationUS
            frameUS := int64(1_000_000 * plan.Output.FPSDen / plan.Output.FPSNum)
            if windowEnd > actualUS+frameUS {
                return fmt.Errorf("source %q window ends at %d us beyond probed duration %d us", segment.AssetID, windowEnd, actualUS)
            }
        }
        return nil
    }

    func writeSliceConcatList(path string, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, bindings runtimeassets.Bindings) error {
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString("ffconcat version 1.0\n")
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            binding, ok := bindings[segment.AssetID]
            if !ok || !binding.Verified || strings.TrimSpace(binding.Path) == "" {
                return fmt.Errorf("source %q is not ready for stream-copy concat", segment.AssetID)
            }
            abs, err := filepath.Abs(binding.Path)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            // The concat demuxer uses shell-like single-quoted paths; embedded
            // quotes are represented by closing, escaping, and reopening quotes.
            quoted := strings.ReplaceAll(abs, "'", "'\\''")
            frameDurationUS := segment.FrameCount * int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000 / int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
            fmt.Fprintf(&b, "file '%s'\ninpoint 0\noutpoint %s\n", quoted, seconds(frameDurationUS))
        }
        return os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o600)
    }
    
    func sliceConcatMuxArgs(listPath, audioPath, output string, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) ([]string, error) {
        if strings.TrimSpace(audioPath) == "" {
            return nil, errors.New("final audio path is empty")
        }
        return []string{"-nostdin", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y",
            "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", listPath,
            "-threads", "1", "-i", audioPath,
            "-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c:v", "copy", "-c:a", "copy",
            "-frames:v", strconv.FormatInt(slicePlanFrameCount(plan), 10),
            "-t", seconds(plan.DurationUS), "-video_track_timescale", strconv.Itoa(plan.Output.TimeBaseDen),
            "-movflags", "+faststart", output}, nil
    }
    
    func slicePlanFrameCount(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) int64 {
        var frames int64
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            frames += segment.FrameCount
        }
        return frames
    }
    
    func seconds(microseconds int64) string {
        return strconv.FormatFloat(float64(microseconds)/1_000_000, 'f', 6, 64)
    }

    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) Execute(ctx context.Context, execCtx executor.ExecutionContext, spec executor.TaskSpec) (executor.ExecutionResult, error) {
        started := time.Now().UTC()
        fail := func(code string, err error) (executor.ExecutionResult, error) {
            return executor.ExecutionResult{Status: "failed", ErrorCode: code, ErrorDetail: err.Error(), StartedAt: started, CompletedAt: time.Now().UTC()}, nil
        }
        if err := e.Validate(spec); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID", err)
        }
        plan, _ := decodeCompiledPlanV2(spec)
        bindings, ok := runtimeassets.FromContext(ctx)
        if !ok {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_MISSING", errors.New("verified runtime asset bindings are required"))
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil {
            compiled, err := e.compileStockPoolPlan(ctx, spec, plan, bindings)
            if err != nil {
                return fail("DRIVE_STOCK_POOL_INCOMPATIBLE", err)
            }
            plan = compiled
        }
        if err := e.verifyCopyInputs(ctx, plan, bindings); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_COPY_INCOMPATIBLE", err)
        }
        audio, ok := bindings[plan.FinalAudio.AssetID]
        if !ok || !audio.Verified || audio.Size <= 0 || audio.SHA256 == "" || audio.SHA256 != plan.FinalAudio.SHA256 || audio.Size != plan.FinalAudio.SizeBytes {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_INVALID", errors.New("final audio integrity binding does not match the plan"))
        }
        if info, statErr := os.Stat(audio.Path); statErr != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Size() != audio.Size {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_INVALID", errors.New("final audio local file identity is invalid"))
        }
        jobID, err := safeOutputJobID(spec.JobID)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("INVALID_JOB_ID", err)
        }
        outputPath := filepath.Join(e.outputRoot, jobID+".mp4")
        if resolver := storageResolverFromExecutionContext(execCtx); resolver != nil {
            if placement, placeErr := resolver.Place(storage.ArtifactStaging, jobID+".mp4", estimateOutputBytesFromDuration(plan.DurationUS)); placeErr == nil {
                outputPath = placement.Path
            }
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(outputPath), 0o750); err != nil {
            return fail("OUTPUT_DIRECTORY", err)
        }
        // The concat manifest is the only temporary file. Video packets are copied
        // directly from the verified cache; this executor never invokes an encoder.
        workRoot := filepath.Dir(outputPath)
        if resolver := storageResolverFromExecutionContext(execCtx); resolver != nil {
            workRoot = resolver.Config().TempDir
        }
        if strings.TrimSpace(workRoot) == "" {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_STORAGE_INVALID", errors.New("disk-backed slice work directory is not configured"))
        }
        tempDir, err := os.MkdirTemp(workRoot, "drive-slice-copy-"+jobID+"-")
        if err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_STORAGE_INVALID", err)
        }
        defer os.RemoveAll(tempDir)
        listPath := filepath.Join(tempDir, "segments.ffconcat")
        if err := writeSliceConcatList(listPath, plan, bindings); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_STORAGE_INVALID", err)
        }
        args, err := sliceConcatMuxArgs(listPath, audio.Path, outputPath, plan)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_INVALID", err)
        }
        metrics, renderErr := e.runner.Run(ctx, ffmpegrunner.FFmpegRequest{Operation: ffmpegrunner.OperationEncode, Args: args})
        if renderErr != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_COPY_FAILED", fmt.Errorf("stream-copy concat/mux: %w", renderErr))
        }
        if err := e.verifyFinalMedia(ctx, outputPath, plan); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_OUTPUT_INVALID", err)
        }
        artifact, err := artifactFromFile("video/mp4", outputPath)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("FINAL_OUTPUT_INVALID", err)
        }
        raw := rawMetricsFromFFmpegResult(metrics)
        raw.OutputBytes = artifact.SizeBytes
        raw.OutputFileSize = artifact.SizeBytes
        raw.OutputSha256 = artifact.Hash
        raw.EncodePasses = 0
        raw.ConcatMode = "stream_copy"
        raw.FinalConcatStreamCopy = true
        raw.MediaDurationSeconds = float64(plan.DurationUS) / 1_000_000
        raw.WallClockSeconds = float64(metrics.ProcessWallMS) / 1000
        return executor.ExecutionResult{
            Status: "succeeded", Outputs: []executor.ArtifactRef{artifact}, RawMetrics: raw,
            StartedAt: started, CompletedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
        }, nil
    }

    package executors
    
    import (
        "context"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "strings"
        "testing"
    
        "velox-shared/contract"
        "velox-worker-agent/internal/publisher"

    )
    
    type sliceFFmpegRunner struct {
        args        [][]string
        concatInput string
    }
    
    func (r *sliceFFmpegRunner) Run(_ context.Context, req ffmpegrunner.FFmpegRequest) (ffmpegrunner.FFmpegResult, error) {
        r.args = append(r.args, append([]string(nil), req.Args...))
        for i := 0; i+1 < len(req.Args); i++ {
            if req.Args[i] == "-i" && strings.HasSuffix(req.Args[i+1], "segments.ffconcat") {
                data, err := os.ReadFile(req.Args[i+1])
                if err != nil {
                    return ffmpegrunner.FFmpegResult{}, err
                }
                r.concatInput = string(data)
            }
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(req.Args[len(req.Args)-1], []byte("remote-render"), 0o640); err != nil {
            return ffmpegrunner.FFmpegResult{}, err
        }
        return ffmpegrunner.FFmpegResult{ProcessWallMS: 12}, nil
    }
    
    type sliceMediaProbeStub struct{}
    
    func (sliceMediaProbeStub) ProbeMediaDetails(_ context.Context, path string) (publisher.MediaProbe, error) {
        if strings.HasSuffix(path, "stock.mp4") {
            return publisher.MediaProbe{HasVideo: true, VideoCodec: "h264", VideoCodecTag: "avc1", VideoProfile: "High", VideoLevel: 40, VideoPixelFormat: "yuv420p", VideoFPSNum: 24, VideoFPSDen: 1, VideoTimeBaseNum: 1, VideoTimeBaseDen: 90000, VideoExtradataHash: "same-sps", VideoFrameCount: 480, DurationSec: 20, Width: 1920, Height: 1080}, nil
        }
        return publisher.MediaProbe{HasVideo: true, HasAudio: true, VideoCodec: "h264", AudioCodec: "aac", VideoProfile: "High", VideoLevel: 40, VideoPixelFormat: "yuv420p", VideoFPSNum: 24, VideoFPSDen: 1, VideoFrameCount: 24, DurationSec: 1, Width: 1920, Height: 1080}, nil
    }
    
    func driveSlicePlan() *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2 {
        const timelineHash = "cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc"
        return &contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2{
            PlanVersion: 2, TimelineRevision: 7, TimelineSHA256: timelineHash, DurationUS: 1_000_000,
            Output: contract.OutputContractV2{
                Container: "mp4", VideoCodec: "h264", Width: 1920, Height: 1080,
                FPSNum: 24, FPSDen: 1, PixelFormat: "yuv420p", ProfileID: contract.CanonicalVideoProfileIDV1,
                CodecProfile: "high", CodecLevel: "4.0", GOPSize: 48, BFrames: 0,
                ClosedGOP: true, TimeBaseNum: 1, TimeBaseDen: 90000,
            },
            FinalAudio:  contract.FinalAudioV2{Mode: contract.AudioModeFinalAudioCopy, AssetID: "audio", SHA256: copyOnlySHA([]byte("audio")), SizeBytes: 5, Codec: "aac", SampleRateHz: 48000, Channels: 2, DurationUS: 1_000_000, TimelineRevision: 7, TimelineSHA256: timelineHash},
            VideoTracks: []contract.VideoTrackV2{{TrackID: "main", Segments: []contract.VideoSegmentV2{{SegmentID: "segment-0003", AssetID: "drive:stock-01", TimelineStartFrame: 0, FrameCount: 24, SourceInUS: 0, SourceDurationUS: 1_000_000}}}},
            Assets: []contract.AssetRefV2{
                {AssetID: "drive:stock-01", AssetKey: "drive:stock-01", SourceKind: "drive", DriveFileID: "stock-01", SHA256: strings.Repeat("b", 64), SizeBytes: 5, Kind: "video", DurationUS: 20_000_000, Width: 1920, Height: 1080, ProfileID: contract.CanonicalVideoProfileIDV1, FrameCount: 480, FirstFrameKeyframe: true, ClosedGOP: true},
                {AssetID: "audio", SHA256: copyOnlySHA([]byte("audio")), SizeBytes: 5, Kind: "final_audio", DurationUS: 1_000_000},
            },
        }
    }
    
    func TestVideoAssembleSlice_CopiesDriveSourceWindowsWithoutReencoding(t *testing.T) {
        plan := driveSlicePlan()
        canonical, err := plan.CanonicalJSON()
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        videoPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "stock.mp4")
        audioPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "audio.m4a")
        if err := os.WriteFile(videoPath, []byte("stock"), 0o640); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(audioPath, []byte("audio"), 0o640); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        runner := &sliceFFmpegRunner{}
        exec := &videoAssembleSliceExecutor{runner: runner, prober: sliceMediaProbeStub{}, outputRoot: t.TempDir()}
        spec := executorTaskSpec(VideoAssembleSliceID, "job-drive-slice", canonical, plan)
        result, err := exec.Execute(runtimeassets.WithBindings(context.Background(), runtimeassets.Bindings{
            "drive:stock-01": {AssetID: "drive:stock-01", Path: videoPath, SHA256: strings.Repeat("b", 64), Size: 5, Verified: true},
            "audio":          {AssetID: "audio", Path: audioPath, SHA256: copyOnlySHA([]byte("audio")), Size: 5, Verified: true},
        }), nil, spec)
        if err != nil || result.Status != "succeeded" {
            t.Fatalf("slice execution result=%+v err=%v", result, err)
        }
        if len(result.Outputs) != 1 || result.RawMetrics == nil || result.RawMetrics.ConcatMode != "stream_copy" || result.RawMetrics.EncodePasses != 0 || !result.RawMetrics.FinalConcatStreamCopy {
            t.Fatalf("slice result did not report copy-only remote assembly: %+v", result)
        }
        if len(runner.args) != 1 {
            t.Fatalf("FFmpeg call count = %d, want one stream-copy concat/mux", len(runner.args))
        }
        copyArgs := strings.Join(runner.args[0], " ")
        for _, want := range []string{"-f concat", "-c:v copy", "-c:a copy", "-frames:v 24"} {
            if !strings.Contains(copyArgs, want) {
                t.Errorf("FFmpeg stream-copy args missing %q: %s", want, copyArgs)
            }
        }
        if strings.Contains(copyArgs, "libx264") || strings.Contains(copyArgs, "filter_complex") {
            t.Fatalf("copy path must not contain an encoder or filter graph: %s", copyArgs)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(runner.concatInput, "inpoint 0\noutpoint 1.000000") {
            t.Fatalf("concat manifest does not contain the expected source window: %q", runner.concatInput)
        }
        if strings.Contains(copyArgs, "14.000000") {
            t.Fatalf("copy path unexpectedly trims a non-keyframe source offset: %s", copyArgs)
        }
        }
    }
    
    func TestVideoAssembleSlice_RejectsNonKeyframeOffsetBeforeFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
        plan := driveSlicePlan()

        if err != nil || result.Status != "failed" {
            t.Fatalf("invalid copy plan result=%+v err=%v, want immediate failure", result, err)

            t.Fatalf("invalid cut was not rejected before FFmpeg: result=%+v ffmpeg_calls=%d", result, len(runner.args))
        }
    }

    +func TestCompatibleAVC1AVC3CopyPairAllowsContainerVariantWithoutTranscoding(t *testing.T) {
    +	stock := publisher.MediaProbe{
    +		VideoCodec: "h264", VideoCodecTag: "avc1", VideoProfile: "High", VideoLevel: 40,
    +		VideoPixelFormat: "yuv420p", VideoFPSNum: 24, VideoFPSDen: 1,
    +		VideoTimeBaseNum: 1, VideoTimeBaseDen: 12288, VideoExtradataHash: "stock-sps-pps",
    +	}
    +	overlay := stock
    +	overlay.VideoCodecTag = "avc3"
    +	overlay.VideoTimeBaseDen = 90000
    +	overlay.VideoExtradataHash = "overlay-inband-sps-pps"
    +	if !compatibleAVC1AVC3CopyPair(stock, overlay) {
    +		t.Fatal("compatible avc1/avc3 H.264 streams with in-band parameter sets were rejected")
    +	}
    +	if sameSliceCopySignature(stock, overlay) {
    +		t.Fatal("container variants should remain distinct signatures")
    +	}
    +	args, err := sliceConcatMuxArgs("segments.ffconcat", "audio.m4a", "out.mp4", driveSlicePlan(), "avc3")
    +	if err != nil {
    +		t.Fatal(err)
    +	}
    +	joined := strings.Join(args, " ")
    +	if !strings.Contains(joined, "-tag:v avc3") || strings.Contains(joined, "libx264") {
    +		t.Fatalf("mixed container stream-copy must signal avc3 without encoding: %s", joined)
    +	}
    +
    +	divergent := overlay
    +	divergent.VideoLevel = 41
    +	if compatibleAVC1AVC3CopyPair(stock, divergent) {
    +		t.Fatal("divergent H.264 levels must still be rejected")
    +	}
    +	divergent = overlay
    +	divergent.VideoCodecTag = "avc1"
    +	if compatibleAVC1AVC3CopyPair(stock, divergent) {
    +		t.Fatal("avc1-to-avc1 parameter-set drift must still be rejected")
    +	}
    +}

## Assistant

Ho trovato il secondo punto: i 240 stock sono coerenti tra loro, mentre i 22 overlay usano lo stesso H.264 ma il contenitore segnala `avc3` con time base diverso dai `avc1` stock. Ho verificato con FFmpeg che si concatenano e si decodificano in stream-copy; sto aggiornando il worker per accettare solo questa combinazione compatibile e produrre `avc3`, mantenendo il rifiuto per differenze di profilo, livello o frame rate.

    The retired Ansible deployment API no longer executes playbooks. Host
    connectivity remains owned by `WorkerNodeRegistry`/`ansible_hosts`; release
    activation runs only through FleetController. There
    is no operator-side static inventory and no `--vault-password-file`:
    
    ```bash
    export MASTER_URL=https://MASTER.example.invalid:8000
    
    # 1. Drain through the Master and wait until active_tasks=0.
    scripts/fleetctl drain <worker_id> "legacy bridge rollout"
    scripts/fleetctl inspect <worker_id>   # repeat until DRAINING and active_tasks=0
    # 2. Trigger the Master-side preflight/update for this worker via
    #    POST /api/v1/admin/ansible/computers/run_action (action=update).
    ```
    
    Before proceeding, verify the bundle identity against the commit, version,
    source/bundle hash and engine hash that are intended for the canary. This path
    still performs a local build on the worker, so it is a bridge and not a
    reproducible GHCR release deployment.
    
    After the bridge, verify the canonical unit, one container, readiness,
    registration, fresh heartbeat, a real Level-D smoke, and a short canary window.
    Only then resume the worker and continue one host at a time.
    
    ### One-time migration limitations
    
    - It does **not** prove that every worker runs identical image bytes; use the
      digest rollout path for release certification.
    - It must not be used to roll out a mutable Docker tag.
    - It must not be run against all workers concurrently.
    - It must not be used as evidence that a GHCR digest was signed or certified.
    - Once the completion marker exists, do not re-run legacy cleanup as part of a
      normal rollout; investigate a missing marker or broken canonical tree first.
    
    ## 2. GHCR Ansible bridge — RETIRED
    
    The transitional host-side bridge (`deploy/playbooks/rollout-worker-digest.yml`,
    `FLEET_INVENTORY`, `FLEET_ROLLOUT_PLAYBOOK`, `ansible-playbook`) has been
    retired. `scripts/fleetctl update` / `scripts/fleetctl rollback` now POST the
    pinned digest directly to the Master API and poll the `fleet_operations`
    ledger; see §3.

    func verifyFirstPacketKeyframe(ctx context.Context, path string) error {
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries", "packet=flags", "-read_intervals", "%+#1", "-of", "csv=p=0", path)
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("ffprobe first packet: %w", err)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(string(out), "K") {
            return errors.New("first video packet is not a keyframe")
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    func slicePlanDurationFrameCount(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) int64 {
        n := plan.DurationUS * int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
        d := int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000
        return (n + d - 1) / d
    }

    +func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) remuxAVC3Timebases(ctx context.Context, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, bindings runtimeassets.Bindings, compatibility sliceCopyCompatibility, tempDir string) (map[string]string, error) {
    +	if len(compatibility.RemuxAssetIDs) == 0 {
    +		return nil, nil
    +	}
    +	if compatibility.TimeBaseNum != 1 || compatibility.TimeBaseDen <= 0 {
    +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported packet-copy normalization time base %d/%d", compatibility.TimeBaseNum, compatibility.TimeBaseDen)
    +	}
    +	assets := make(map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, len(plan.Assets))
    +	for _, asset := range plan.Assets {
    +		assets[asset.AssetID] = asset
    +	}
    +	assetIDs := make([]string, 0, len(compatibility.RemuxAssetIDs))
    +	for assetID := range compatibility.RemuxAssetIDs {
    +		assetIDs = append(assetIDs, assetID)
    +	}
    +	sort.Strings(assetIDs)
    +	paths := make(map[string]string, len(assetIDs))
    +	for i, assetID := range assetIDs {
    +		binding, ok := bindings[assetID]
    +		if !ok || !binding.Verified || strings.TrimSpace(binding.Path) == "" {
    +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("avc3 source %q is not available for packet-copy time-base normalization", assetID)
    +		}
    +		path := filepath.Join(tempDir, fmt.Sprintf("normalized-%03d.mp4", i))
    +		args := []string{"-nostdin", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-i", binding.Path,
    +			"-map", "0:v:0", "-c:v", "copy", "-tag:v", "avc3", "-video_track_timescale", strconv.Itoa(compatibility.TimeBaseDen), path}
    +		if _, err := e.runner.Run(ctx, ffmpegrunner.FFmpegRequest{Operation: ffmpegrunner.OperationEncode, Args: args}); err != nil {
    +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("packet-copy remux source %q to time base %d/%d: %w", assetID, compatibility.TimeBaseNum, compatibility.TimeBaseDen, err)
    +		}
    +		probe, err := e.prober.ProbeMediaDetails(ctx, path)
    +		if err != nil {
    +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("probe packet-copy remux source %q: %w", assetID, err)
    +		}
    +		original, err := e.prober.ProbeMediaDetails(ctx, binding.Path)
    +		if err != nil {
    +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("recheck original avc3 source %q: %w", assetID, err)
    +		}
    +		if probe.VideoCodec != "h264" || probe.VideoCodecTag != "avc3" || probe.VideoFrameCount != assets[assetID].FrameCount || probe.VideoExtradataHash != original.VideoExtradataHash || probe.VideoTimeBaseNum != compatibility.TimeBaseNum || probe.VideoTimeBaseDen != compatibility.TimeBaseDen {
    +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("packet-copy remux source %q did not preserve its H.264 packets and target time base", assetID)

## Assistant

Ho individuato e corretto anche il motivo del conteggio frame corto: FFmpeg concat gestiva male PTS con time base diversi. Il worker ora fa un remux **stream-copy** solo dei 22 overlay, uniformando la loro time base a quella degli stock; i pacchetti video restano identici. Una prova stock+overlay produce 227/227 frame a 24 fps e si decodifica senza errori. Ora ricostruisco l’immagine e ripeto il job completo.
