    struct CertifiedAsset {
        std::string asset_id;
        std::string sha256;
        std::string kind;
        std::string mime;
        std::string profile_id;
        std::string timeline_sha256;
        int64_t duration_us{0};
        int64_t frame_count{0};
        int64_t timeline_revision{0};
        int64_t timeline_start_frame{0};
        bool first_frame_keyframe{false};
        bool closed_gop{false};
    };
    
    bool canonicalPacketCopyOutput(
        const std::string& output,
        const velox::core::CanonicalVideoProfile& profile) {
        return ju::extractJsonStringValue(output, "container") == profile.container &&
            ju::extractJsonStringValue(output, "video_codec") == profile.stream_codec &&
            ju::extractJsonNumberValue(output, "width") == profile.width &&
            ju::extractJsonNumberValue(output, "height") == profile.height &&
            ju::extractJsonNumberValue(output, "fps_num") == profile.fps_num &&
            ju::extractJsonNumberValue(output, "fps_den") == profile.fps_den &&
            ju::extractJsonStringValue(output, "pixel_format") == profile.pixel_format_name &&
            ju::extractJsonStringValue(output, "profile_id") == profile.profile_id &&
            ju::extractJsonStringValue(output, "codec_profile") == profile.codec_profile_name &&
            ju::extractJsonStringValue(output, "codec_level") == profile.codec_level_name &&
            ju::hasJsonKey(output, "gop_size") &&
            ju::extractJsonNumberValue(output, "gop_size") == profile.gop_size &&
            ju::hasJsonKey(output, "b_frames") &&
            ju::extractJsonNumberValue(output, "b_frames") == profile.max_b_frames &&
            ju::hasJsonKey(output, "closed_gop") &&
            ju::extractJsonBoolValue(output, "closed_gop") &&
            ju::extractJsonNumberValue(output, "time_base_num") == profile.time_base_num &&
            ju::extractJsonNumberValue(output, "time_base_den") == profile.time_base_den;
    }
    
    std::vector<CertifiedAsset> parseAssetCertificates(const std::string& json) {
        std::vector<CertifiedAsset> assets;
        const auto block = ju::extractArrayBlock(json, "assets");
        for (const auto& object : ju::splitTopLevelObjects(block)) {
            CertifiedAsset asset;
            asset.asset_id = ju::extractJsonStringValue(object, "asset_id");
            asset.sha256 = ju::extractJsonStringValue(object, "sha256");
            asset.kind = ju::extractJsonStringValue(object, "kind");
            asset.mime = ju::extractJsonStringValue(object, "mime");
            asset.profile_id = ju::extractJsonStringValue(object, "profile_id");
            asset.timeline_sha256 = ju::extractJsonStringValue(object, "timeline_sha256");
            asset.duration_us = static_cast<int64_t>(
                ju::extractJsonNumberValue(object, "duration_us", 0.0));
            asset.frame_count = static_cast<int64_t>(
                ju::extractJsonNumberValue(object, "frame_count", 0.0));
            asset.timeline_revision = static_cast<int64_t>(
                ju::extractJsonNumberValue(object, "timeline_revision", 0.0));
            asset.timeline_start_frame = static_cast<int64_t>(
                ju::extractJsonNumberValue(object, "timeline_start_frame", -1.0));
            asset.first_frame_keyframe = ju::hasJsonKey(object, "first_frame_keyframe") &&
                ju::extractJsonBoolValue(object, "first_frame_keyframe");
            asset.closed_gop = ju::hasJsonKey(object, "closed_gop") &&
                ju::extractJsonBoolValue(object, "closed_gop");
            if (!asset.asset_id.empty()) assets.push_back(std::move(asset));
        }
        return assets;
    }
    
    const CertifiedAsset* findAsset(const std::vector<CertifiedAsset>& assets,
                                    const std::string& asset_id) {
        for (const auto& asset : assets) {
            if (asset.asset_id == asset_id) return &asset;
        }
        return nullptr;
    }
    
    bool certifiedVideoAsset(const CertifiedAsset* asset,
                             const std::string& stream_profile_id,
                             const std::string& segment_sha256,
                             const std::string& timeline_sha256,
                             int64_t timeline_revision,
                             int64_t timeline_start_frame,
                             int64_t frame_count,
                             int64_t duration_us,
                             int64_t source_in_us) {
        return asset != nullptr &&
            (asset->kind == "video" || asset->kind == "prepared_video_fragment") &&
            asset->sha256 == segment_sha256 &&
            asset->profile_id == stream_profile_id &&
            asset->frame_count == frame_count &&
            asset->timeline_revision == timeline_revision &&
            asset->timeline_sha256 == timeline_sha256 &&
            asset->timeline_start_frame == timeline_start_frame &&
            asset->duration_us == duration_us &&
            asset->first_frame_keyframe && asset->closed_gop && source_in_us == 0;
    }

    // RenderCompiledPlanV2 delegates to the native zero-spawn V2 path. A runner
    // without that capability fails closed; it never falls back to FFmpeg.
    func (r *Runner) RenderCompiledPlanV2(ctx context.Context, planJSON []byte, outputPath string) (RenderMetrics, error) {
        if r == nil || r.renderClient == nil {
            return RenderMetrics{}, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: compiled V2 renderer is not configured")
        }
        renderer, ok := r.renderClient.(CompiledPlanV2Renderer)
        if !ok {
            return RenderMetrics{}, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: compiled V2 renderer is not supported")
        }
        return renderer.RenderCompiledPlanV2(ctx, planJSON, outputPath)
    }

        return &Runner{
            registry:     registry,

            logger:       log,
        }
    }

    bool initializeOutputStream(AVFormatContext* output, const AVStream* input,
                                AVStream*& destination, std::string& error) {
        destination = avformat_new_stream(output, nullptr);
        if (destination == nullptr) {
            error = "avformat_new_stream failed";
            return false;
        }
        const int rc = avcodec_parameters_copy(destination->codecpar, input->codecpar);
        if (rc < 0) {
            error = "avcodec_parameters_copy: " + packet::ffmpegError(rc);
            return false;
        }
        destination->codecpar->codec_tag = 0;
        destination->time_base = packet::kMicrosecondTimeBase;
        destination->avg_frame_rate = input->avg_frame_rate;
        return true;
    }
    
    int64_t streamDurationUs(const AVFormatContext* context, const AVStream* stream) {
        if (stream != nullptr && packet::validTimestamp(stream->duration) && stream->duration > 0) {

    func marshalCopyOnlyWire(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, jobID, outputPath string, bindings runtimeassets.Bindings) ([]byte, error) {
        if plan == nil || strings.TrimSpace(jobID) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(outputPath) == "" {
            return nil, errors.New("video.assemble.copy.v1: incomplete native wire document")
        }
        paths := make(map[string]string, len(bindings))
        for assetID, binding := range bindings {
            paths[assetID] = binding.Path
        }
        return json.Marshal(copyOnlyPlanWire{CompiledRenderPlanV2: plan, JobID: jobID, OutputPath: outputPath, Bindings: paths})
    }

    // registerCanonicalRenderExecutors installs the sole worker entry point for
    // compiled V2 video plans: packet-copy assembly.
    func registerCanonicalRenderExecutors(reg *executor.Registry, outputRoot string, runners []*pipeline.Runner) error {
        if len(runners) > 0 && runners[0] != nil {
            if err := reg.Register(executors.NewVideoAssembleCopy(runners[0], outputRoot)); err != nil {
                return err
            }
        }
        if err := reg.Register(executors.NewVideoAssembleSlice(outputRoot, ffmpegrunner.NewProcessRunner())); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        return nil
    }

    func slicePlanDurationFrameCount(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) int64 {
        n := plan.DurationUS * int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
        d := int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000
        return (n + d - 1) / d
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) verifyFinalMedia(ctx context.Context, outputPath string, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) error {
        probe, err := e.prober.ProbeMediaDetails(ctx, outputPath)
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("probe assembled output: %w", err)
        }
        if !probe.HasVideo || !probe.HasAudio || probe.VideoCodec != "h264" || probe.AudioCodec != "aac" || probe.Width != plan.Output.Width || probe.Height != plan.Output.Height {
            return fmt.Errorf("assembled output streams/profile invalid: video=%t/%s audio=%t/%s size=%dx%d want=h264/aac %dx%d", probe.HasVideo, probe.VideoCodec, probe.HasAudio, probe.AudioCodec, probe.Width, probe.Height, plan.Output.Width, plan.Output.Height)
        }
        if probe.VideoFrameCount != slicePlanFrameCount(plan) {
            return fmt.Errorf("assembled output has %d frames, plan requires %d; refusing to publish", probe.VideoFrameCount, slicePlanFrameCount(plan))
        }
        wantDuration := float64(plan.DurationUS) / 1_000_000
        frameTolerance := float64(plan.Output.FPSDen)/float64(plan.Output.FPSNum) + 0.1
        if probe.DurationSec <= 0 || probe.DurationSec-wantDuration > frameTolerance || wantDuration-probe.DurationSec > frameTolerance {
            return fmt.Errorf("assembled output duration %.3fs does not match plan %.3fs (tolerance %.3fs)", probe.DurationSec, wantDuration, frameTolerance)
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    func writeSliceConcatList(path string, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, bindings runtimeassets.Bindings) error {
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString("ffconcat version 1.0\n")
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            binding, ok := bindings[segment.AssetID]
            if !ok || !binding.Verified || strings.TrimSpace(binding.Path) == "" {
                return fmt.Errorf("source %q is not ready for stream-copy concat", segment.AssetID)
            }
            abs, err := filepath.Abs(binding.Path)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            quoted := strings.ReplaceAll(abs, "'", "'\\''")
            frameDurationUS := segment.FrameCount * int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000 / int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
            frameDuration := seconds(frameDurationUS)
            fmt.Fprintf(&b, "file '%s'\ninpoint 0\noutpoint %s\nduration %s\n", quoted, frameDuration, frameDuration)
        }
        return os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o600)
    }
    
    func sliceConcatMuxArgs(listPath, audioPath, output string, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, videoTag string) ([]string, error) {
        if strings.TrimSpace(audioPath) == "" {
            return nil, errors.New("final audio path is empty")
        }
        if videoTag != "avc1" && videoTag != "avc3" {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported H.264 MP4 sample entry %q", videoTag)
        }
        return []string{"-nostdin", "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y",
            "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", listPath,
            "-threads", "1", "-i", audioPath,
            "-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c:v", "copy", "-tag:v", videoTag, "-c:a", "copy",
            "-frames:v", strconv.FormatInt(slicePlanFrameCount(plan), 10),
            "-t", seconds(plan.DurationUS), "-video_track_timescale", strconv.Itoa(plan.Output.TimeBaseDen),
            "-movflags", "+faststart", output}, nil
    }
    
    func slicePlanFrameCount(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) int64 {
        var frames int64
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            frames += segment.FrameCount
        }
        return frames
    }

            if left.AssetID != right.AssetID {
                return left.AssetID < right.AssetID

            // Asset IDs are expected to be unique, but deterministic tie-breaking
            // keeps canonicalization stable even before semantic validation runs.
            return assetRefV2SortKey(left) < assetRefV2SortKey(right)

    //

    // The intent is to keep pkg/bootstrap decoupled from the pipeline
    // constructor's identity-check obligations while still letting the
    // self-render step drive the canonical worker-side renderer.
    func (r *Runner) RenderClient() RenderClient {
        if r == nil {
            return nil
        }

    }

    const (
        VideoAssembleSliceID      = "video.assemble.slice.v1"
        VideoAssembleSliceVersion = 1
    )
    
    // videoAssembleSliceExecutor copies compatible source packets from verified
    // runtime assets in the worker cache into the final mux. It never encodes.
    type videoAssembleSliceExecutor struct {
        runner     *pipeline.Runner
        prober     sliceMediaProber
        outputRoot string
    }
    
    type sliceMediaProber interface {
        ProbeMediaDetails(context.Context, string) (publisher.MediaProbe, error)
    }
    
    type ffprobeSliceMediaProber struct{}
    
    func (ffprobeSliceMediaProber) ProbeMediaDetails(ctx context.Context, path string) (publisher.MediaProbe, error) {
        return publisher.ProbeMediaDetails(ctx, path)
    }
    
    func NewVideoAssembleSlice(outputRoot string, runner *pipeline.Runner) executor.Executor {
        if strings.TrimSpace(outputRoot) == "" {
            outputRoot = filepath.Join(os.TempDir(), "velox", "video-assemble-slice")
        }
        return &videoAssembleSliceExecutor{runner: runner, prober: ffprobeSliceMediaProber{}, outputRoot: outputRoot}
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) Descriptor() executor.Descriptor {
        return executor.Descriptor{
            ID: VideoAssembleSliceID, Version: VideoAssembleSliceVersion,
            InputTypes: []string{"render.compiled.v2.drive"}, OutputTypes: []string{"video/mp4"},
            ResourceClass: executor.ResourceCPU, Deterministic: true, Cacheable: true,
            TemporalMode: executor.TemporalGlobal,
        }
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) Validate(spec executor.TaskSpec) error {
        if spec.ExecutorID != VideoAssembleSliceID {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: executor_id must be %q", VideoAssembleSliceID)
        }
        if e == nil || e.runner == nil || e.runner.RenderClient() == nil {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: native packet-copy renderer is not configured")
        }
        if e.prober == nil {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: FFprobe media validation is not configured")
        }
        plan, err := decodeCompiledPlanV2(spec)
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: invalid CompiledRenderPlanV2: %w", err)
        }
        if _, err := contract.KnownCanonicalVideoProfileV1(plan.Output.ProfileID); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: canonical output profile required: %w", err)
        }
        assets := make(map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, len(plan.Assets))
        runtimeDriveIDs := sliceRuntimeDriveFileIDs(spec.Payload["runtime_assets"])
        hasDrive := plan.StockPool != nil
        for _, asset := range plan.Assets {
            assets[asset.AssetID] = asset
            driveSource := asset.Kind == "video" && isSliceDriveSource(asset, runtimeDriveIDs)
            hasDrive = hasDrive || driveSource
        }
        if !hasDrive {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: plan must contain at least one Drive video source")
        }
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || (len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) == 0 && plan.StockPool == nil) {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: exactly one video track is required; segments or stock_pool must be supplied")
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil {
            members := 0
            for _, item := range sliceRuntimePoolMembers(spec.Payload["runtime_assets"]) {
                if item.StockPoolMember && strings.TrimSpace(item.DriveFileID) != "" {
                    members++
                }
            }
            if members == 0 {
                return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: Master did not resolve any stock_pool files")
            }
        }
        var nextFrame int64
        stockPoolSlots := 0
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            if segment.StockPoolSlot {
                if plan.StockPool == nil {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q has stock_pool_slot without stock_pool", segment.SegmentID)
                }
                stockPoolSlots++
                if segment.FrameCount <= 0 {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: stock pool slot %q has invalid frame count", segment.SegmentID)
                }
            } else {
                asset, ok := assets[segment.AssetID]
                if !ok || (asset.Kind != "video" && asset.Kind != "prepared_video_fragment") {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q must reference a video asset", segment.SegmentID)
                }
                if asset.ProfileID != plan.Output.ProfileID || asset.FrameCount <= 0 || !asset.FirstFrameKeyframe || !asset.ClosedGOP {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: asset %q is not certified for packet-copy assembly", segment.AssetID)
                }
                if segment.SourceInUS != 0 {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q starts at a non-keyframe offset (%d us); packet-copy is unsafe", segment.SegmentID, segment.SourceInUS)
                }
                if segment.FrameCount <= 0 || segment.FrameCount > asset.FrameCount {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q frame count %d exceeds certified source frames %d", segment.SegmentID, segment.FrameCount, asset.FrameCount)
                }
            }
            if segment.TimelineStartFrame != nextFrame {
                return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q leaves a timeline gap or overlap at frame %d", segment.SegmentID, nextFrame)
            }
            nextFrame += segment.FrameCount
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil && stockPoolSlots == 0 {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: stock_pool requires at least one stock slot")
        }
        framesNum := int64(plan.DurationUS) * int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
        framesDen := int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000
        wantFrames := (framesNum + framesDen - 1) / framesDen
        if nextFrame != wantFrames {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: timeline has %d frames, plan duration requires %d", nextFrame, wantFrames)
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) Execute(ctx context.Context, execCtx executor.ExecutionContext, spec executor.TaskSpec) (executor.ExecutionResult, error) {
        started := time.Now().UTC()
        fail := func(code string, err error) (executor.ExecutionResult, error) {
            return executor.ExecutionResult{Status: "failed", ErrorCode: code, ErrorDetail: err.Error(), StartedAt: started, CompletedAt: time.Now().UTC()}, nil
        }
        if err := e.Validate(spec); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID", err)
        }
        plan, _ := decodeCompiledPlanV2(spec)
        bindings, ok := runtimeassets.FromContext(ctx)
        if !ok {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_MISSING", errors.New("verified runtime asset bindings are required"))
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil {
            compiled, err := e.compileStockPoolPlan(ctx, spec, plan, bindings)
            if err != nil {
                return fail("DRIVE_STOCK_POOL_INCOMPATIBLE", err)
            }
            plan = compiled
        }
        if err := validateCopyOnlyPlan(plan); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID", err)
        }
        audio, ok := bindings[plan.FinalAudio.AssetID]
        if !ok || !audio.Verified || audio.Size <= 0 || audio.SHA256 == "" || audio.SHA256 != plan.FinalAudio.SHA256 || audio.Size != plan.FinalAudio.SizeBytes {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_INVALID", errors.New("final audio integrity binding does not match the plan"))
        }
        if info, statErr := os.Stat(audio.Path); statErr != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Size() != audio.Size {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_INVALID", errors.New("final audio local file identity is invalid"))
        }
        jobID, err := safeOutputJobID(spec.JobID)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("INVALID_JOB_ID", err)
        }
        outputPath := filepath.Join(e.outputRoot, jobID+".mp4")
        if resolver := storageResolverFromExecutionContext(execCtx); resolver != nil {
            if placement, placeErr := resolver.Place(storage.ArtifactStaging, jobID+".mp4", estimateOutputBytesFromDuration(plan.DurationUS)); placeErr == nil {
                outputPath = placement.Path
            }
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(outputPath), 0o750); err != nil {
            return fail("OUTPUT_DIRECTORY", err)
        }
        wire, err := marshalCopyOnlyWire(plan, spec.JobID, outputPath, bindings)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID", err)
        }
        metrics, renderErr := e.runner.RenderCompiledPlanV2(ctx, wire, outputPath)
        if renderErr != nil {
            return fail(copyOnlyRenderErrorCode(renderErr), renderErr)
        }
        if err := e.verifyFinalMedia(ctx, outputPath, plan); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_OUTPUT_INVALID", err)
        }
        artifact, err := artifactFromFile("video/mp4", outputPath)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("FINAL_OUTPUT_INVALID", err)
        }
        raw := copyOnlyRawMetrics(plan, metrics, artifact)
        return executor.ExecutionResult{
            Status: "succeeded", Outputs: []executor.ArtifactRef{artifact}, RawMetrics: raw,
            Segments: projectSegments(metrics), DetailedPhases: projectDetailedPhases(metrics),
            StartedAt: started, CompletedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
        }, nil
    }
    
    type slicePoolMember struct {
        AssetID         string `json:"asset_id"`
        DriveFileID     string `json:"drive_file_id"`
        SizeBytes       int64  `json:"size_bytes"`
        DurationMS      int64  `json:"duration_ms"`
        StockPoolMember bool   `json:"stock_pool_member"`
    }
    
    func sliceRuntimePoolMembers(raw interface{}) []slicePoolMember {
        data, err := json.Marshal(raw)
        if err != nil {
            return nil
        }
        var members []slicePoolMember
        _ = json.Unmarshal(data, &members)
        return members
    }

        if plan.StockPool == nil || plan.StockPool.Selection != "shuffle" {
            return nil, errors.New("unsupported stock_pool selection")
        }
        members := sliceRuntimePoolMembers(spec.Payload["runtime_assets"])
        ordered := make([]slicePoolMember, 0, len(members))

    // registerCanonicalRenderExecutors installs the sole worker entry point for
    // compiled V2 video plans: packet-copy assembly.
    func registerCanonicalRenderExecutors(reg *executor.Registry, outputRoot string, runners []*pipeline.Runner) error {
        if len(runners) > 0 && runners[0] != nil {
            if err := reg.Register(executors.NewVideoAssembleCopy(runners[0], outputRoot)); err != nil {
                return err
            }
        }
        if err := reg.Register(executors.NewVideoAssembleSlice(outputRoot, ffmpegrunner.NewProcessRunner())); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        return nil
    }

    bool prepareSegment(CursorSegment& segment, std::string& error) {
        if (segment.validated) return true;
        if (segment.session == nullptr) {
            if (segment.registry == nullptr) {
                error = "cursor has no input session for " + segment.path;
                return false;
            }
            segment.session = segment.registry->resolve(segment.path, error);
            if (segment.session == nullptr) return false;
        }
        if (segment.stream_index < 0) {
            if (segment.media_type == AVMEDIA_TYPE_UNKNOWN) {
                error = "cursor has no media type for " + segment.path;
                return false;
            }
            segment.stream_index = segment.session->demuxer().firstStream(segment.media_type);
            if (segment.stream_index < 0) {
                error = "cursor input stream is unavailable: " + segment.path;
                return false;
            }
        }
        if (segment.transform_required) {
            error = "segment_execution_rejected: media transform required for " + segment.path;
            return false;
        }
        if (segment.legacy_required) {
            error = "segment_execution_rejected: legacy renderer required for " + segment.path;
            return false;
        }
        if (segment.media_type == AVMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO && !segment.normalized &&
            !segment.session->sourceWindowStartsOnKeyframe(
                segment.stream_index, segment.source_in_us, error)) {
            return false;
        }
        if (segment.has_target_signature) {
            const MediaSignature source = mediaSignatureFromStream(
                segment.session->demuxer().stream(segment.stream_index));
            std::string reason;
            if (!mediaSignaturesCompatible(source, segment.target_signature, &reason)) {
                error = "segment_execution_rejected: " + reason + " for " + segment.path;
                return false;
            }
        }
        segment.validated = true;
        return true;
    }
    
    bool fill(PendingPacket& pending, AVPacket& scratch, const CursorSegment& segment,
              TimestampState& state, AVPacket* lastVideo, bool* haveLast,
              PacketRewriteDecision* decision, std::string& error) {
        *decision = PacketRewriteDecision::BeforeWindow;
        pending.reset();
        const AVStream* input = segment.session->demuxer().stream(segment.stream_index);
        if (input == nullptr) {
            error = "cursor input stream is unavailable: " + segment.path;
            return false;
        }
        const int64_t sourceStart = validTimestamp(input->start_time) ? input->start_time : 0;
        int64_t sortDts = AV_NOPTS_VALUE;
        const PacketRewriteDecision rewrite_decision = rewritePacket(
            scratch, input, segment.output_stream, sourceStart,
            segment.source_in_us, segment.timeline_offset_us,
            segment.duration_us, state, sortDts);
        *decision = rewrite_decision;
        if (rewrite_decision != PacketRewriteDecision::Accepted) {
            return false;
        }
        if (lastVideo != nullptr && haveLast != nullptr) {
            av_packet_unref(lastVideo);
            if (av_packet_ref(lastVideo, &scratch) < 0) {
                error = "cursor failed to retain the last video packet";
                return false;
            }
            *haveLast = true;
        }
        av_packet_move_ref(&pending.packet, &scratch);
        pending.output_stream_index = segment.output_stream->index;
        pending.sort_dts = sortDts;
        pending.ready = true;
        return true;
    }

    bool VideoTimelineCursor::emitTailPacket(std::string& error) {
        if (!tail_extension_active_ || !have_last_video_packet_) return false;
        if (firstSegment.source_in_us >
            std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max() - firstSegment.source_duration_us) {
            return fail(result, "copy-only source video window overflows int64");
        }
        if (firstSegment.normalized && firstSegment.source_in_us != 0) {
            return fail(result, "copy-only normalized segment must start at source_in_us 0");
        }
        if (firstSegment.transform_required) {
            return fail(result, "segment_execution_rejected: media transform required for " +
                firstSegment.path.string());
        }
        if (firstSegment.legacy_required) {
            return fail(result, "segment_execution_rejected: legacy renderer required for " +
                firstSegment.path.string());
        }
        auto* firstSession = sessions.resolve(firstSegment.path, error);
        if (firstSession == nullptr) return fail(result, error);
        auto& firstDemuxer = firstSession->demuxer();
        const int firstVideoIndex = firstDemuxer.firstStream(AVMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO);
        if (firstVideoIndex < 0) {
            return fail(result, "video stream missing from " + firstSegment.path.string());
        }
        const AVStream* firstVideo = firstDemuxer.stream(firstVideoIndex);
        const MediaSignature firstVideoSignature = mediaSignatureFromStream(firstVideo);
        std::string compatibilityReason;
        if (requestedVideoTarget && !mediaSignaturesCompatible(
                firstVideoSignature, *requestedVideoTarget, &compatibilityReason)) {
            return fail(result, "segment_execution_rejected: copy-only segment execution rejected at " +
                firstSegment.path.string() + ": " + compatibilityReason);
        }
        videoTarget = firstVideoSignature;
        // SPS/PPS extradata is intentionally not part of the cross-segment
        // identity. Profile and level are decoder-advertised H.264 metadata and
        // may differ between otherwise packet-compatible assets produced by
        // different encoders. Keep the hard packet-safety checks (codec,
        // dimensions, pixel format and frame rate), but do not reject a later
        // segment solely because its profile/level differs from the first one.
        // The output stream remains initialized from the first concrete source.
        videoTarget->extradata.clear();
        videoTarget->profile = -1;
        videoTarget->level = -1;
        const bool firstKeyframeSafe = firstSegment.normalized ||
            firstSession->sourceWindowStartsOnKeyframe(
                firstVideoIndex, firstSegment.source_in_us, error);
        if (!firstKeyframeSafe) {
            return fail(result, "segment_execution_rejected: source window is not keyframe-safe for packet copy: " + error);
        }
        if (!initializeOutputStream(output, firstVideo, plan.streams.video, error)) {
            return fail(result, error);
        }
    
        int firstAudioIndex = -1;
        packet::InputSession* firstAudioSession = nullptr;
        if (firstSegment.include_audio) {
            firstAudioSession = firstSession;
            firstAudioIndex = firstDemuxer.firstStream(AVMEDIA_TYPE_AUDIO);
        } else {
            for (std::size_t index = 1; index < request.video_segments.size(); ++index) {
                if (!request.video_segments[index].include_audio) continue;
                firstAudioSession = sessions.resolve(request.video_segments[index].path, error);
                if (firstAudioSession != nullptr) {
                    firstAudioIndex = firstAudioSession->demuxer().firstStream(AVMEDIA_TYPE_AUDIO);
                }
                break;
            }
        }

    }
    
    func sliceRuntimePoolMembers(raw interface{}) []slicePoolMember {
        data, err := json.Marshal(raw)
        if err != nil {
            return nil
        }
        var members []slicePoolMember
        _ = json.Unmarshal(data, &members)
        return members
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) compileStockPoolPlan(_ context.Context, spec executor.TaskSpec, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, bindings runtimeassets.Bindings) (*contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, error) {
        if plan.StockPool == nil || plan.StockPool.Selection != "shuffle" {
            return nil, errors.New("unsupported stock_pool selection")
        }
        members := sliceRuntimePoolMembers(spec.Payload["runtime_assets"])
        ordered := make([]slicePoolMember, 0, len(members))
        for _, member := range members {
            binding, selected := bindings["stockpool:"+member.DriveFileID]
            if member.StockPoolMember && selected && binding.Verified && binding.Size > 0 && member.DurationMS > 0 {
                ordered = append(ordered, member)
            }
        }
        if len(ordered) == 0 {
            return nil, errors.New("stock_pool has no selected sources with Drive duration metadata")
        }
        sort.Slice(ordered, func(i, j int) bool { return ordered[i].DriveFileID < ordered[j].DriveFileID })
        seedBytes := sha256.Sum256([]byte(spec.JobID + ":" + plan.TimelineSHA256 + ":" + plan.StockPool.DriveFolderID))
        rng := rand.New(rand.NewSource(int64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(seedBytes[:8]))))
        rng.Shuffle(len(ordered), func(i, j int) { ordered[i], ordered[j] = ordered[j], ordered[i] })
        compiled := *plan
        compiled.StockPool = nil
        compiled.Assets = append([]contract.AssetRefV2(nil), plan.Assets...)
        compiled.VideoTracks = append([]contract.VideoTrackV2(nil), plan.VideoTracks...)
        for i := range compiled.VideoTracks {
            compiled.VideoTracks[i].Segments = append([]contract.VideoSegmentV2(nil), plan.VideoTracks[i].Segments...)
        }
        poolCursor := 0
        framesLeft := make(map[string]int64, len(ordered))
        for _, member := range ordered {
            assetID := "stockpool:" + member.DriveFileID
            framesLeft[assetID] = member.DurationMS * int64(plan.Output.FPSNum) / (1000 * int64(plan.Output.FPSDen))
        }
        for trackIndex := range compiled.VideoTracks {
            segments := make([]contract.VideoSegmentV2, 0, len(compiled.VideoTracks[trackIndex].Segments))
            for _, segment := range compiled.VideoTracks[trackIndex].Segments {
                if !segment.StockPoolSlot {
                    segments = append(segments, segment)
                    continue
                }
                remaining, timelineFrame := segment.FrameCount, segment.TimelineStartFrame
                part := 0
                for remaining > 0 {
                    for poolCursor < len(ordered) && framesLeft["stockpool:"+ordered[poolCursor].DriveFileID] <= 0 {
                        poolCursor++
                    }
                    if poolCursor >= len(ordered) {
                        return nil, errors.New("selected stock pool duration is shorter than its timeline slots")
                    }
                    member := ordered[poolCursor]
                    part++
                    baseAssetID := "stockpool:" + member.DriveFileID
                    binding := bindings[baseAssetID]
                    count := framesLeft[baseAssetID]
                    if count > remaining {
                        count = remaining
                    }
                    assetID := fmt.Sprintf("%s:timeline:%d", baseAssetID, timelineFrame)
                    durationUS := count * int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000 / int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
                    asset := contract.AssetRefV2{AssetID: assetID, AssetKey: member.DriveFileID, SourceKind: "drive", DriveFileID: member.DriveFileID, SHA256: binding.SHA256, SizeBytes: binding.Size, Kind: "video", MIME: "video/mp4", ProfileID: plan.Output.ProfileID, FrameCount: count, TimelineRevision: plan.TimelineRevision, TimelineSHA256: plan.TimelineSHA256, TimelineStartFrame: timelineFrame, FirstFrameKeyframe: true, ClosedGOP: true, DurationUS: durationUS, Width: plan.Output.Width, Height: plan.Output.Height}
                    compiled.Assets = append(compiled.Assets, asset)
                    bindings[assetID] = binding
                    segments = append(segments, contract.VideoSegmentV2{SegmentID: fmt.Sprintf("%s-source-%03d", segment.SegmentID, part), AssetID: assetID, SHA256: asset.SHA256, TimelineStartFrame: timelineFrame, FrameCount: count, SourceDurationUS: durationUS})
                    framesLeft[baseAssetID] -= count
                    remaining -= count
                    timelineFrame += count
                    if framesLeft[assetID] == 0 {
                        poolCursor++
                    }
                }
            }
            compiled.VideoTracks[trackIndex].Segments = segments
        }
        return &compiled, nil
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) verifyFinalMedia(ctx context.Context, outputPath string, plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) error {
        probe, err := e.prober.ProbeMediaDetails(ctx, outputPath)
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("probe assembled output: %w", err)
        }
        if !probe.HasVideo || !probe.HasAudio || probe.VideoCodec != "h264" || probe.AudioCodec != "aac" || probe.Width != plan.Output.Width || probe.Height != plan.Output.Height {
            return fmt.Errorf("assembled output streams/profile invalid: video=%t/%s audio=%t/%s size=%dx%d want=h264/aac %dx%d", probe.HasVideo, probe.VideoCodec, probe.HasAudio, probe.AudioCodec, probe.Width, probe.Height, plan.Output.Width, plan.Output.Height)
        }
        if probe.VideoFrameCount != slicePlanFrameCount(plan) {
            return fmt.Errorf("assembled output has %d frames, plan requires %d; refusing to publish", probe.VideoFrameCount, slicePlanFrameCount(plan))
        }
        wantDuration := float64(plan.DurationUS) / 1_000_000
        frameTolerance := float64(plan.Output.FPSDen)/float64(plan.Output.FPSNum) + 0.1
        if probe.DurationSec <= 0 || probe.DurationSec-wantDuration > frameTolerance || wantDuration-probe.DurationSec > frameTolerance {
            return fmt.Errorf("assembled output duration %.3fs does not match plan %.3fs (tolerance %.3fs)", probe.DurationSec, wantDuration, frameTolerance)
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    func slicePlanFrameCount(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) int64 {
        var frames int64
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            frames += segment.FrameCount
        }
        return frames
    }

    // copyOnlyRenderErrorCode classifies a native copy-only render failure into
    // a stable worker-facing error code. The native engine already fails closed
    // for every packet-mux rejection (it never re-encodes), but it reports them
    // all under a generic packet_mux_failed code; the worker re-classifies the
    // keyframe-safety rejection so operators can distinguish "the cut is not
    // packet-copy safe" from an unrelated mux failure without losing the exact
    // engine reason.
    func copyOnlyRenderErrorCode(err error) string {
        if err == nil {
            return "PACKET_COPY_FAILED"
        }
        lower := strings.ToLower(err.Error())
        if strings.Contains(lower, "must start on an exact video keyframe") ||
            strings.Contains(lower, "not keyframe-safe for packet copy") {
            return "COPY_ONLY_NOT_KEYFRAME_SAFE"
        }
        return "PACKET_COPY_FAILED"
    }
    
    func validateCopyOnlyPlan(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) error {
        if plan == nil {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.copy.v1: plan is nil")
        }
        profile, err := validateCopyOnlyProfile(plan)
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) == 0 {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.copy.v1: exactly one non-empty video track is required")
        }
        assets := make(map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, len(plan.Assets))
        for _, asset := range plan.Assets {
            assets[asset.AssetID] = asset
        }
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            if err := validateCopyOnlySegment(plan, profile, assets, segment); err != nil {
                return err
            }
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    // validateCopyOnlyProfile resolves the output's canonical profile and checks
    // every stream-identity field against it. The packet-copy path can only accept
    // streams produced under an admitted profile.
    func validateCopyOnlyProfile(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) (contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1, error) {
        if plan.Output.ProfileID == "" {
            return contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: output.profile_id is required", ErrCopyOnlyProfileMismatch)
        }
        profile, err := contract.KnownCanonicalVideoProfileV1(plan.Output.ProfileID)
        if err != nil {
            return contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrCopyOnlyProfileMismatch, err)
        }
        if err := profile.MatchesOutput(plan.Output); err != nil {
            return contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrCopyOnlyProfileMismatch, err)
        }
        if plan.Output.CodecProfile != profile.CodecProfile || plan.Output.CodecLevel != profile.CodecLevel || plan.Output.GOPSize != profile.GOPSize || plan.Output.BFrames != profile.BFrames || plan.Output.TimeBaseNum != profile.TimeBaseNum || plan.Output.TimeBaseDen != profile.TimeBaseDen || !plan.Output.ClosedGOP {
            return contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: output encoder/time-base fields do not match profile %q", ErrCopyOnlyProfileMismatch, profile.ProfileID)
        }
        return profile, nil
    }
    
    // validateCopyOnlySegment certifies one prepared video fragment against its
    // declared asset manifest: the reference must exist, be a prepared-video kind,
    // and match the plan's timeline identity and frame bounds exactly.
    func validateCopyOnlySegment(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, profile contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1, assets map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, segment contract.VideoSegmentV2) error {
        asset, ok := assets[segment.AssetID]
        if !ok || (asset.Kind != "video" && asset.Kind != "prepared_video_fragment") {
            return fmt.Errorf("%w: segment %q does not reference a prepared video asset", ErrCopyOnlyCertification, segment.SegmentID)
        }
        if asset.SHA256 != segment.SHA256 || asset.ProfileID != profile.StreamProfile() || asset.FrameCount != segment.FrameCount || asset.TimelineRevision != plan.TimelineRevision || asset.TimelineSHA256 != plan.TimelineSHA256 || asset.TimelineStartFrame != segment.TimelineStartFrame || asset.DurationUS != segment.SourceDurationUS || !asset.FirstFrameKeyframe || !asset.ClosedGOP || segment.SourceInUS != 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("%w: segment %q manifest binding is not exact", ErrCopyOnlyCertification, segment.SegmentID)
        }
        return nil
    }

                : item.duration_seconds;
            const int progress = 10 + static_cast<int>(
                (static_cast<double>(i + 1) / plan.timeline.size()) * 55.0);
            reportProgress(progress, "staging_copy_inputs");
            reportDetailedProgress(
                last_progress_, static_cast<int>(i + 1), static_cast<int>(plan.timeline.size()),
                static_cast<int>(i + 1), static_cast<int>(plan.timeline.size()),
                "staging_copy_inputs", 0, 0, 0,
                std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
                    std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - renderStart).count(), true);
        }

    # ============================================================================
    # Velox Worker — Self-sufficient multistage build: cpp-builder → go-builder → slim runtime.
    # ============================================================================
    # PR-3: the worker Dockerfile is now buildable from a fresh checkout with
    # nothing more than `docker build` — no pre-build `make agent` step required.
    # Both the C++ engine and the Go worker-agent binary are produced during
    # the image build, inside their dedicated builder stages.
    #
    # Build context: <repo-root>
    #   The build context is now the repo root (NOT RemoteCodex/, NOT
    #   native/worker-agent-go/) because worker-agent-go's go.mod declares
    #     replace velox-shared v0.0.0 => ../../../shared
    #   which resolves to <repo-root>/shared only when the build module sits
    #   at <repo-root>/RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/ inside the builder's
    #   filesystem. The go.work workspace-level replace is NOT taken into
    #   account by `go build` from inside a go-builder stage because the
    #   builder has no ambient go.work lookup path.
    #
    # The go-builder stage delegates the worker-agent build to the project's
    # own Makefile (`make BIN_DIR=/out agent evict benchmark-tools`) so that:
    #   1. VERSION.txt is enforced (Makefile FATALs when missing — the
    #      Dockerfile would otherwise silently fall back to "dev").
    #   2. Reproducible Builds BUILD_TIME chain (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH → git
    #      commit timestamp → "unknown") lives in one place (Makefile).
    #   3. LDFLAGS pattern (-X main.Version=… -X main.BuildTime=…) is the
    #      same as on host builds — no drift risk.
    # No outer build-args are required; the Makefile is the single source of
    # truth for VERSION + BUILD_TIME resolution.
    #
    # Rendered builts:
    #   `docker build -f RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/Dockerfile .`
    # produces the same image as the legacy flow did (pre-Docker `make agent`
    # + bin/ copy), but without the pre-step requirement.
    #
    # Image layer order is intentional for cache locality:
    #   * OS + runtime deps (stage 3): slowest-changing layer.
    #   * C++ engine binary (stage-3 COPY --from=cpp-builder): medium-frequency.
    #   * Go worker binary (stage-3 COPY --from=go-builder): most frequent layer,
    #     applied AFTER the C++ engine COPY so a Go-only diff does NOT invalidate
    #     the C++ engine build cache.
    #   * useradd + USER + HEALTHCHECK + ENTRYPOINT: below all binary COPYs so
    #     they are not invalidated by binary changes.
    #
    # Runtime identity: container runs as the unprivileged `velox` user with
    # a deterministic UID/GID of 10001 (configurable via the VELOX_UID /
    # VELOX_GID ARGs at build time). Operators do NOT need a blanket
    # `chown -R velox /opt/velox` — only the writable subtrees must be owned
    # by this UID (cache, assets_cache, runtime_dir). These are configured by
    # DataServer/data/ansible/playbooks/tasks/systemd_setup.yml.
    
    # ─── Stage 1: C++ engine builder ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Keep one explicit base reference for both builder and runtime. Release
    # automation may override it with a fully pinned @sha256 digest; using the
    # same reference in both stages prevents an ABI drift between stages.
    ARG VELOX_DEBIAN_BASE=debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:88200866dfff7ea7f5cbcb6ec7c8a701889efe6fe859fe64d6990e4b07ea4171
    ARG SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0
    FROM ${VELOX_DEBIAN_BASE} AS cpp-builder
    ARG SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
    ENV SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}
    
    ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
    
    # Build deps only (cmake, g++, build-essential). NOT copied to runtime.
    # Pin the Debian package set as well as the base image. The pinned
    # bookworm snapshot currently resolves these exact versions; an unexpected
    # repository update must fail the build instead of silently changing the
    # compiler/FFmpeg ABI and engine hash.
    ARG BUILD_ESSENTIAL_VERSION=12.9
    ARG CMAKE_VERSION=3.25.1-1
    ARG GXX_VERSION=4:12.2.0-3
    ARG PKG_CONFIG_VERSION=1.8.1-1
    ARG CA_CERTIFICATES_VERSION=20230311+deb12u1
    ARG FFMPEG_VERSION=7:5.1.9-0+deb12u1
    ARG PROCPS_VERSION=2:4.0.2-3
    ARG LIBC_BIN_VERSION=2.36-9+deb12u14
    RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt,sharing=locked \
        --mount=type=cache,target=/var/lib/apt,sharing=locked \
        apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            build-essential=${BUILD_ESSENTIAL_VERSION} \
            cmake=${CMAKE_VERSION} \
            g++=${GXX_VERSION} \
            ccache \
            pkg-config=${PKG_CONFIG_VERSION} \
            ca-certificates=${CA_CERTIFICATES_VERSION} \
            ffmpeg=${FFMPEG_VERSION} \
            libavformat-dev=${FFMPEG_VERSION} \
            libavcodec-dev=${FFMPEG_VERSION} \
            libavutil-dev=${FFMPEG_VERSION} \
            libswscale-dev=${FFMPEG_VERSION} \
            procps=${PROCPS_VERSION} \
            libc-bin=${LIBC_BIN_VERSION} \
        && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    
    # Build context is the repo root — paths MUST reflect that layout.
    COPY RemoteCodex/scripts/build-video-engine.sh /usr/local/bin/build-video-engine.sh
    COPY RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp /app/native/video-engine-cpp
    
    # Compile and test the engine into /usr/local/bin/velox_video_engine.
    # The builder also writes the canonical binary hash consumed by the runtime
    # verification gate; no host-built or docker-copied binary is accepted.
    RUN --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-cpp-ccache,target=/root/.ccache,sharing=locked \
        --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-cpp-build,target=/tmp/velox-video-engine-build,sharing=locked \
        ccache -z 2>/dev/null || true; \
        /usr/local/bin/build-video-engine.sh && \
        test -x /usr/local/bin/velox_video_engine && \
        test -s /usr/local/share/velox/video-engine.sha256
    
    
    # ─── Stage 2: Go worker-builder ────────────────────────────────────────────
    # PR-3: this stage replaces the pre-built bin/velox-worker-agent contract.
    # It is independent of the C++ engine build, so BuildKit can execute stages
    # 1 and 2 in parallel when cache permits. The velox-shared replace CLI
    # directive in worker-agent-go/go.mod drives the resolution to the in-tree
    # shared/ tree; no ambient go.work lookup is required.
    #
    # The actual `go build` is delegated to the project's Makefile so the
    # LDFLAGS pattern + VERSION.txt enforcement + Reproducible Builds chain
    # are uniformly governed by Makefile.source-of-truth — NOT duplicated in
    # Dockerfile. See RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/Makefile for the
    # contract (VERSION_FILE, BUILD_TIME fallback, LDFLAGS).
    FROM golang:1.25.8-bookworm@sha256:4557cf171e3cdf5053a298d5171b1a5f5734d920260c25f22c79e94760eb2084 AS go-builder
    
    ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
    
    # golang:1.25.8-bookworm does NOT ship `make`. PR-3 requires it because
    # the go-builder delegates to the host Makefile. Keep the dep set
    # minimal: only what's needed to run the Makefile's agent and evict targets.
    RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt,sharing=locked \
        --mount=type=cache,target=/var/lib/apt,sharing=locked \
        apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            make \
            ca-certificates \
        && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    
    # Workspace layout inside the builder. /src is a synthetic mount-anchor;
    # `WORKDIR` is a per-stage baseline so relative paths in `go build` (e.g.
    # the `replace ../../../shared` directive) resolve correctly.
    WORKDIR /src
    
    # Layer-ordering rationale:
    #   * VERSION.txt first (slowest-changing; FATAL at Makefile parse time
    #     when missing; changes invalidate the agent build AND the published
    #     bundle-version assertion).
    #   * shared/ next (slowest-changing, large; the `replace velox-shared`
    #     points here).
    #   * go.mod + go.sum third (cache key for go mod download).
    #   * source code last (most frequent).
    # This ordering lets a Go-only diff avoid re-downloading dependencies.
    COPY VERSION.txt /src/VERSION.txt
    COPY shared/go.mod shared/go.sum /src/shared/
    COPY RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/go.mod \
         RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/go.sum \
         /src/RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/
    
    # `go mod download` reads go.mod + go.sum only — no source files yet.
    # Backing the module cache with BuildKit cache mount so subsequent builds
    # reuse the same /go/pkg/mod layers (Huge speedup once the dep graph lands).
    WORKDIR /src/RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go
    RUN --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-go-mod,target=/go/pkg/mod,sharing=locked \
        go mod download
    
    # Now copy the full module. The Makefile's `make agent evict` targets then
    # take over from BIN_DIR=/out: `agent` bakes main.Version + main.BuildTime
    # via the Makefile's LDFLAGS contract (VERSION.txt + Reproducible-Builds
    # chain), while `evict` builds the cache-admin CLI without version stamping.
    COPY RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/ /src/RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/
    COPY shared/ /src/shared/
    
    # The Makefile is the single source of truth for the LDFLAGS pattern,
    # so the image's main.Version + main.BuildTime match the host `make agent`
    # output byte-for-byte (modulo /go/pkg/mod cache contents). /out is then
    # COPYed in stage 3.
    RUN --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-go-mod,target=/go/pkg/mod,sharing=locked \
        --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-go-build,target=/root/.cache/go-build,sharing=locked \
        make BIN_DIR=/out agent evict benchmark-tools && \
        test -x /out/velox-worker-agent && \
        test -x /out/velox-cache-evict && \
        test -x /out/velox-benchmark && \
        test -x /out/velox-fixture-gen && \
        test -x /out/velox-fixture-gate
    
    
    # ─── Stage 3: runtime — NO compilers, NO cmake, NO binutils ─────────────────
    FROM ${VELOX_DEBIAN_BASE}
    ARG SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
    ENV SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}
    
    # Pinned non-root identity. Operators chown 10001:10001 on the writable
    # host bind-mounts (cache, assets_cache, runtime_dir) so files written
    # by the container remain owned by this UID.
    ARG VELOX_UID=10001
    ARG VELOX_GID=10001
    
    ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
    ENV VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_CPP_BIN=/usr/local/bin/velox_video_engine
    ENV VELOX_HEALTH_PORT=8081
    
    WORKDIR /app
    
    # The bootstrap gate resolves the self-render baseline relative to the
    scripts/ops/dev-master.sh:18:#   scripts/ops/dev-master.sh build-image [tag]     # docker build local image (default tag velox-server:local)

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    
    ENGINE_SRC="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_SRC:-}"
    OUT_BIN="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_OUT:-/usr/local/bin/velox_video_engine}"
    BUILD_DIR="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_BUILD_DIR:-/tmp/velox-video-engine-build}"
    BUILD_JOBS="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_BUILD_JOBS:-2}"
    METADATA_DIR="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_METADATA_DIR:-/usr/local/share/velox}"
    ENGINE_SHA_FILE="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_SHA_FILE:-${METADATA_DIR}/video-engine.sha256}"
    
    echo "== Velox C++ engine build =="
    echo "Source: $ENGINE_SRC"
    echo "Output: $OUT_BIN"
    echo "Build dir: $BUILD_DIR"
    
    resolve_engine_source() {
      local candidate
      for candidate in \
        "${ENGINE_SRC}" \
        /app/native/video-engine-cpp \
        /app/RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp \
        /opt/velox/current/RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp
      do
        [ -n "$candidate" ] || continue
        if [ -d "$candidate" ]; then
          printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
          return 0
        fi
      done
      return 1
    }
    
    if [ -z "$ENGINE_SRC" ]; then
      ENGINE_SRC="$(resolve_engine_source || true)"
    fi
    
    if [ -z "$ENGINE_SRC" ] || [ ! -d "$ENGINE_SRC" ]; then
      echo "ERROR: C++ engine source directory not found. Tried /app/native/video-engine-cpp, /app/RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp and /opt/velox/current/RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp" >&2
      exit 10
    fi
    
    echo "Resolved source: $ENGINE_SRC"
    
    # Clean stale artifacts from bundle (never build inside the synced dir)
    rm -rf \
        "$ENGINE_SRC/build" \
        "$ENGINE_SRC/CMakeFiles" \
        "$ENGINE_SRC/CMakeCache.txt" \
        "$ENGINE_SRC/cmake_install.cmake"
    
    # Keep the out-of-source build directory intact when it is backed by a
    # BuildKit cache mount. CMake's dependency tracking plus ccache can then
    # reuse unchanged objects between image builds; deleting this directory here
    # turned the cache mount into an expensive no-op.
    mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
    
    if [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/CMakeLists.txt" ]; then
      echo "Detected CMake project"
    
      # Optional in-process LibAV backend (MediaProbe + packet mux). The CMake
      # default is OFF; the canonical builder opts in whenever the pinned dev
      # libraries are present so the produced engine keeps the zero-spawn probe
      # and copy-only packet pipeline. VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV overrides the
      # pkg-config detection (set to OFF for a conservative ffprobe-only build).
      if [ -z "${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV:-}" ]; then
        if pkg-config --exists libavformat libavcodec libavutil 2>/dev/null; then
          VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV=ON
        else
          VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV=OFF
        fi
      fi
      echo "LibAV in-process backend: $VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV"
    
      cmake \
          -S "$ENGINE_SRC" \
          -B "$BUILD_DIR" \
          -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache \
          -DVELOX_ENABLE_LIBAV="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV}"
    
      cmake --build "$BUILD_DIR" --parallel "$BUILD_JOBS"
      ctest --test-dir "$BUILD_DIR" --output-on-failure
    
      if [ -f "$BUILD_DIR/velox_video_engine" ]; then
        install -m 0755 "$BUILD_DIR/velox_video_engine" "$OUT_BIN"
      elif [ -f "$BUILD_DIR/video_engine" ]; then
        install -m 0755 "$BUILD_DIR/video_engine" "$OUT_BIN"
      else
        echo "ERROR: CMake build completed but engine binary was not found" >&2
        find "$BUILD_DIR" -maxdepth 3 -type f -perm -111 -print
        exit 11
      fi
    
    elif [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/Makefile" ] || [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/makefile" ]; then
      echo "Detected Makefile project"
      make -C "$ENGINE_SRC" CC="ccache cc" CXX="ccache c++" -j"$BUILD_JOBS"
    
      if [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/velox_video_engine" ]; then
        install -m 0755 "$ENGINE_SRC/velox_video_engine" "$OUT_BIN"
      elif [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/video_engine" ]; then
        install -m 0755 "$ENGINE_SRC/video_engine" "$OUT_BIN"
      else
        echo "ERROR: Make build completed but engine binary was not found" >&2
        find "$ENGINE_SRC" -maxdepth 3 -type f -perm -111 -print
        exit 12
      fi
    
    else
      echo "ERROR: no CMakeLists.txt or Makefile found in $ENGINE_SRC" >&2
      exit 13
    fi
    
    echo "== Built binary =="
    ls -lh "$OUT_BIN"
    file "$OUT_BIN" || true
    
    # Validate the binary against the same builder image that produced it. This
    # fails the image build before the artifact can cross into the runtime stage.
    # The runtime stage repeats this check through worker-entrypoint.sh.
    LDD_OUTPUT="$(ldd "$OUT_BIN" 2>&1 || true)"
    printf '%s\n' "$LDD_OUTPUT"
    if printf '%s\n' "$LDD_OUTPUT" | grep -q 'not found'; then
      echo "ERROR: unresolved shared dependencies detected for $OUT_BIN" >&2
      exit 14
    fi
    
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ENGINE_SHA_FILE")"
    sha256sum "$OUT_BIN" > "$ENGINE_SHA_FILE"
    echo "Engine SHA-256: $(awk '{print $1}' "$ENGINE_SHA_FILE")"
    echo "Engine metadata: $ENGINE_SHA_FILE"
    # verification gate; no host-built or docker-copied binary is accepted.
    RUN --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-cpp-ccache,target=/root/.ccache,sharing=locked \
        --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-cpp-build,target=/tmp/velox-video-engine-build,sharing=locked \
        ccache -z 2>/dev/null || true; \
        /usr/local/bin/build-video-engine.sh && \
        test -x /usr/local/bin/velox_video_engine && \
        test -s /usr/local/share/velox/video-engine.sha256
    
    
    # ─── Stage 2: Go worker-builder ────────────────────────────────────────────
    # PR-3: this stage replaces the pre-built bin/velox-worker-agent contract.
    # It is independent of the C++ engine build, so BuildKit can execute stages
    # 1 and 2 in parallel when cache permits. The velox-shared replace CLI
    # directive in worker-agent-go/go.mod drives the resolution to the in-tree
    # shared/ tree; no ambient go.work lookup is required.
    #
    # The actual `go build` is delegated to the project's Makefile so the
    # LDFLAGS pattern + VERSION.txt enforcement + Reproducible Builds chain
    # are uniformly governed by Makefile.source-of-truth — NOT duplicated in
    # Dockerfile. See RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/Makefile for the
    # contract (VERSION_FILE, BUILD_TIME fallback, LDFLAGS).
    FROM golang:1.25.8-bookworm@sha256:4557cf171e3cdf5053a298d5171b1a5f5734d920260c25f22c79e94760eb2084 AS go-builder
    
    ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
    
    # golang:1.25.8-bookworm does NOT ship `make`. PR-3 requires it because
    # the go-builder delegates to the host Makefile. Keep the dep set
    # minimal: only what's needed to run the Makefile's agent and evict targets.
    RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt,sharing=locked \
        --mount=type=cache,target=/var/lib/apt,sharing=locked \
        apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            make \
            ca-certificates \
        && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    
    # Workspace layout inside the builder. /src is a synthetic mount-anchor;
    # `WORKDIR` is a per-stage baseline so relative paths in `go build` (e.g.
    # the `replace ../../../shared` directive) resolve correctly.
    WORKDIR /src
    
    # Layer-ordering rationale:
    #   * VERSION.txt first (slowest-changing; FATAL at Makefile parse time
    #     when missing; changes invalidate the agent build AND the published
    #     bundle-version assertion).
    #   * shared/ next (slowest-changing, large; the `replace velox-shared`
    #     points here).
    #   * go.mod + go.sum third (cache key for go mod download).
    #   * source code last (most frequent).
    # This ordering lets a Go-only diff avoid re-downloading dependencies.
    COPY VERSION.txt /src/VERSION.txt
    COPY shared/go.mod shared/go.sum /src/shared/
    COPY RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/go.mod \
         RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/go.sum \
         /src/RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/
    
    # `go mod download` reads go.mod + go.sum only — no source files yet.
    # Backing the module cache with BuildKit cache mount so subsequent builds
    # reuse the same /go/pkg/mod layers (Huge speedup once the dep graph lands).
    WORKDIR /src/RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go
    RUN --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-go-mod,target=/go/pkg/mod,sharing=locked \
        go mod download
    
    # Now copy the full module. The Makefile's `make agent evict` targets then
    # take over from BIN_DIR=/out: `agent` bakes main.Version + main.BuildTime
    # via the Makefile's LDFLAGS contract (VERSION.txt + Reproducible-Builds
    # chain), while `evict` builds the cache-admin CLI without version stamping.
    COPY RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/ /src/RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/
    COPY shared/ /src/shared/
    
    # The Makefile is the single source of truth for the LDFLAGS pattern,
    # so the image's main.Version + main.BuildTime match the host `make agent`
    # output byte-for-byte (modulo /go/pkg/mod cache contents). /out is then
    # COPYed in stage 3.
    RUN --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-go-mod,target=/go/pkg/mod,sharing=locked \
        --mount=type=cache,id=velox-worker-go-build,target=/root/.cache/go-build,sharing=locked \
        make BIN_DIR=/out agent evict benchmark-tools && \
        test -x /out/velox-worker-agent && \
        test -x /out/velox-cache-evict && \
        test -x /out/velox-benchmark && \
        test -x /out/velox-fixture-gen && \
        test -x /out/velox-fixture-gate

     M RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp/src/core/render_engine_packet.cpp

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # dev-master.sh — fast local loop for Velox master development.
    #
    # Why this exists: a full CI release (race matrix + image build + sign)
    # takes 15-30+ minutes from push to a deployable image. Most intake /
    # validation / projection changes can be verified in seconds locally:
    #   1. go build + go test on touched packages (seconds)
    #   2. this script: run the REAL master binary on scratch ports/DB (1-2 min)
    #   3. local docker image (first build slow, then cached)
    #   4. CI release image (production only)
    # See docs/DEV-LOOP.md for the tier guide with measured times.
    #
    # Usage:
    #   scripts/ops/dev-master.sh build                 # compile ./velox-server-dev (repo root/DataServer)
    #   scripts/ops/dev-master.sh run                   # build + serve dev master on :18000 (scratch DB)
    #   scripts/ops/dev-master.sh dry-run <payload.json> [endpoint] [master]
    #                                                   # POST payload to ?dry_run=true, print summary+warnings
    #   scripts/ops/dev-master.sh build-image [tag]     # docker build local image (default tag velox-server:local)
    #   scripts/ops/dev-master.sh push-image [tag]      # build + push ghcr.io/<owner>/velox-server:<tag>
    #
    # The dev master NEVER touches production: fresh scratch DB under
    # $DEV_DIR, HTTP :18000, gRPC :19000, fixed dev admin token printed at boot.
    set -euo pipefail
    
    REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
    DEV_DIR="${VELOX_DEV_DIR:-/tmp/velox-dev-master}"
    # NOTE: :18000/:18200 on this host are SSH tunnels to the OVH production
    # master (see the -L flags on the pierone@51.91.11.36 ssh process) — the
    # dev master defaults to :18001/:19001 to stay clear of them AND of the
    # local production container (:8000/:9000).
    DEV_HTTP_PORT="${VELOX_DEV_HTTP_PORT:-18001}"
    DEV_GRPC_PORT="${VELOX_DEV_GRPC_PORT:-19001}"
    DEV_ADMIN_TOKEN="velox-dev-local-token"
    BIN="$REPO_ROOT/DataServer/velox-server-dev"
    
    cmd_build() {
      echo "==> go build ./cmd/server -> $BIN"
      (cd "$REPO_ROOT/DataServer" && go build -o "$BIN" ./cmd/server)
      echo "built: $(du -h "$BIN" | cut -f1)"
    }
    
    cmd_run() {
      cmd_build
      mkdir -p "$DEV_DIR/data"
      # The boot data-layer audit requires the DB file to exist; an empty
      # file is fine (migrations initialize the schema). Production data is
      # never copied here.
      touch "$DEV_DIR/data/velox.db"
      echo "==> dev master: http=:${DEV_HTTP_PORT} grpc=:${DEV_GRPC_PORT} db=$DEV_DIR/data/velox.db"
      echo "    admin token: $DEV_ADMIN_TOKEN (dev only, never production)"

    // issueM2MKeyRequest is the JSON body for POST /api/v1/admin/m2m/keys.
    //
    // All fields other than ClientID are optional. Defaults applied at
    // issue time:
    //   - Scopes:             ["jobs.submit"]
    //   - Description:        ""
    //   - RateLimitRPS:       0 → cfg.M2M.DefaultRPS at enforcement
    //   - RateLimitBurst:     0 → cfg.M2M.DefaultBurst
    //   - QuotaMaxScenes:     0 → cfg.M2M.MaxScenesPerRequest
    //   - QuotaMaxTotalS:     0 → cfg.M2M.MaxTotalDurationSecondsPerRequest
    type issueM2MKeyRequest struct {
        ClientID          string   `json:"client_id"`
        Description       string   `json:"description"`
        Scopes            []string `json:"scopes"`
        RateLimitRPS      *int     `json:"rate_limit_rps"`
        RateLimitBurst    *int     `json:"rate_limit_burst"`
        QuotaMaxScenes    *int     `json:"quota_max_scenes"`
        QuotaMaxTotalSecs *float64 `json:"quota_max_total_secs"`
    }
    
    // issueM2MKeyResponse is the JSON returned by POST on success.
    // PlaintextSecret is the ONLY time the plaintext exists outside the
    // admin's clipboard; the row in `m2m_api_keys` contains only its
    // SHA-256 hash.
    type issueM2MKeyResponse struct {
        ClientID        string    `json:"client_id"`
        PlaintextSecret string    `json:"plaintext_secret"` // returned ONCE
        SecretHash      string    `json:"secret_hash"`
        Scopes          []string  `json:"scopes"`
        IsActive        bool      `json:"is_active"`
        Description     string    `json:"description"`
        RateLimitRPS    *int      `json:"rate_limit_rps"`
        RateLimitBurst  *int      `json:"rate_limit_burst"`
        QuotaMaxScenes  *int      `json:"quota_max_scenes"`
        QuotaMaxTotalS  *float64  `json:"quota_max_total_secs"`
        CreatedAt       time.Time `json:"created_at"`
    }

    package executors

    type sliceFFmpegRunner struct {
        args        [][]string
        concatInput string
    }
    
    func (r *sliceFFmpegRunner) Run(_ context.Context, req ffmpegrunner.FFmpegRequest) (ffmpegrunner.FFmpegResult, error) {
        r.args = append(r.args, append([]string(nil), req.Args...))
        for i := 0; i+1 < len(req.Args); i++ {
            if req.Args[i] == "-i" && strings.HasSuffix(req.Args[i+1], "segments.ffconcat") {
                data, err := os.ReadFile(req.Args[i+1])
                if err != nil {
                    return ffmpegrunner.FFmpegResult{}, err
                }
                r.concatInput = string(data)
            }
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(req.Args[len(req.Args)-1], []byte("remote-render"), 0o640); err != nil {
            return ffmpegrunner.FFmpegResult{}, err
        }
        return ffmpegrunner.FFmpegResult{ProcessWallMS: 12}, nil
    }
    
    type sliceMediaProbeStub struct{}
    
    func (sliceMediaProbeStub) ProbeMediaDetails(_ context.Context, path string) (publisher.MediaProbe, error) {
        if strings.HasSuffix(path, "stock.mp4") {
            return publisher.MediaProbe{HasVideo: true, VideoCodec: "h264", VideoCodecTag: "avc1", VideoProfile: "High", VideoLevel: 40, VideoPixelFormat: "yuv420p", VideoFPSNum: 24, VideoFPSDen: 1, VideoTimeBaseNum: 1, VideoTimeBaseDen: 90000, VideoExtradataHash: "same-sps", VideoFrameCount: 480, DurationSec: 20, Width: 1920, Height: 1080}, nil
        }
        return publisher.MediaProbe{HasVideo: true, HasAudio: true, VideoCodec: "h264", AudioCodec: "aac", VideoProfile: "High", VideoLevel: 40, VideoPixelFormat: "yuv420p", VideoFPSNum: 24, VideoFPSDen: 1, VideoFrameCount: 24, DurationSec: 1, Width: 1920, Height: 1080}, nil
    }
    
    func driveSlicePlan() *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2 {
        const timelineHash = "cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc"
        return &contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2{
            PlanVersion: 2, TimelineRevision: 7, TimelineSHA256: timelineHash, DurationUS: 1_000_000,
            Output: contract.OutputContractV2{
                Container: "mp4", VideoCodec: "h264", Width: 1920, Height: 1080,
                FPSNum: 24, FPSDen: 1, PixelFormat: "yuv420p", ProfileID: contract.CanonicalVideoProfileIDV1,
                CodecProfile: "high", CodecLevel: "4.0", GOPSize: 48, BFrames: 0,
                ClosedGOP: true, TimeBaseNum: 1, TimeBaseDen: 90000,
            },
            FinalAudio:  contract.FinalAudioV2{Mode: contract.AudioModeFinalAudioCopy, AssetID: "audio", SHA256: copyOnlySHA([]byte("audio")), SizeBytes: 5, Codec: "aac", SampleRateHz: 48000, Channels: 2, DurationUS: 1_000_000, TimelineRevision: 7, TimelineSHA256: timelineHash},
            VideoTracks: []contract.VideoTrackV2{{TrackID: "main", Segments: []contract.VideoSegmentV2{{SegmentID: "segment-0003", AssetID: "drive:stock-01", TimelineStartFrame: 0, FrameCount: 24, SourceInUS: 0, SourceDurationUS: 1_000_000}}}},
            Assets: []contract.AssetRefV2{
                {AssetID: "drive:stock-01", AssetKey: "drive:stock-01", SourceKind: "drive", DriveFileID: "stock-01", SHA256: strings.Repeat("b", 64), SizeBytes: 5, Kind: "video", DurationUS: 20_000_000, Width: 1920, Height: 1080, ProfileID: contract.CanonicalVideoProfileIDV1, FrameCount: 480, FirstFrameKeyframe: true, ClosedGOP: true},
                {AssetID: "audio", SHA256: copyOnlySHA([]byte("audio")), SizeBytes: 5, Kind: "final_audio", DurationUS: 1_000_000},
            },
        }
    }
    
    func TestVideoAssembleSlice_CopiesDriveSourceWindowsWithoutReencoding(t *testing.T) {
        plan := driveSlicePlan()
        canonical, err := plan.CanonicalJSON()
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        videoPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "stock.mp4")
        audioPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "audio.m4a")
        if err := os.WriteFile(videoPath, []byte("stock"), 0o640); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(audioPath, []byte("audio"), 0o640); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        runner := &sliceFFmpegRunner{}
        exec := &videoAssembleSliceExecutor{runner: runner, prober: sliceMediaProbeStub{}, outputRoot: t.TempDir()}
        spec := executorTaskSpec(VideoAssembleSliceID, "job-drive-slice", canonical, plan)
        result, err := exec.Execute(runtimeassets.WithBindings(context.Background(), runtimeassets.Bindings{
            "drive:stock-01": {AssetID: "drive:stock-01", Path: videoPath, SHA256: strings.Repeat("b", 64), Size: 5, Verified: true},
            "audio":          {AssetID: "audio", Path: audioPath, SHA256: copyOnlySHA([]byte("audio")), Size: 5, Verified: true},
        }), nil, spec)
        if err != nil || result.Status != "succeeded" {
            t.Fatalf("slice execution result=%+v err=%v", result, err)
        }
        if len(result.Outputs) != 1 || result.RawMetrics == nil || result.RawMetrics.ConcatMode != "stream_copy" || result.RawMetrics.EncodePasses != 0 || !result.RawMetrics.FinalConcatStreamCopy {
            t.Fatalf("slice result did not report copy-only remote assembly: %+v", result)
        }
        if len(runner.args) != 1 {
            t.Fatalf("FFmpeg call count = %d, want one stream-copy concat/mux", len(runner.args))
        }
        copyArgs := strings.Join(runner.args[0], " ")
        for _, want := range []string{"-f concat", "-c:v copy", "-tag:v avc3", "-c:a copy", "-frames:v 24"} {
            if !strings.Contains(copyArgs, want) {
                t.Errorf("FFmpeg stream-copy args missing %q: %s", want, copyArgs)
            }
        }
        if strings.Contains(copyArgs, "libx264") || strings.Contains(copyArgs, "filter_complex") {
            t.Fatalf("copy path must not contain an encoder or filter graph: %s", copyArgs)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(runner.concatInput, "inpoint 0\noutpoint 1.000000\nduration 1.000000") {
            t.Fatalf("concat manifest does not contain the expected source window: %q", runner.concatInput)
        }
        if strings.Contains(copyArgs, "14.000000") {
            t.Fatalf("copy path unexpectedly trims a non-keyframe source offset: %s", copyArgs)
        }
    }
    
    func TestVideoAssembleSlice_RejectsNonKeyframeOffsetBeforeFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
        plan := driveSlicePlan()
        plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[0].SourceInUS = 14_000_000
        canonical, err := plan.CanonicalJSON()
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        runner := &sliceFFmpegRunner{}
        exec := &videoAssembleSliceExecutor{runner: runner, prober: sliceMediaProbeStub{}, outputRoot: t.TempDir()}
        spec := executorTaskSpec(VideoAssembleSliceID, "job-drive-slice-invalid-cut", canonical, plan)
        result, err := exec.Execute(context.Background(), nil, spec)
        if err != nil || result.Status != "failed" {
            t.Fatalf("invalid copy plan result=%+v err=%v, want immediate failure", result, err)
        }
        if result.ErrorCode != "DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID" || len(runner.args) != 0 {
            t.Fatalf("invalid cut was not rejected before FFmpeg: result=%+v ffmpeg_calls=%d", result, len(runner.args))
        }
    }

    // RenderClient is the interface for executing a RenderPlan.
    // Implemented by the native C++ render client.
    type RenderClient interface {
        Render(ctx context.Context, p *plan.RenderPlan) error
        RenderWithMetrics(ctx context.Context, p *plan.RenderPlan) (RenderMetrics, error)
    }
    
    // CompiledPlanV2Renderer is the narrow optional native surface used by the
    // packet-copy executor. Keeping it separate preserves existing test clients
    // and prevents legacy V1 pipeline callers from depending on V2.
    type CompiledPlanV2Renderer interface {
        RenderCompiledPlanV2(context.Context, []byte, string) (RenderMetrics, error)
    }
    
    // RenderMetrics captures the native engine sidecar + subprocess wall-clock
    // counters. The zero value is safe — executors that don't use native
    // rendering return it unpopulated.
    type RenderMetrics struct {
        // Native CPU budget selected by the worker for this attempt.
        EffectiveCPUCores int
        RenderCPUBudget   int
        DecoderThreads    int
        EncoderThreads    int
        SegmentWorkers    int
        Frames            int64

    package pipeline
    
    import (
        "context"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "testing"
    
        "velox-worker-agent/pkg/logger"
        "velox-worker-agent/pkg/video/plan"
    )
    
    // fakeRenderClient is a stub RenderClient used by runner_test.go to
    // verify that RenderClient() exposes the same instance the constructor
    // was given.
    type fakeRenderClient struct {
        called  bool
        payload []byte
    }
    
    type hookTestCompiler struct{}
    
    func (hookTestCompiler) ID() string { return "hook-test.v1" }
    
    func (hookTestCompiler) Validate(map[string]interface{}) error { return nil }
    
    func (hookTestCompiler) Compile(_ context.Context, jobID string, _ map[string]interface{}, outputPath string) (*plan.RenderPlan, error) {
        return &plan.RenderPlan{
            Version: 1,
            JobID:   jobID,
            Canvas:  plan.CanvasSpec{Width: 1, Height: 1, Fps: 1},
            Timeline: []plan.TimelineItem{{
                Source:          plan.MediaSource{Type: "color", ColorHex: "#000000"},
                DurationSeconds: 0.1,
            }},
            OutputPath: outputPath,
        }, nil
    }
    
    func (f *fakeRenderClient) Render(_ context.Context, p *plan.RenderPlan) error {
        _, err := f.RenderWithMetrics(context.Background(), p)
        return err
    }
    
    func (f *fakeRenderClient) RenderWithMetrics(_ context.Context, p *plan.RenderPlan) (RenderMetrics, error) {
        f.called = true
        if p == nil || p.OutputPath == "" {
            return RenderMetrics{}, nil
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p.OutputPath), 0o755); err != nil {
            return RenderMetrics{}, err
        }
        return RenderMetrics{}, os.WriteFile(p.OutputPath, f.payload, 0o644)
    }
    
    // TestRunner_RenderClientAccessor: the accessor's contract is "return
    // the SAME pointer the constructor was given". A test that synthesises
    // a Runner, then calls its Render accessor, verifies the resulting
    // interface still drives the underlying fake.
    func TestRunner_RenderClientAccessor(t *testing.T) {
        reg := NewRegistry()
        rc := &fakeRenderClient{payload: []byte("accessor-test-bytes")}
        log := logger.New(logger.InfoLevel, os.Stderr)
        runner := NewRunner(reg, rc, log)
        if runner == nil {
