    ---
    # PR D — Worker Docker image release pipeline.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 1 of 100% Velox certification plan (cap. 2): every published digest
    # is sign + verify + baseline-recorded + bootstrap-tested under REAL deps
    # before the operator side ever sees a tag. NO `:latest`. NO fake-ffmpeg
    # bootstrap smoke. NO unsigned image accepted.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    name: Worker image release
    
    on:
      push:
        tags:
          - 'worker-v*'
        branches:
          - main
        paths:
          - 'RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/**'
          - 'RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp/**'
          - 'RemoteCodex/scripts/build-video-engine.sh'
          - 'shared/**'
          - 'VERSION.txt'
          - '.github/workflows/worker-image.yml'
          - '.github/actions/worker-*/**'
          - 'scripts/ci/test-worker-image-freshness.py'
          - 'scripts/ci/check-mixed-render-gate.sh'
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          version:
            description: 'Version label (e.g. 1.2.3 or v1.2.3-rc1). The leading v is optional.'
            required: true
            default: ''
          no_push:
            description: 'Build + sign skipped locally — do NOT push, do NOT sign.'
            required: false
            default: 'false'
            type: boolean
    
    # Serialize certification/publish and replace stale pending builds, but do not
    # cancel an active sign/certification run after it may have pushed an image.
    concurrency:
      group: worker-image-release
      cancel-in-progress: false
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
    
    env:
      REGISTRY: ghcr.io
      IMAGE_NAME: velox-worker
      IMAGE_REPO: ghcr.io/marcuss-ops/velox-worker
      BUILD_DIR: RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go
      DOCKERFILE: RemoteCodex/native/worker-agent-go/Dockerfile
      BUILD_CONTEXT: .
    
    jobs:
      build-publish:
        name: Build, test, push, sign, verify, baseline, real-bootstrap
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 30
    
        steps:
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              fetch-depth: 0
    
          - name: Verify release freshness controls
            run: python3 scripts/ci/test-worker-image-freshness.py
    
          - name: Verify checkout is the event commit
            run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              CHECKOUT_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
              if [ "$CHECKOUT_SHA" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
                echo "::error::checkout commit ($CHECKOUT_SHA) does not match event commit ($GITHUB_SHA). Refusing to certify an ambiguous source tree." >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "Release source commit: $GITHUB_SHA"

              echo "Release source commit: $GITHUB_SHA"
    
          - name: Read VERSION.txt (canonical source)
            id: read-version
            run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              VERSION="$(tr -d '[:space:]' < VERSION.txt)"
              if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
                echo "::error::VERSION.txt is empty — refusing to publish." >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "version=${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "Resolved version from VERSION.txt: ${VERSION}"
    
          - name: Resolve effective version + determine push
            id: version
            run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "push" ] && [ "${{ github.ref_type }}" = "tag" ]; then
                TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#worker-v}"
              elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "push" ]; then
                TAG="${{ steps.read-version.outputs.version }}"
                TAG="${TAG#v}"
              elif [ -n "${{ inputs.version }}" ]; then
                INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
                TAG="${INPUT#v}"
              else
                TAG="${{ steps.read-version.outputs.version }}"
              fi
              if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
                echo "::error::Could not resolve version." >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              EXPECTED="${{ steps.read-version.outputs.version }}"
              EXPECTED="${EXPECTED#v}"
              if [ -n "$EXPECTED" ] && [ "$TAG" != "$EXPECTED" ]; then
                echo "::error::Resolved tag ($TAG) != canonical VERSION.txt ($EXPECTED). Refusing." >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "tag=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              SHORT_SHA="${GITHUB_SHA::7}"
              echo "short_sha=${SHORT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "push" ]; then
                SHOULD_PUSH="true"
              elif [ "${{ inputs.no_push }}" = "true" ]; then
                SHOULD_PUSH="false"
              else
                SHOULD_PUSH="true"
              fi
              echo "push=${SHOULD_PUSH}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    
          # The test action owns only the worker race gate. It deliberately runs
          # before Buildx and publication, preserving the fail-fast release order.
          - name: Worker tests (race detector)
            uses: ./.github/actions/worker-test
            with:
              build-dir: ${{ env.BUILD_DIR }}
    
          # Run the native mixed golden before Buildx. This is deliberately an
          # image-independent source gate: a legacy video fallback or a broken
          # designated initializer must fail before build/sign/certification.
          - name: Mixed packet-copy golden gate
            run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              sudo apt-get update
              sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
                cmake ffmpeg pkg-config libavformat-dev libavcodec-dev libavutil-dev libswscale-dev
              VIDEO_MIXED_BUILD_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/velox-mixed-render-build" \
                bash scripts/ci/check-mixed-render-gate.sh

    package executors

    type sliceNativeRenderer struct {
        calls int
        wire  []byte
    }
    
    func (*sliceNativeRenderer) Render(context.Context, *plan.RenderPlan) error { return nil }
    
    func (*sliceNativeRenderer) RenderWithMetrics(context.Context, *plan.RenderPlan) (pipeline.RenderMetrics, error) {
        return pipeline.RenderMetrics{}, nil
    }
    
    func (r *sliceNativeRenderer) RenderCompiledPlanV2(_ context.Context, wire []byte, outputPath string) (pipeline.RenderMetrics, error) {
        r.calls++
        r.wire = append([]byte(nil), wire...)
        if err := os.WriteFile(outputPath, []byte("native-packet-mux"), 0o640); err != nil {
            return pipeline.RenderMetrics{}, err
        }
        return pipeline.RenderMetrics{TotalMs: 12, DurationSec: 1, ConcatMode: "packet_copy"}, nil
    }
    
    type sliceMediaProbeStub struct{}

    func TestVideoAssembleSlice_CopiesDriveSourceWindowsWithoutReencoding(t *testing.T) {

            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(audioPath, []byte("audio"), 0o640); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }

        runner := pipeline.NewRunner(nil, renderer, nil)
        exec := &videoAssembleSliceExecutor{runner: runner, prober: sliceMediaProbeStub{}, outputRoot: t.TempDir()}
        spec := executorTaskSpec(VideoAssembleSliceID, "job-drive-slice", canonical, plan)
        result, err := exec.Execute(runtimeassets.WithBindings(context.Background(), runtimeassets.Bindings{
            "drive:stock-01": {AssetID: "drive:stock-01", Path: videoPath, SHA256: strings.Repeat("b", 64), Size: 5, Verified: true},
            "audio":          {AssetID: "audio", Path: audioPath, SHA256: copyOnlySHA([]byte("audio")), Size: 5, Verified: true},
        }), nil, spec)
        if err != nil || result.Status != "succeeded" {
            t.Fatalf("slice execution result=%+v err=%v", result, err)
        }
        if len(result.Outputs) != 1 || result.RawMetrics == nil || result.RawMetrics.ConcatMode != "stream_copy" || result.RawMetrics.EncodePasses != 0 || !result.RawMetrics.FinalConcatStreamCopy {
            t.Fatalf("slice result did not report copy-only remote assembly: %+v", result)
        }
        if renderer.calls != 1 {
            t.Fatalf("native packet renderer call count = %d, want one", renderer.calls)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(string(renderer.wire), `"bindings"`) || !strings.Contains(string(renderer.wire), `"output_path"`) {
            t.Fatalf("native render did not receive the bound compiled plan: %s", renderer.wire)
        }
    }

    }

    func validateCopyOnlyPlan(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) error {
        if plan == nil {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.copy.v1: plan is nil")
        }
        profile, err := validateCopyOnlyProfile(plan)
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) == 0 {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.copy.v1: exactly one non-empty video track is required")
        }
        assets := make(map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, len(plan.Assets))
        for _, asset := range plan.Assets {
            assets[asset.AssetID] = asset
        }
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            if err := validateCopyOnlySegment(plan, profile, assets, segment); err != nil {
                return err
            }
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    // validateCopyOnlyProfile resolves the output's canonical profile and checks
    // every stream-identity field against it. The packet-copy path can only accept
    // streams produced under an admitted profile.
    func validateCopyOnlyProfile(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2) (contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1, error) {
        if plan.Output.ProfileID == "" {
            return contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: output.profile_id is required", ErrCopyOnlyProfileMismatch)
        }
        profile, err := contract.KnownCanonicalVideoProfileV1(plan.Output.ProfileID)
        if err != nil {
            return contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrCopyOnlyProfileMismatch, err)
        }
        if err := profile.MatchesOutput(plan.Output); err != nil {
            return contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrCopyOnlyProfileMismatch, err)
        }
        if plan.Output.CodecProfile != profile.CodecProfile || plan.Output.CodecLevel != profile.CodecLevel || plan.Output.GOPSize != profile.GOPSize || plan.Output.BFrames != profile.BFrames || plan.Output.TimeBaseNum != profile.TimeBaseNum || plan.Output.TimeBaseDen != profile.TimeBaseDen || !plan.Output.ClosedGOP {
            return contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: output encoder/time-base fields do not match profile %q", ErrCopyOnlyProfileMismatch, profile.ProfileID)
        }
        return profile, nil
    }
    
    // validateCopyOnlySegment certifies one prepared video fragment against its
    // declared asset manifest: the reference must exist, be a prepared-video kind,
    // and match the plan's timeline identity and frame bounds exactly.
    func validateCopyOnlySegment(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, profile contract.CanonicalVideoProfileV1, assets map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, segment contract.VideoSegmentV2) error {
        asset, ok := assets[segment.AssetID]
        if !ok || (asset.Kind != "video" && asset.Kind != "prepared_video_fragment") {
            return fmt.Errorf("%w: segment %q does not reference a prepared video asset", ErrCopyOnlyCertification, segment.SegmentID)
        }
        if asset.SHA256 != segment.SHA256 || asset.ProfileID != profile.StreamProfile() || asset.FrameCount != segment.FrameCount || asset.TimelineRevision != plan.TimelineRevision || asset.TimelineSHA256 != plan.TimelineSHA256 || asset.TimelineStartFrame != segment.TimelineStartFrame || asset.DurationUS != segment.SourceDurationUS || !asset.FirstFrameKeyframe || !asset.ClosedGOP || segment.SourceInUS != 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("%w: segment %q manifest binding is not exact", ErrCopyOnlyCertification, segment.SegmentID)
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    func validatePreparedAssetBindings(plan *contract.CompiledRenderPlanV2, bindings runtimeassets.Bindings) error {
        if err := validateCopyOnlyPlan(plan); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            binding := bindings[segment.AssetID]
            if strings.TrimSpace(binding.Path) == "" {
                return fmt.Errorf("%w: missing binding for %q", ErrCopyOnlyCertification, segment.AssetID)
            }
        }
        return nil
    }

    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) Validate(spec executor.TaskSpec) error {
        if spec.ExecutorID != VideoAssembleSliceID {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: executor_id must be %q", VideoAssembleSliceID)
        }
        if e == nil || e.runner == nil || e.runner.RenderClient() == nil {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: native packet-copy renderer is not configured")
        }
        if e.prober == nil {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: FFprobe media validation is not configured")
        }
        plan, err := decodeCompiledPlanV2(spec)
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: invalid CompiledRenderPlanV2: %w", err)
        }
        if _, err := contract.KnownCanonicalVideoProfileV1(plan.Output.ProfileID); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: canonical output profile required: %w", err)
        }
        assets := make(map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, len(plan.Assets))
        runtimeDriveIDs := sliceRuntimeDriveFileIDs(spec.Payload["runtime_assets"])
        hasDrive := plan.StockPool != nil
        for _, asset := range plan.Assets {
            assets[asset.AssetID] = asset
            driveSource := asset.Kind == "video" && isSliceDriveSource(asset, runtimeDriveIDs)
            hasDrive = hasDrive || driveSource
        }
        if !hasDrive {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: plan must contain at least one Drive video source")
        }
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || (len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) == 0 && plan.StockPool == nil) {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: exactly one video track is required; segments or stock_pool must be supplied")
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil {
            members := 0
            for _, item := range sliceRuntimePoolMembers(spec.Payload["runtime_assets"]) {
                if item.StockPoolMember && strings.TrimSpace(item.DriveFileID) != "" {
                    members++
                }
            }
            if members == 0 {
                return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: Master did not resolve any stock_pool files")
            }
        }
        var nextFrame int64
        stockPoolSlots := 0
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            if segment.StockPoolSlot {
                if plan.StockPool == nil {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q has stock_pool_slot without stock_pool", segment.SegmentID)
                }
                stockPoolSlots++
                if segment.FrameCount <= 0 {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: stock pool slot %q has invalid frame count", segment.SegmentID)
                }
            } else {
                asset, ok := assets[segment.AssetID]
                if !ok || (asset.Kind != "video" && asset.Kind != "prepared_video_fragment") {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q must reference a video asset", segment.SegmentID)
                }
                if asset.ProfileID != plan.Output.ProfileID || asset.FrameCount <= 0 || !asset.FirstFrameKeyframe || !asset.ClosedGOP {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: asset %q is not certified for packet-copy assembly", segment.AssetID)
                }
                if segment.SourceInUS != 0 {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q starts at a non-keyframe offset (%d us); packet-copy is unsafe", segment.SegmentID, segment.SourceInUS)
                }
                if segment.FrameCount <= 0 || segment.FrameCount > asset.FrameCount {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q frame count %d exceeds certified source frames %d", segment.SegmentID, segment.FrameCount, asset.FrameCount)
                }
            }
            if segment.TimelineStartFrame != nextFrame {
                return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q leaves a timeline gap or overlap at frame %d", segment.SegmentID, nextFrame)
            }
            nextFrame += segment.FrameCount
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil && stockPoolSlots == 0 {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: stock_pool requires at least one stock slot")
        }
        framesNum := int64(plan.DurationUS) * int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
        framesDen := int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000
        wantFrames := (framesNum + framesDen - 1) / framesDen
        if nextFrame != wantFrames {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: timeline has %d frames, plan duration requires %d", nextFrame, wantFrames)
        }
        return nil
    }

    func TestCopyOnlyRenderErrorCode(t *testing.T) {
        cases := []struct {
            name string
            err  error
            want string
        }{
            {"nil error defaults to generic", nil, "PACKET_COPY_FAILED"},
            {"exact keyframe rejection", errors.New("engine failed: copy-only source window must start on an exact video keyframe: /c.mp4 source_in_us=60000000"), "COPY_ONLY_NOT_KEYFRAME_SAFE"},
            {"mixed-path keyframe rejection", errors.New("segment_execution_rejected: source window is not keyframe-safe for packet copy (segment 0)"), "COPY_ONLY_NOT_KEYFRAME_SAFE"},
            {"unrelated mux failure stays generic", errors.New("engine failed: copy-only packet mux failed: avformat_alloc_output_context2"), "PACKET_COPY_FAILED"},
        }
        for _, tc := range cases {
            t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
                if got := copyOnlyRenderErrorCode(tc.err); got != tc.want {
                    t.Fatalf("copyOnlyRenderErrorCode(%v) = %q, want %q", tc.err, got, tc.want)
                }
            })
        }
    }

    name: Worker tests
    description: Run the worker-agent Go race test gate with one retry.
    inputs:
      build-dir:
        description: Worker agent directory containing go.mod.
        required: true
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - name: Setup Go
          uses: actions/setup-go@v5
          with:
            go-version: '1.25.8'
            cache-dependency-path: ${{ inputs.build-dir }}/go.sum
    
        - name: Run tests with race detector (fail-fast gate)
          shell: bash
          working-directory: ${{ inputs.build-dir }}
          run: |
            set -euo pipefail
            for attempt in 1 2; do
              if go test -race -timeout 5m ./internal/... ./pkg/...; then
                exit 0
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" -eq 1 ]; then
                echo "Race suite failed once; retrying once to distinguish a transient failure." >&2
              fi
            done
            exit 1

    // Reserve protects an asset for an imminent job until expiresAt. Reservations
    // are durable and participate in the same cleanup protection barrier as leases.
    func (c *Cache) Reserve(ctx context.Context, assetKey, reservationID string, expiresAt time.Time) error {
        if assetKey == "" {
            return ErrEmptyID
        }
        if reservationID == "" || expiresAt.IsZero() {
            return fmt.Errorf("workercache.Reserve: reservation ID and expiry are required")
        }
        res, err := c.db.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO cached_asset_reservations (asset_key, reservation_id, expires_at) SELECT asset_key, ?, ? FROM cached_assets WHERE asset_key = ?`, reservationID, expiresAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano), assetKey)
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("workercache.Reserve(%q, %q): %w", assetKey, reservationID, err)
        }
        return mustHaveAffected(res, assetKey, "Reserve")
    }
    
    // ReleaseReservation removes one future-job reservation. It is idempotent
    // when the cache row still exists.
    func (c *Cache) ReleaseReservation(ctx context.Context, assetKey, reservationID string) error {
        if assetKey == "" {
            return ErrEmptyID
        }
        if _, err := c.db.ExecContext(ctx, `DELETE FROM cached_asset_reservations WHERE asset_key = ? AND reservation_id = ?`, assetKey, reservationID); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("workercache.ReleaseReservation(%q, %q): %w", assetKey, reservationID, err)
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    // DeleteIfUnleased atomically removes an unleased and unreserved cache row.
    // The predicates close the List→Delete race when another job acquires a lease
    // or future-job reservation while cleanup is scanning. Cleanup should prefer
    // EvictIfUnleased so physical removal and index deletion share a write fence.
    func (c *Cache) DeleteIfUnleased(ctx context.Context, assetKey string) error {
        if assetKey == "" {
            return ErrEmptyID
        }
        res, err := c.db.ExecContext(ctx, `DELETE FROM cached_assets WHERE asset_key = ? AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cached_asset_leases WHERE asset_key = ?) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cached_asset_reservations WHERE asset_key = ? AND julianday(expires_at) > julianday('now'))`, assetKey, assetKey, assetKey)
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("workercache.DeleteIfUnleased(%q): %w", assetKey, err)
        }
        if err := mustHaveAffected(res, assetKey, "DeleteIfUnleased"); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        c.deleteOrphanedBlobs(ctx)
        return nil
    }

    func (c *Cache) Find(ctx context.Context, assetKey string) (Entry, bool, error) {
        if assetKey == "" {
            return Entry{}, false, ErrEmptyID
        }
        row := c.db.QueryRowContext(ctx,
            `SELECT `+selectCols+selectFrom+` WHERE a.asset_key = ?`,
            assetKey)
        e, err := scanEntry(row)
        if errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) {
            return Entry{}, false, nil
        }
        if err != nil {
            return Entry{}, false, fmt.Errorf("workercache.Find(%q): %w", assetKey, err)
        }
        if e.DownloadComplete {
            if !validStoredContentHash(e.storedContentHash) {
                if invalidateErr := c.invalidateStoredBlob(ctx, e.storedContentHash); invalidateErr != nil && !errors.Is(invalidateErr, ErrNotFound) && !errors.Is(invalidateErr, ErrBlobInFlight) && !errors.Is(invalidateErr, ErrBlobProtected) {
                    return Entry{}, false, fmt.Errorf("workercache.Find(%q): invalidate invalid hash: %w", assetKey, invalidateErr)
                }
                e.LocalPath = ""
                e.SizeBytes = 0
                e.DownloadComplete = false
                return *e, true, nil
            }
            valid, validationErr := c.validatePhysicalPath(e.LocalPath, e.SizeBytes)
            if validationErr != nil {
                return Entry{}, false, fmt.Errorf("workercache.Find(%q): validate blob: %w", assetKey, validationErr)
            }
            if !valid {
                if invalidateErr := c.invalidateStoredBlob(ctx, e.storedContentHash); invalidateErr != nil && !errors.Is(invalidateErr, ErrNotFound) && !errors.Is(invalidateErr, ErrBlobInFlight) && !errors.Is(invalidateErr, ErrBlobProtected) {
                    return Entry{}, false, fmt.Errorf("workercache.Find(%q): invalidate blob: %w", assetKey, invalidateErr)
                }
                // Keep asset_key → content_hash metadata, but turn this lookup into
                // a miss so the resolver downloads and promotes a fresh blob.
                e.LocalPath = ""
                e.SizeBytes = 0
                e.DownloadComplete = false
            }
        }
        return *e, true, nil
    }

    func TestDispatchTaskRunner_V2LeasesAllAssetsAndReleasesOnSuccess(t *testing.T) {
        probe := &dispatchLeaseProbeExecutor{wait: true, started: make(chan struct{}), release: make(chan struct{})}
        w, cache, payload, keys := newDispatchV2LeaseFixture(t, probe)
        jobID := "job-v2-lease-success"
        resultCh := make(chan error, 1)
        go func() {
            _, err := w.dispatchTaskRunner(context.Background(), dispatchV2LeaseTask(payload, jobID))
            resultCh <- err
        }()
    
        <-probe.started
        assertV2Leases(t, cache, keys, jobID, 1)
        if !containsString(keys, "v2-audio") {
            t.Fatalf("lease set %v does not include final_audio", keys)
        }
        close(probe.release)
        if err := <-resultCh; err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("dispatch success returned error: %v", err)
        }
        assertV2Leases(t, cache, keys, "", 0)
    }

    240:func (w *Worker) syncClipCache(ctx context.Context, assetID, localPath string, sizeBytes int64, hash assetref.ContentHash) error {
    func (w *Worker) assetDownloadConcurrency() int {
        if w.config != nil && w.config.AssetDownloadConcurrency > 0 {
            return w.config.AssetDownloadConcurrency
        }
        return downloader.DefaultAssetConcurrency
    }
    
    // syncClipCache records a verified asset in the durable remote-worker index.
    // The content-addressed byte cache remains the data source; this index owns
    // leases, protected snapshots and eviction decisions.
    func (w *Worker) syncClipCache(ctx context.Context, assetID, localPath string, sizeBytes int64, hash assetref.ContentHash) error {
        if w.canonicalAssetCache == nil {
            return nil
        }
        key := assetref.AssetKey(assetID)
        entry := workercache.Entry{AssetKey: key, ContentHash: hash, LocalPath: localPath, SizeBytes: sizeBytes, DownloadComplete: true}
        if err := w.canonicalAssetCache.Store(ctx, entry); err != nil {
            if !errors.Is(err, workercache.ErrDuplicate) {
                return err
            }
            if err := w.canonicalAssetCache.PreserveContentHash(ctx, key, localPath, sizeBytes, hash); err != nil {
                return err
            }
        }
        return w.canonicalAssetCache.MarkUsed(ctx, key)
    }

## User

Sì, ho capito perfettamente: mai più taglio locale. Il materiale sul Drive è già nel codec giusto e non va scaricato, tagliato, ricodificato o ricaricato. Il Producer deve solo passare al Master il riferimento Drive e i metadata; il consumo dei byte è a valle. Ritiro esplicitamente il suggerimento precedente di ripristinare i frammenti stock: sarebbe esattamente il lavoro inutile che rifiuti.

Ho quindi provato solo la strada “metadata-only”:

Cosa ho cambiato
- In  refactored/internal/app/wiring/remote_final_job_resolve.go  il ref stock ora porta:
-  source_uri  = URL HTTPS diretto del file Drive ( drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=... ), verificato pubblicamente:  video/mp4 , 3.152.434 byte, coerente col size certificato;
-  asset_id  = SHA-256 completo, non più  stock-sha256-<sha24> , applicando la stessa regola di identità canonica già corretta in r37 v2.
- Nessun byte stock è stato scaricato, tagliato o pubblicato dal pipeline.
- Build e test mirati  FinalJob|Stock  passano; binario ricompilato e servizio riavviato (PID 315407, health 200).

Esito dei due run
-  retry2 : FAILED in 136 s.
-  retry3  (con  asset_id  = SHA completo): FAILED in 130 s.
- Errore identico, sempre in  reserve  prima dell’assembly:
 worker.reserveJobAssetProtection(<sha completo>): workercache: cached asset not found 
- Nel payload finalize c’erano 177 ref stock con  drive_file_id ,  url: velox-drive://…  e il nuovo  source_uri . Quindi il riferimento arriva al Master, ma il workercache non viene popolato: il worker copy-only continua a pretendere il frammento già in cache.

Conclusione
Con il vincolo “niente taglio locale”, lato Producer non c’è un’altra correzione sensata. Il pezzo mancante è sul Master/worker: deve accettare lo stock come sorgente Drive, fare lui il prefetch di  source_uri  nel workercache sotto l’ asset_id  canonico (allowlist per  drive.usercontent.google.com ) e poi assemblare in packet-copy, senza ricodifica. Finché resta  video.assemble.copy.v1  con “frammenti già cachati”, il job non può chiudersi senza quel ingest remoto.

File del test:  r39-20261106-new-stock-drive-retry2-job-full.json  e  r39-20261106-new-stock-drive-retry3-job-full.json  in  ops/jobs/garlasco_editorial_e2e_20261030/ .  capito ?

Ho trovato anche che i test devono usare l’identità cache effettiva, non lo SHA come alias, e sto correggendo questo allineamento prima del nuovo rilascio.

    package worker
    
    import (
        "context"
        "errors"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "sync"
        "testing"
        "time"
    
        "velox-shared/assetref"
        "velox-worker-agent/internal/executor"
        "velox-worker-agent/internal/taskrunner"
        "velox-worker-agent/internal/workercache"
        "velox-worker-agent/pkg/config"
        "velox-worker-agent/pkg/logger"
    )
    
    type dispatchLeaseProbeExecutor struct {
        id      string
        wait    bool
        fail    bool
        started chan struct{}
        release chan struct{}
        once    sync.Once
    }
    
    func (e *dispatchLeaseProbeExecutor) Descriptor() executor.Descriptor {
        id := e.id
        if id == "" {
            id = "video.assemble.copy.v1"
        }
        return executor.Descriptor{
            ID: id, Version: 1,
            ResourceClass: executor.ResourceCPU, TemporalMode: executor.TemporalGlobal,
            Deterministic: true, Cacheable: true,
        }
    }
    
    func (e *dispatchLeaseProbeExecutor) Validate(executor.TaskSpec) error { return nil }
    
    func (e *dispatchLeaseProbeExecutor) Execute(ctx context.Context, _ executor.ExecutionContext, _ executor.TaskSpec) (executor.ExecutionResult, error) {
        e.once.Do(func() { close(e.started) })
        if e.wait {
            select {
            case <-e.release:
            case <-ctx.Done():
                return executor.ExecutionResult{}, ctx.Err()
            }
        }
        if e.fail {
            return executor.ExecutionResult{}, errors.New("forced render failure")
        }
        return executor.ExecutionResult{Status: "succeeded"}, nil
    }
    
    func newDispatchV2LeaseFixture(t *testing.T, probe *dispatchLeaseProbeExecutor) (*Worker, *workercache.Cache, map[string]interface{}, []string) {
        t.Helper()
        assets := map[string][]byte{
            "v2-video": []byte("prepared-video-bytes"),
            "v2-audio": []byte("final-audio-bytes"),
        }
        payload := compiledPlanAssetPayload(t, assets)
        cache, err := workercache.Open(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "cache.db"))
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("open worker cache: %v", err)
        }
        t.Cleanup(func() { _ = cache.Close() })
        for assetID, body := range assets {
            path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), assetID+".asset")
            if err := os.WriteFile(path, body, 0o640); err != nil {
                t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", assetID, err)
            }
            hash := assetSHA(body)
            if err := cache.Store(context.Background(), workercache.Entry{
                AssetKey:         assetref.AssetKey(assetID),
                ContentHash:      assetref.ContentHash(hash),
                LocalPath:        path,
                SizeBytes:        int64(len(body)),
                DownloadComplete: true,
            }); err != nil {
                t.Fatalf("store %s: %v", assetID, err)
            }
        }
    
        registry := executor.NewRegistry()
        if err := registry.Register(probe); err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("register probe executor: %v", err)
        }
        log := logger.New(logger.InfoLevel, os.Stderr)
        w := &Worker{
            config: &config.WorkerConfig{WorkerID: "worker-v2-lease", WorkDir: t.TempDir()},
            logger: log, activeTasks: make(map[string]*ActiveTaskExecution),
            taskRunner: taskrunner.NewTaskRunner(registry, log),
            clipCache:  cache, canonicalAssetCache: workercache.NewCanonicalAssetStore(cache),
        }
        t.Cleanup(func() {
            if w.assetManager != nil {
                w.assetManager.Close()
            }
        })
        keys := extractAssetKeysFromJSON(payload)
        return w, cache, payload, keys
    }
    
    func dispatchV2LeaseTask(payload map[string]interface{}, jobID string) *PendingTaskExecution {
        return &PendingTaskExecution{
            TaskID: "task-" + jobID, JobID: jobID, AttemptID: "attempt-" + jobID,
            ExecutorID: "video.assemble.copy.v1", ExecutorVersion: 1,
            Spec: executor.TaskSpec{
                Version: 1, JobID: jobID, ExecutorID: "video.assemble.copy.v1", Payload: payload,
            },
        }
    }

    func (t *masterAssetTransferer) shouldChunk(req downloader.DownloadRequest) bool {
        enabled, threshold, _ := t.chunkedConfig()

    // chunkedConfig resolves the effective chunked-download settings from the
    // worker config, applying the canonical defaults for zero values so callers

    func (t *masterAssetTransferer) chunkedConfig() (enabled bool, threshold int64, concurrency int) {
        if t == nil || t.w == nil || t.w.config == nil {
            return false, 0, 0
        }
        cfg := t.w.config
        if !cfg.AssetChunkedDownloadEnabled {
            return false, 0, 0
        }
        threshold = cfg.AssetChunkedDownloadThresholdBytes
        if threshold <= 0 {
            threshold = config.DefaultAssetChunkedDownloadThresholdBytes
        }
        concurrency = cfg.AssetChunkedDownloadConcurrency
        if concurrency < 1 {
            concurrency = config.DefaultAssetChunkedDownloadConcurrency
        }

## Activity

    $ sed -n '140,230p' .github/workflows/worker-image.yml; gh run view 42195586207 --log-failed 2>&1 | grep -n -A10 -B5 'Verify published image digest\|Process completed with exit code 255' | tail -60
          # Run the native mixed golden before Buildx. This is deliberately an
          # image-independent source gate: a legacy video fallback or a broken
          # designated initializer must fail before build/sign/certification.
          - name: Mixed packet-copy golden gate
            run: |
              set -euo pipefail
              sudo apt-get update
              sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
                cmake ffmpeg pkg-config libavformat-dev libavcodec-dev libavutil-dev libswscale-dev
              VIDEO_MIXED_BUILD_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/velox-mixed-render-build" \
                bash scripts/ci/check-mixed-render-gate.sh
    
          # This action owns Buildx, GHCR login, explicit non-latest tags, image
          # publication, digest extraction, registry digest verification, and the
          # worker-image-digest artifact. It keeps the digest in the same job so
          # later signing and certification consume the exact build output.
          - name: Worker image build and digest verification
            id: build
            uses: ./.github/actions/worker-build
            with:
              registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
              image-repo: ${{ env.IMAGE_REPO }}
              build-context: ${{ env.BUILD_CONTEXT }}
              dockerfile: ${{ env.DOCKERFILE }}
              tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
              push: ${{ steps.version.outputs.push }}
              github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
              # Share the warm BuildKit cache across main, tags, and dispatches.
              cache-scope: velox-worker-build
    
          # Signing remains digest-only and is disabled for no-push validation
          # runs. The action contains the repository/workflow-bound OIDC identity
          # policy and the canonical token issuer check.
          - name: Worker image signing and verification
            if: steps.build.outputs.digest != '' && steps.version.outputs.push == 'true'
            uses: ./.github/actions/worker-sign
            with:
              image-repo: ${{ env.IMAGE_REPO }}
              digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
              push: ${{ steps.version.outputs.push }}
    
          # Certification runs only against the immutable published digest and
          # preserves baseline, real bootstrap, audio canary, mixed canary, and
          # entrypoint smoke in their original order.
          - name: Worker image certification
            if: steps.build.outputs.digest != '' && steps.version.outputs.push == 'true'
            uses: ./.github/actions/worker-certify
            with:
              image-repo: ${{ env.IMAGE_REPO }}
              digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}

    $ cat .github/actions/worker-build/action.yml;
    name: Worker image build
    description: Build, optionally publish, verify, and record the worker image digest.
    inputs:
      registry:
        description: Container registry hostname.
        required: true
      image-repo:
        description: Fully qualified worker image repository.
        required: true
      build-context:
        description: Docker build context.
        required: true
      dockerfile:
        description: Worker Dockerfile path.
        required: true
      tag:
        description: Canonical release tag without the worker-v prefix.
        required: true
      push:
        description: Whether the image may be pushed to the registry.
        required: true
      github-token:
        description: GitHub token used for GHCR authentication.
        required: true
      cache-scope:
        description: Buildx cache scope.
        required: true
    outputs:
      digest:
        description: Immutable digest emitted by docker/build-push-action.
        value: ${{ steps.digest.outputs.digest }}
      tags:
        description: Explicit image tags generated by docker/metadata-action.
        value: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - name: Set up Docker Buildx
          uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
    
        - name: Log in to GHCR
          if: inputs.push == 'true'
          uses: docker/login-action@v3
          with:
            registry: ${{ inputs.registry }}
            username: ${{ github.actor }}
            password: ${{ inputs.github-token }}
    
        # Never generate :latest. Only the canonical semver and short SHA tags
        # are published for a worker release.
        - name: Compute image tags (NO :latest)
          id: meta
          uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
          with:
            images: ${{ inputs.image-repo }}
            tags: |
              type=raw,value=${{ inputs.tag }}
              type=sha,prefix=sha-,format=short
            flavor: |
              latest=false
    
        - name: Build + push image
          id: build
          uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
          with:
            context: ${{ inputs.build-context }}
            file: ${{ inputs.dockerfile }}
            push: ${{ inputs.push == 'true' }}
            tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
            labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
            build-args: |
              SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0
            provenance: true
            sbom: true
            cache-from: type=gha,scope=${{ inputs.cache-scope }}
            cache-to:   type=gha,mode=max,scope=${{ inputs.cache-scope }}
    
        - name: Extract image digest
          id: digest
          if: steps.build.outputs.digest != ''
          shell: bash
          run: |
            set -euo pipefail
            echo "digest=${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}" > image-digest.txt
            echo "## Image digest" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo ":package: \`${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            TAGS='${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}'
            while IFS= read -r t; do
              [ -n "$t" ] && echo "- \`$t\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            done <<< "$TAGS"
    
        # Verify the registry resolves the exact immutable digest emitted by
        # build-push. This preserves the publication race guard.
        - name: Verify published image digest (canonical)
          if: steps.build.outputs.digest != '' && inputs.push == 'true'
          shell: bash
          run: |
            set -euo pipefail
            IMAGE="${{ inputs.image-repo }}"
            EXPECTED="${{ steps.digest.outputs.digest }}"
            ACTUAL="$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "${IMAGE}:${{ inputs.tag }}" \
              | awk '/Digest:/ {print $2; exit}')"
            if [ "$ACTUAL" != "$EXPECTED" ]; then
              echo "::error::published digest mismatch: expected=${EXPECTED} actual=${ACTUAL}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Published digest verified: ${IMAGE}@${ACTUAL}"
    
        - name: Upload digest artifact
          if: steps.build.outputs.digest != ''
          uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
          with:
            name: worker-image-digest
            path: image-digest.txt
            if-no-files-found: error

    # ─── Stage 2: Go worker-builder ────────────────────────────────────────────
    # PR-3: this stage replaces the pre-built bin/velox-worker-agent contract.
    # It is independent of the C++ engine build, so BuildKit can execute stages
    # 1 and 2 in parallel when cache permits. The velox-shared replace CLI
    # directive in worker-agent-go/go.mod drives the resolution to the in-tree
    # shared/ tree; no ambient go.work lookup is required.
    #
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    
    ENGINE_SRC="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_SRC:-}"
    OUT_BIN="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_OUT:-/usr/local/bin/velox_video_engine}"
    BUILD_DIR="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_BUILD_DIR:-/tmp/velox-video-engine-build}"
    BUILD_JOBS="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_BUILD_JOBS:-2}"
    METADATA_DIR="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_METADATA_DIR:-/usr/local/share/velox}"
    ENGINE_SHA_FILE="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_SHA_FILE:-${METADATA_DIR}/video-engine.sha256}"
    
    echo "== Velox C++ engine build =="
    echo "Source: $ENGINE_SRC"
    echo "Output: $OUT_BIN"
    echo "Build dir: $BUILD_DIR"
    
    resolve_engine_source() {
      local candidate
      for candidate in \
        "${ENGINE_SRC}" \
        /app/native/video-engine-cpp \
        /app/RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp \
        /opt/velox/current/RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp
      do
        [ -n "$candidate" ] || continue
        if [ -d "$candidate" ]; then
          printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
          return 0
        fi
      done
      return 1
    }
    
    if [ -z "$ENGINE_SRC" ]; then
      ENGINE_SRC="$(resolve_engine_source || true)"
    fi
    
    if [ -z "$ENGINE_SRC" ] || [ ! -d "$ENGINE_SRC" ]; then
      echo "ERROR: C++ engine source directory not found. Tried /app/native/video-engine-cpp, /app/RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp and /opt/velox/current/RemoteCodex/native/video-engine-cpp" >&2
      exit 10
    fi
    
    echo "Resolved source: $ENGINE_SRC"
    
    # Clean stale artifacts from bundle (never build inside the synced dir)
    rm -rf \
        "$ENGINE_SRC/build" \
        "$ENGINE_SRC/CMakeFiles" \
        "$ENGINE_SRC/CMakeCache.txt" \
        "$ENGINE_SRC/cmake_install.cmake"
    
    # Keep the out-of-source build directory intact when it is backed by a
    # BuildKit cache mount. CMake's dependency tracking plus ccache can then
    # reuse unchanged objects between image builds; deleting this directory here
    # turned the cache mount into an expensive no-op.
    mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"
    
    if [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/CMakeLists.txt" ]; then
      echo "Detected CMake project"
    
      # Optional in-process LibAV backend (MediaProbe + packet mux). The CMake
      # default is OFF; the canonical builder opts in whenever the pinned dev
      # libraries are present so the produced engine keeps the zero-spawn probe
      # and copy-only packet pipeline. VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV overrides the
      # pkg-config detection (set to OFF for a conservative ffprobe-only build).
      if [ -z "${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV:-}" ]; then
        if pkg-config --exists libavformat libavcodec libavutil 2>/dev/null; then
          VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV=ON
        else
          VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV=OFF
        fi
      fi
      echo "LibAV in-process backend: $VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV"
    
      cmake \
          -S "$ENGINE_SRC" \
          -B "$BUILD_DIR" \
          -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache \
          -DVELOX_ENABLE_LIBAV="${VELOX_VIDEO_ENGINE_LIBAV}"
    
      cmake --build "$BUILD_DIR" --parallel "$BUILD_JOBS"
      if [ "${VELOX_SKIP_ENGINE_TESTS:-0}" != "1" ]; then
        ctest --test-dir "$BUILD_DIR" --output-on-failure
      fi
    
      if [ -f "$BUILD_DIR/velox_video_engine" ]; then
        install -m 0755 "$BUILD_DIR/velox_video_engine" "$OUT_BIN"
      elif [ -f "$BUILD_DIR/video_engine" ]; then
        install -m 0755 "$BUILD_DIR/video_engine" "$OUT_BIN"
      else
        echo "ERROR: CMake build completed but engine binary was not found" >&2
        find "$BUILD_DIR" -maxdepth 3 -type f -perm -111 -print
        exit 11
      fi
    
    elif [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/Makefile" ] || [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/makefile" ]; then
      echo "Detected Makefile project"
      make -C "$ENGINE_SRC" CC="ccache cc" CXX="ccache c++" -j"$BUILD_JOBS"
    
      if [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/velox_video_engine" ]; then
        install -m 0755 "$ENGINE_SRC/velox_video_engine" "$OUT_BIN"
      elif [ -f "$ENGINE_SRC/video_engine" ]; then
        install -m 0755 "$ENGINE_SRC/video_engine" "$OUT_BIN"
      else
        echo "ERROR: Make build completed but engine binary was not found" >&2
        find "$ENGINE_SRC" -maxdepth 3 -type f -perm -111 -print
        exit 12
      fi
    
    else
      echo "ERROR: no CMakeLists.txt or Makefile found in $ENGINE_SRC" >&2
      exit 13
    fi
    
    echo "== Built binary =="
    ls -lh "$OUT_BIN"
    file "$OUT_BIN" || true
    
    # Validate the binary against the same builder image that produced it. This
    # fails the image build before the artifact can cross into the runtime stage.

    $ sed -n '1,130p' docs/operations/fleetctl.md; sed -n '110,145p' docs/operations/worker-rollout-paths.md; rg -n 'Add.*update|update .*image|func.*Update' cmd internal/fleetctl scripts -g '*.go' | head -35
    # Fleet Operations
    
    > **Path selection:** read `docs/operations/worker-rollout-paths.md` before
    > changing a worker. The definitive production path is the FleetController API;
    > the bundle/Ansible path is retained only as a server-side migration bridge for
    > workers that have not yet reached the canonical runtime. Do not treat the
    > bridge and canonical commands as interchangeable.
    
    `scripts/fleetctl` is the operator facade for the worker fleet. It talks to
    the Master with the admin bearer token and never prints that token.
    
    ## Read and control
    
    ```bash
    export VELOX_MASTER_URL="http://MASTER:8000"
    export VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN="..."
    
    scripts/fleetctl status
    scripts/fleetctl inspect worker-id
    scripts/fleetctl inspect --json worker-id   # machine-readable WorkerCard
    scripts/fleetctl drain worker-id "prepare deployment"
    scripts/fleetctl resume worker-id "deployment complete"
    scripts/fleetctl quarantine worker-id "asset failures"
    scripts/fleetctl operations worker-id
    ```
    
    ### Inspect: IMAGE + LAST UPDATE OPERATION
    
    `fleetctl inspect <worker_id>` renders the worker card as two canonical
    sections — image state and rollout history are deliberately separate views:
    
    ```text
    IMAGE
      running_digest = sha256:337...
      target_digest  = sha256:337...
      digest_match   = true
    
    LAST UPDATE OPERATION
      status       = FAILED
      reason       = connection reset by peer
      operation_id = op_2026-08-08_...
      type         = update
      started_at   = 2026-08-08T10:11:12Z
      finished_at  = 2026-08-08T10:11:19Z
    ```
    
    A worker whose digests match is healthy even when the last rollout
    operation failed: `digest_state` no longer conflates the two (Phase A2).
    
    `--json` prints the full machine-readable WorkerCard (`image_state` /
    `operation_state`) for scripts:
    
    ```bash
    scripts/fleetctl inspect --json worker-id | jq '.image_state.digest_match'
    ```
    
    ### Worker identity
    
    `worker_id` is the immutable security identity: it is bound to the mTLS
    certificate, Master registration, leases, and job history. Use it for every
    `fleetctl` command and never replace it with a display name.
    
    `worker_name` is the mutable operator-facing name. `status` output and worker
    API cards show both values as `NAME` and `WORKER_ID`; changing `worker_name`
    must not require certificate or OpenBao changes. Display names must never be
    added to `VELOX_ALLOWED_WORKERS`.
    
    `drain`, `resume`, and `quarantine` use the canonical admin worker routes and
    return the operation ledger response. `operations` reads the audit ledger.
    The smoke command delegates to `tests/worker-cert/smoke_one.sh`, which submits
    a real asset job, waits for `SUCCEEDED`, and verifies the lease worker:
    
    ```bash
    VELOX_SMOKE_ASSET_ID=<ready-asset-id> scripts/fleetctl smoke worker-id
    ```
    
    The smoke command no longer uses a hardcoded asset. It reads the configured
    `VELOX_SMOKE_ASSET_ID`; `--asset-id <ready-asset-id>` may be used for an
    explicit one-off override.
    
    ## Digest rollout — canonical Master API
    
    `scripts/fleetctl update` and `scripts/fleetctl rollback` route through the
    canonical Master API: `POST /api/v1/admin/workers/{worker_id}/update` with the
    pinned `@sha256:` digest. There is no separate rollback route: `rollback`
    re-posts the previous-known-good digest and the Master `UpdateExecutor` owns
    the drain, cosign verification, activation and the `deployment_records` audit
    cascade.
    
    The canonical chain is:
    
    ```text
    fleetctl/API → Master → FleetController → UpdateExecutor →
    WorkerNodeRegistry → SSH → velox-worker-activate-image
    ```
    
    The worker must already be `DRAINING` with `active_jobs=0`. The command
    refuses to run otherwise.
    
    ```bash
    scripts/fleetctl update worker-id \
      ghcr.io/marcuss-ops/velox-worker@sha256:<64-hex-digest> \
      "canary release"
    ```
    
    Manual rollback uses the previously recorded pinned image reference:
    
    ```bash
    scripts/fleetctl rollback worker-id \
      ghcr.io/marcuss-ops/velox-worker@sha256:<previous-64-hex-digest> \
      "rollback after smoke failure"
    ```
    
    No `FLEET_INVENTORY`, `FLEET_ROLLOUT_PLAYBOOK`, `FLEET_ROLLOUT_BUNDLE_HASH` or
    `ansible-*` binaries are used: the release-evidence checks live server-side in
    the FleetController/UpdateExecutor gates. Both commands poll the
    `fleet_operations` ledger to terminal state (`FLEETCTL_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`,
    default 1800 s).
    
    ## Host lifecycle
    
    `restart` sends the existing authenticated worker restart command. It should
    be used only after the worker is drained and has no active jobs:
    
    ```bash
    scripts/fleetctl restart worker-id "restart after config change"
    ```
    
    Image updates, rollback and restart are performed by the Master
    (`fleet_operations` ledger + `UpdateExecutor`); direct `sudo`, SSH, and Docker
    POST /api/v1/admin/workers/{worker_id}/update
    GET  /api/v1/admin/operations/{operation_id}
    ```
    
    The direct API invocation is:
    
    > **Gate before execution:** confirm the current worker-image certification
    > manifest matches the intended commit and digest, and record its bundle hash,
    > engine SHA, executor identity/version, and signed provenance. Confirm that
    > the FleetController backends are wired and green. The command below is not a
    > substitute for those checks.
    
    ```bash
    export VELOX_MASTER_URL=https://MASTER.example.invalid:8000
    export VELOX_ADMIN_TOKEN='read-from-secure-secret-store'
    
    scripts/fleetctl status                 # read-only
    scripts/fleetctl inspect <worker_id>    # read-only
    scripts/fleetctl drain <worker_id> "canary rollout"
    # wait for the drain idle precondition (active_jobs=0), then:
    scripts/fleetctl update <worker_id> \
      ghcr.io/<owner>/velox-worker@sha256:<64-lowercase-hex> \
      "canary rollout"
    ```
    
    The definitive path must consume an immutable digest, not a version tag:
    
    ```text
    ghcr.io/<owner>/velox-worker@sha256:<64-lowercase-hex>
    ```
    
    The image must come from the current worker-image certification run. Never
    reuse a digest certified for an older commit merely because its version tag
    matches the desired version.

## Assistant

### Cosa abbiamo sistemato

Nel worker abbiamo corretto il disallineamento che causava l’errore:

`cached asset not found: stock-sha256-…`

Il piano identificava lo stock con un ID canonico, ma la cache e il sistema di lease potevano cercarlo con una chiave diversa. Ora il worker mantiene la stessa identità dell’asset tra piano, risoluzione, cache e prenotazione del job, usando `drive_file_id` come localizzatore per la sorgente Drive.

La modifica è stata testata, inclusa nella build e certificata. L’immagine è stata installata sul worker `host_57_129_132_133`; il Master conferma che è `CONNECTED`, `HEALTHY`, inattivo e con il digest aggiornato. Gli altri worker risultano ancora disconnessi o in quarantena, come prima.

### Cosa non abbiamo ancora dimostrato

**Non abbiamo ancora verificato un job completo con questa nuova immagine.** Il job r39 fallito è precedente all’aggiornamento del worker. Nel computer attuale non ci sono il suo payload e lo script che lo inviava; inoltre `pipelinegen.service` non è installato qui. Per questo non ho potuto rilanciare il job.

### Cosa resta da fare

1. Recuperare il payload r39 aggiornato, o il checkout del Producer che lo genera.
2. Inviarlo senza download, taglio o ricodifica stock lato Producer.
3. Verificare che il worker scarichi gli stock da Drive, li trovi in cache sotto l’identità del piano e completi l’assemblaggio in packet copy.
4. Controllare il video finale e i log, così da confermare che non ci siano ricodifiche né frammenti stock prodotti localmente.

Quindi il fix del worker è installato; resta da provare il flusso reale Producer → Master → worker.

## Assistant

È un problema di **taglio nel punto sbagliato**.

Il Producer passa al worker il video stock intero, ma il piano gli chiede di usarne solo una finestra: per `segment-0003`, 13 frame a partire da 4,475 s. Quel punto cade dentro un GOP, quindi non corrisponde a un frammento certificato copiabile così com’è.

Il worker attuale, `video.assemble.copy.v1`, sa concatenare frammenti già preparati e verificati; **non sa estrarre finestre arbitrarie dal file intero**. Perciò rifiuta la validazione prima di assemblare. Cache e identità ora funzionano: i 190 asset sono arrivati e il precedente errore “asset non trovato” è risolto.

Per chiudere il flusso senza lavorazione locale, serve un executor remoto che riceva le sorgenti Drive e prepari le finestre richieste. Se non si vuole introdurre questo percorso nel worker, l’alternativa è far arrivare al worker frammenti già certificati; con il vincolo che hai dato, però, quella preparazione deve avvenire a valle del Producer.

## User

cioè io non ti posso ancora dare una carteallc on dentor i file drive e lu scaricahi e l imonti random per quale motivo ?

## Assistant

Sì, puoi dare una cartella Drive. Il problema non è la cartella: **il worker non è ancora programmato per usarla nel modo che descrivi**.

Oggi il piano seleziona file e finestre precise, per esempio «dal file X usa 13 frame a partire da 4,475 s». Il worker `video.assemble.copy.v1` controlla che ogni segmento corrisponda esattamente a un frammento già certificato e copiabile. Il file Drive intero non corrisponde a quella finestra, quindi il controllo lo rifiuta.

Per ottenere il flusso «leggi la cartella, scegli stock a caso, mettili in sequenza e concatena», va cambiato il contratto del job e va aggiunto un executor remoto che:

1. riceve l’ID della cartella e le regole di durata e montaggio;
2. elenca i video e ne verifica codec e keyframe;
3. sceglie clip copiabili, per esempio iniziando da un keyframe;
4. li concatena senza ricodificare;
5. completa il video e registra quali clip ha scelto.

Quel comportamento non è implementato dal fix della cache: quel fix fa trovare i file al worker, ma non gli insegna a inventare la sequenza né a tagliare finestre arbitrarie. Perciò r40 si ferma correttamente in validazione prima di assemblare.

## User

1. riceve l’ID della cartella e le regole di durata e montaggio;
2. elenca i video e ne verifica codec e keyframe; allora nel nostro sotkc noi abbiaom già questo nel senso crea la cartelald rive con codece e keyframe uguali quindi non serve ancora rifalrie sempre tu o meglio il remoto dovrebbe solo scaircear e concatenare senza fare pprobe o cose ripetute o stupide

## Assistant

Hai ragione: se la cartella è già normalizzata con codec, timebase e keyframe compatibili, ripetere probe e controlli su ogni file a ogni job è lavoro duplicato. Sto verificando dove il piano trasforma quei file interi in finestre parziali, perché è lì che nasce la richiesta impossibile di tagliare a 4,475 s; il worker deve poter consumare la pool preparata come clip intere e concatenabili.

    Il client M2M di polling dispone dello scope:
    
    ```
    jobs.submit
    ```
    
    ## Invio di un job
    
    Il contratto canonico attualmente attivo per `POST /api/v1/jobs` è
    `SubmitJobRequest`: il client invia i campi tipizzati direttamente nel body.
    Il producer deve inviare il `CompiledRenderPlanV2` completo nei due campi top-level
    `compiled_render_plan_json` e `compiled_render_plan_sha256`. Il Master conserva
    quei byte e li valida. I piani con `stock_pool` (folder Drive, selezione
    `shuffle` e segmenti `stock_pool_slot`) vengono instradati automaticamente a
    `video.assemble.slice.v1`. Il Master enumera il folder e passa al worker i
    riferimenti e i metadati; non scarica, non prepara e non pre-riscalda i file del
    pool. Il worker li risolve nella propria cache, verifica che il materiale sia
    compatibile con il profilo H.264 dichiarato, riempie gli slot casualmente e
    concatena video e audio con stream copy. La preparazione anticipata resta per
    overlay, clip e audio fissi. Se i file del pool hanno profili o parametri H.264
    incompatibili, il job fallisce senza ricodifica.
    
    Per usare il pool con stream copy, il folder deve essere omogeneo rispetto al
    profilo del piano, inclusi livello H.264, timebase e codec extradata (SPS/PPS).
    Non basta che i file siano tutti MP4 o H.264: per esempio, un pool con livelli
    4.0 e 4.1 non è concatenabile secondo il profilo `VELOX_ASSEMBLY_READY_V1`.
    I piani senza `stock_pool` mantengono il percorso copy per asset già certificati.
    Il Master non compila un piano alternativo e non deduce il profilo dal flag del
    worker.

    . /path/to/computer-editor-77-01.env

    IDEMPOTENCY_KEY="matt-damon-5-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
    PLAN_JSON=/path/to/compiled-render-plan-v2.json
    PLAN_SHA256="$(sha256sum "$PLAN_JSON" | awk '{print $1}')"

    // videoAssembleSliceExecutor copies compatible source packets from verified
    // runtime assets in the worker cache into the final mux. It never encodes.
    type videoAssembleSliceExecutor struct {
        runner     *pipeline.Runner
        prober     sliceMediaProber
        outputRoot string
    }
    
    type sliceMediaProber interface {
        ProbeMediaDetails(context.Context, string) (publisher.MediaProbe, error)
    }
    
    type ffprobeSliceMediaProber struct{}
    
    func (ffprobeSliceMediaProber) ProbeMediaDetails(ctx context.Context, path string) (publisher.MediaProbe, error) {
        return publisher.ProbeMediaDetails(ctx, path)
    }
    
    func NewVideoAssembleSlice(outputRoot string, runner *pipeline.Runner) executor.Executor {
        if strings.TrimSpace(outputRoot) == "" {
            outputRoot = filepath.Join(os.TempDir(), "velox", "video-assemble-slice")
        }
        return &videoAssembleSliceExecutor{runner: runner, prober: ffprobeSliceMediaProber{}, outputRoot: outputRoot}
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) Descriptor() executor.Descriptor {
        return executor.Descriptor{
            ID: VideoAssembleSliceID, Version: VideoAssembleSliceVersion,
            InputTypes: []string{"render.compiled.v2.drive"}, OutputTypes: []string{"video/mp4"},
            ResourceClass: executor.ResourceCPU, Deterministic: true, Cacheable: true,
            TemporalMode: executor.TemporalGlobal,
        }
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) Validate(spec executor.TaskSpec) error {
        if spec.ExecutorID != VideoAssembleSliceID {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: executor_id must be %q", VideoAssembleSliceID)
        }
        if e == nil || e.runner == nil || e.runner.RenderClient() == nil {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: native packet-copy renderer is not configured")
        }
        if e.prober == nil {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: FFprobe media validation is not configured")
        }
        plan, err := decodeCompiledPlanV2(spec)
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: invalid CompiledRenderPlanV2: %w", err)
        }
        if _, err := contract.KnownCanonicalVideoProfileV1(plan.Output.ProfileID); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: canonical output profile required: %w", err)
        }
        assets := make(map[string]contract.AssetRefV2, len(plan.Assets))
        runtimeDriveIDs := sliceRuntimeDriveFileIDs(spec.Payload["runtime_assets"])
        hasDrive := plan.StockPool != nil
        for _, asset := range plan.Assets {
            assets[asset.AssetID] = asset
            driveSource := asset.Kind == "video" && isSliceDriveSource(asset, runtimeDriveIDs)
            hasDrive = hasDrive || driveSource
        }
        if !hasDrive {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: plan must contain at least one Drive video source")
        }
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || (len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) == 0 && plan.StockPool == nil) {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: exactly one video track is required; segments or stock_pool must be supplied")
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil {
            members := 0
            for _, item := range sliceRuntimePoolMembers(spec.Payload["runtime_assets"]) {
                if item.StockPoolMember && strings.TrimSpace(item.DriveFileID) != "" {
                    members++
                }
            }
            if members == 0 {
                return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: Master did not resolve any stock_pool files")
            }
        }
        var nextFrame int64
        stockPoolSlots := 0
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            if segment.StockPoolSlot {
                if plan.StockPool == nil {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q has stock_pool_slot without stock_pool", segment.SegmentID)
                }
                stockPoolSlots++
                if segment.FrameCount <= 0 {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: stock pool slot %q has invalid frame count", segment.SegmentID)
                }
            } else {
                asset, ok := assets[segment.AssetID]
                if !ok || (asset.Kind != "video" && asset.Kind != "prepared_video_fragment") {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q must reference a video asset", segment.SegmentID)
                }
                if asset.ProfileID != plan.Output.ProfileID || asset.FrameCount <= 0 || !asset.FirstFrameKeyframe || !asset.ClosedGOP {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: asset %q is not certified for packet-copy assembly", segment.AssetID)
                }
                if segment.SourceInUS != 0 {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q starts at a non-keyframe offset (%d us); packet-copy is unsafe", segment.SegmentID, segment.SourceInUS)
                }
                if segment.FrameCount <= 0 || segment.FrameCount > asset.FrameCount {
                    return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q frame count %d exceeds certified source frames %d", segment.SegmentID, segment.FrameCount, asset.FrameCount)
                }
            }
            if segment.TimelineStartFrame != nextFrame {
                return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: segment %q leaves a timeline gap or overlap at frame %d", segment.SegmentID, nextFrame)
            }
            nextFrame += segment.FrameCount
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil && stockPoolSlots == 0 {
            return errors.New("video.assemble.slice.v1: stock_pool requires at least one stock slot")
        }
        framesNum := int64(plan.DurationUS) * int64(plan.Output.FPSNum)
        framesDen := int64(plan.Output.FPSDen) * 1_000_000
        wantFrames := (framesNum + framesDen - 1) / framesDen
        if nextFrame != wantFrames {
            return fmt.Errorf("video.assemble.slice.v1: timeline has %d frames, plan duration requires %d", nextFrame, wantFrames)
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    func (e *videoAssembleSliceExecutor) Execute(ctx context.Context, execCtx executor.ExecutionContext, spec executor.TaskSpec) (executor.ExecutionResult, error) {
        started := time.Now().UTC()
        fail := func(code string, err error) (executor.ExecutionResult, error) {
            return executor.ExecutionResult{Status: "failed", ErrorCode: code, ErrorDetail: err.Error(), StartedAt: started, CompletedAt: time.Now().UTC()}, nil
        }
        if err := e.Validate(spec); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID", err)
        }
        plan, _ := decodeCompiledPlanV2(spec)
        bindings, ok := runtimeassets.FromContext(ctx)
        if !ok {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_MISSING", errors.New("verified runtime asset bindings are required"))
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil {
            compiled, err := e.compileStockPoolPlan(ctx, spec, plan, bindings)
            if err != nil {
                return fail("DRIVE_STOCK_POOL_INCOMPATIBLE", err)
            }
            plan = compiled
        }
        if err := validateCopyOnlyPlan(plan); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID", err)
        }
        audio, ok := bindings[plan.FinalAudio.AssetID]
        if !ok || !audio.Verified || audio.Size <= 0 || audio.SHA256 == "" || audio.SHA256 != plan.FinalAudio.SHA256 || audio.Size != plan.FinalAudio.SizeBytes {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_INVALID", errors.New("final audio integrity binding does not match the plan"))
        }
        if info, statErr := os.Stat(audio.Path); statErr != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Size() != audio.Size {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_ASSETS_INVALID", errors.New("final audio local file identity is invalid"))
        }
        jobID, err := safeOutputJobID(spec.JobID)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("INVALID_JOB_ID", err)
        }
        outputPath := filepath.Join(e.outputRoot, jobID+".mp4")
        if resolver := storageResolverFromExecutionContext(execCtx); resolver != nil {
            if placement, placeErr := resolver.Place(storage.ArtifactStaging, jobID+".mp4", estimateOutputBytesFromDuration(plan.DurationUS)); placeErr == nil {
                outputPath = placement.Path
            }
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(outputPath), 0o750); err != nil {
            return fail("OUTPUT_DIRECTORY", err)
        }
        wire, err := marshalCopyOnlyWire(plan, spec.JobID, outputPath, bindings)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID", err)
        }
        metrics, renderErr := e.runner.RenderCompiledPlanV2(ctx, wire, outputPath)
        if renderErr != nil {
            return fail(copyOnlyRenderErrorCode(renderErr), renderErr)
        }
        if err := e.verifyFinalMedia(ctx, outputPath, plan); err != nil {
            return fail("DRIVE_SLICE_OUTPUT_INVALID", err)
        }
        artifact, err := artifactFromFile("video/mp4", outputPath)
        if err != nil {
            return fail("FINAL_OUTPUT_INVALID", err)
        }
        raw := copyOnlyRawMetrics(plan, metrics, artifact)
        return executor.ExecutionResult{
            Status: "succeeded", Outputs: []executor.ArtifactRef{artifact}, RawMetrics: raw,
            Segments: projectSegments(metrics), DetailedPhases: projectDetailedPhases(metrics),
            StartedAt: started, CompletedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
        }, nil
    }
    
    type slicePoolMember struct {
        AssetID         string `json:"asset_id"`
        DriveFileID     string `json:"drive_file_id"`
        SizeBytes       int64  `json:"size_bytes"`
        DurationMS      int64  `json:"duration_ms"`

    }
    
    func sliceRuntimePoolMembers(raw interface{}) []slicePoolMember {
        data, err := json.Marshal(raw)
        if err != nil {
            return nil
        }
        var members []slicePoolMember
        _ = json.Unmarshal(data, &members)
        return members
    }

    // resolveCompiledRenderPlanAssets is an adapter/orchestrator around the
    // existing common asset resolver. It deliberately does not download bytes or
    // write cache rows itself: resolveCommonAssetPayload owns that verified path.
    //
    // The synthetic payload exists only in memory so the common resolver can
    // consume the typed V2 references. Local paths returned by that resolver are
    // projected into runtimeassets.Bindings and never written back into the
    // canonical CompiledRenderPlanV2 JSON.
    func (w *Worker) resolveCompiledRenderPlanAssets(ctx context.Context, payload map[string]interface{}) (runtimeassets.Bindings, error) {
        if payload == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: payload is required")
        }
        plan, err := contract.DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2Payload(payload)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: decode: %w", err)
        }
        if plan == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: %q is required", contract.PayloadKeyCompiledRenderPlanJSON)
        }
    
        // This structure is an adapter input, not a replacement plan. The
        // resolver understands the existing asset envelope and returns verified
        // worker-local paths for each uri. AssetKey is the canonical cache/transfer
        // identity when supplied; AssetID remains the stable plan/binding identity.
        planAssets := append([]contract.AssetRefV2(nil), plan.Assets...)
        // Folder members are a Master-resolved runtime snapshot, not editorial
        // per-file assignments in the immutable plan. Resolve them through the same
        // verified cache path as every other V2 asset.
        var runtimePool []struct {
            AssetID         string `json:"asset_id"`
            DriveFileID     string `json:"drive_file_id"`
            SizeBytes       int64  `json:"size_bytes"`
            DurationMS      int64  `json:"duration_ms"`
            StockPoolMember bool   `json:"stock_pool_member"`
        }
        if raw, marshalErr := json.Marshal(payload["runtime_assets"]); marshalErr == nil {
            _ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &runtimePool)
        }
        if plan.StockPool != nil {
            var framesNeeded int64
            for _, track := range plan.VideoTracks {
                for _, segment := range track.Segments {
                    if segment.StockPoolSlot {
                        framesNeeded += segment.FrameCount
                    }
                }
            }
            if framesNeeded <= 0 {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiled render plan v2: stock_pool has no positive slot duration")
            }
            pool := make([]struct {
                AssetID         string `json:"asset_id"`
                DriveFileID     string `json:"drive_file_id"`
                SizeBytes       int64  `json:"size_bytes"`
                DurationMS      int64  `json:"duration_ms"`
                StockPoolMember bool   `json:"stock_pool_member"`
            }, 0, len(runtimePool))
            for _, item := range runtimePool {
                if item.StockPoolMember && item.DurationMS > 0 && item.SizeBytes > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(item.DriveFileID) != "" {
                    pool = append(pool, item)
                }
            }
            seed := time.Now().UnixNano()
            if plan.TimelineSHA256 != "" {

                    Kind: "video", SizeBytes: item.SizeBytes,

                }

    package pipeline
    
    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
    
        "velox-shared/assetref"
        "velox-shared/contract"
    )
    
    // resolveStockPoolRuntimeAssets is the one V2 folder-resolution boundary.
    // It lists metadata only; media bytes remain worker-owned transfers.
    func (h *Handlers) resolveStockPoolRuntimeAssets(ctx context.Context, req *SubmitJobRequest) error {
        if req == nil || req.CompiledRenderPlanJSON == "" {
            return nil
        }
        plan, err := contract.DecodeCompiledRenderPlanV2([]byte(req.CompiledRenderPlanJSON))
        if err != nil {
            return nil // Canonical plan validation returns the structured V2 error later.
        }
        if plan.StockPool == nil {
            return nil
        }
        if h.stockFolderLister == nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("stock_pool requires the Master Drive folder-listing capability")
        }
        folderURL := "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/" + plan.StockPool.DriveFolderID
        folderID, err := assetref.ParseDriveFolderID(folderURL)
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        files, err := listStockFolderVideos(ctx, h.stockFolderLister, folderID.String(), 0, make(map[string]struct{}))
        if err != nil {
            return err
        }
        if len(files) == 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("stock_pool Drive folder contains no video files")
        }
        runtimeAssets := append([]map[string]interface{}(nil), req.RuntimeAssets...)
        seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(runtimeAssets)+len(files))
        for _, asset := range runtimeAssets {
            if id, ok := asset["asset_id"].(string); ok {
                seen[id] = struct{}{}
            }
        }
        for _, file := range files {
            if _, exists := seen[file.ID]; exists {
                continue
            }
            asset := map[string]interface{}{
                "asset_id": file.ID, "asset_key": file.ID, "drive_file_id": file.ID,
                "url":        "velox-drive://" + file.ID,
                "source_uri": "https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=" + file.ID,
                "kind":       "video", "stock_pool_member": true,
            }
            if file.Size > 0 {
                asset["size_bytes"] = file.Size
            }
            if file.VideoMediaMetadata.DurationMillis > 0 {
                asset["duration_ms"] = file.VideoMediaMetadata.DurationMillis
            }
            runtimeAssets = append(runtimeAssets, asset)
            seen[file.ID] = struct{}{}
        }
        req.RuntimeAssets = runtimeAssets
        // Ensure downstream payload projection sees the stable snapshot. The plan
        // remains byte-for-byte hash-bound; retries reuse the accepted runtime list.
        return nil
    }

    func resolveInternalExecutorID(payloadMap map[string]interface{}) string {
        if !compiledRenderPlanV2Present(payloadMap) {
            return ""
        }
        if executorID := contract.RequiredVideoAssemblyExecutor(payloadMap); executorID != "" {
            return executorID + "@1"
        }
        return canonicalCompiledPlanExecutor
    }
    
    func resolveRequiredCapabilities(executorID string) []string {
        if strings.HasPrefix(executorID, "video.assemble.copy.v1") || strings.HasPrefix(executorID, "video.assemble.slice.v1") {
            return []string{"artifact.commit.v1"}
        }
        return nil
    }

        h := sha256.New()

                if trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(value); trimmed != "" {
                    h.Write([]byte(trimmed))

    ## Asset rule
    
    Do not send local creator paths such as `C:\clips\video.mp4` or `/home/creator/audio.mp3`. Subworkers cannot read another computer's filesystem. Every voiceover, stock clip, image and subtitle reference must be either:
    
    - a `velox-asset://` reference already resolvable by the master; or
    - an HTTP(S) URL reachable by the master and workers.
    
    For a stock pool, `scenes[].stock` may contain one Drive folder reference:
    
    ```json
    "stock": [
      {"url": "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/<FOLDER_ID>"}
    ]
    ```
