    // Runtime-asset resolution for the remote final job: the identity cache, the
    // stock staging and its receipts, and the prefetch lanes that keep handoff
    // from re-resolving one source per fragment.
    
    // resolverClock accumulates the runtime-asset resolution time of one handoff.
    // It answers the only question the receipt could not: how much of handoff_ms is
    // spent finding and publishing sources rather than encoding fragments.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolverClock() func() {
        started := time.Now()
        return func() {
            if a != nil {
                a.resolverNS.Add(time.Since(started).Nanoseconds())
            }
        }
    }
    
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) ResolveFinalJobAsset(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        return a.resolveOnce("objectstore:"+strings.TrimSpace(id), func() (map[string]any, error) {
            defer a.resolverClock()()
            started := time.Now()
            ref, err := a.ResolveFinalJobObjectStoreAsset(ctx, id)
            log.Printf("final_job resolve kind=objectstore id=%s bytes=%v ms=%d err=%v",
                id, ref["size_bytes"], time.Since(started).Milliseconds(), err != nil)
            return ref, err
        })
    }
    
    // resolveOnce answers a repeated resolution from the handoff's own cache. The
    // cached reference is copied on the way out so a caller cannot mutate the entry
    // (the payload builder stamps roles and durations onto the map it receives).
    //
    // Concurrent callers of the SAME identity share one resolution (single flight):
    // the prefetch warms a folder while the walk asks for the file it needs, and
    // without this the prefetch would be duplicated work instead of saved work.
    // An error is never cached — a failed warm-up must not poison the walk.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolveOnce(key string, build func() (map[string]any, error)) (map[string]any, error) {
        if a == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job adapter is not configured")
        }
        a.resolvedMu.Lock()
        if cached, ok := a.resolved[key]; ok {
            a.hits++
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
            return copyFinalJobRef(cached), nil
        }
        a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
    
        a.inflightMu.Lock()
        if call, ok := a.inflight[key]; ok {
            a.inflightMu.Unlock()
            <-call.done
            if call.err != nil {
                return nil, call.err
            }
            a.resolvedMu.Lock()
            a.hits++
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
            return copyFinalJobRef(call.ref), nil
        }
        if a.inflight == nil {
            a.inflight = make(map[string]*finalJobResolveCall, 16)
        }
        call := &finalJobResolveCall{done: make(chan struct{})}
        a.inflight[key] = call
        a.inflightMu.Unlock()
    
        func() {
            defer close(call.done)
            defer func() {
                a.inflightMu.Lock()
                delete(a.inflight, key)
                a.inflightMu.Unlock()
            }()
            call.ref, call.err = build()
            if call.err != nil {
                return
            }
            a.resolvedMu.Lock()
            if a.resolved == nil {
                a.resolved = make(map[string]map[string]any, 16)
            }
            a.resolved[key] = copyFinalJobRef(call.ref)
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        }()
        if call.err != nil {
            return nil, call.err
        }
        return copyFinalJobRef(call.ref), nil
    }
    
    const (
        // defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency is how many Drive sources one handoff
        // resolves at a time. It is 1 because concurrency was MEASURED and it loses
        // on this stack: serial r69/r73 cost ~190 ms per source (61 sources = 10,9 s
        // of the handoff), while a 64-file warm-up at 6 workers paid 576 ms per
        // source on average (max 2.068 ms) and turned the same handoff into 49,5 s.
        // The per-call cost triples under load — the path is throughput bound, not
        // latency bound — so parallelising it multiplies work instead of hiding it.
        // The knob stays so a future stack fix can be measured against this table.
        defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency = 1
        // maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency bounds the operator knob: beyond this the
        // handoff is no longer latency bound and a folder listing becomes a spike.
        maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency = 16
        // finalJobPrefetchPerFolder caps how many of one folder's files a prefetch
        // warms. It is a WINDOW, not a sample: the folder cursor consumes the list
        // in order, so warming the head of the list is exactly what the walk asks
        // for next (r73: a 240-file folder, 61 of them consumed, 12 warmed → 10,9 s
        // still spent on the critical path). 64 covers a long timeline at ~5 s per
        // source while costing ceil(64/6)·190 ms ≈ 2 s of wall instead of 64·190 ms.
        // A folder of hundreds is never resolved wholesale.
        finalJobPrefetchPerFolder = 64
    )
    
    // finalJobResolveConcurrency reads VELOX_FINAL_JOB_RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY. Absent
    // means the measured default, 1 means the pre-2026-11-01 serial handoff, and a
    // malformed value degrades to serial rather than inventing parallelism.
    func finalJobResolveConcurrency() int {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency
        }
        value, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || value < 1 {
            return 1
        }
        if value > maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency {
            return maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency
        }
        return value
    }
    
    // PrewarmFinalJobStockSources is the capability the scripts runner calls while
    // the overlay render is still running (FinalJobSourcePrewarmer). It walks the
    // FINAL JOB's own stock selection through the same planner the payload build
    // uses, so the identities it resolves are exactly the ones the handoff would
    // have resolved serially, and the handoff then answers them from this cache.
    //
    // It never fails the run: the error is returned for the log, and the handoff
    // re-walks the same selection and reports its own error.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx context.Context, runID string, req scriptgen.GenerateRequest, result *scriptgen.GenerateResult) error {
        if a == nil || result == nil {
            return nil
        }
        // The prewarm owns the cache of THIS run; StartFinalJob keeps it because it
        // sees the same run id.
        a.beginHandoffCache(runID)
        started := time.Now()
        windows, err := scriptgen.PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx, result, a)
        a.resolvedMu.Lock()
        unique := len(a.resolved)
        a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        log.Printf("final_job prewarm kind=stock windows=%d unique_resolved=%d wall_ms=%d err=%v",
            windows, unique, time.Since(started).Milliseconds(), err)
        return err
    }
    
    // beginHandoffCache scopes the per-handoff resolution cache to ONE run without
    // throwing away what a prewarm of the SAME run already resolved.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) beginHandoffCache(runID string) {
        if a == nil {
            return
        }
        runID = strings.TrimSpace(runID)
        a.resolvedMu.Lock()
        defer a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        if a.resolvedRunID == runID && a.resolved != nil {
            return
        }
        a.resolvedRunID = runID
        a.resolved = nil
        a.hits = 0
    }
    
    // PrefetchFinalJobStockAssets warms the handoff cache for the Drive sources one
    // stock folder is about to offer. It returns when every requested identity has
    // been attempted (or the context ended), and it never reports an error: a
    // source that cannot be warmed is resolved — and reported — by the walk.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) PrefetchFinalJobStockAssets(ctx context.Context, ids []string) {
        a.prefetchFinalJobSources(ctx, ids, a.ResolveFinalJobStockAsset)
    }
    
    // prefetchFinalJobSources is the scheduling half of the prefetch: dedupe, skip
    // what the cache already holds, then resolve with a bounded pool. The resolver
    // is a parameter so the scheduling is testable without a Drive or an object
    // store.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) prefetchFinalJobSources(ctx context.Context, ids []string, resolve func(context.Context, string) (map[string]any, error)) {
        if a == nil || resolve == nil {
            return
        }
        workers := finalJobResolveConcurrency()
        if workers <= 1 {
            return
        }
        unique := make([]string, 0, len(ids))
        seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(ids))
        for _, raw := range ids {
            id := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
            if id == "" {
                continue
            }
            if _, ok := seen[id]; ok {
                continue
            }
            seen[id] = struct{}{}
            a.resolvedMu.Lock()
            _, cached := a.resolved["drive:"+id]
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
            if cached {
                continue
            }
            unique = append(unique, id)
            if len(unique) == finalJobPrefetchPerFolder {
                break
            }
        }
        if len(unique) == 0 {
            return
        }
        if len(unique) < workers {
            workers = len(unique)
        }
        started := time.Now()
        log.Printf("final_job prefetch kind=drive requested=%d warm=%d workers=%d", len(ids), len(unique), workers)
        queue := make(chan string)
        var wg sync.WaitGroup
        for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
            wg.Add(1)
            _ = tmp.Close()
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("download stock Drive file %q: %w", id, err)
        }
        written, copyErr := io.Copy(tmp, reader)
        readerErr := reader.Close()
        fileErr := tmp.Close()
        if copyErr != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("copy stock Drive file %q: %w", id, copyErr)
        }
        if readerErr != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("close stock Drive response %q: %w", id, readerErr)
        }
        if fileErr != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("close staged stock file %q: %w", id, fileErr)
        }
        if written != size {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("stock Drive file %q downloaded %d bytes, expected %d", id, written, size)
        }
        if err := os.Rename(tmpPath, cached); err != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("commit stock cache entry %q: %w", cached, err)
        }
        return cached, func() {}, nil
    }
    
    // ResolveFinalJobStockAsset retains the explicitly allowed Drive path for
    // selected stock-folder videos. Every other final-job asset goes through the
    // HTTPS Objectstore resolver above.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) ResolveFinalJobStockAsset(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        return a.resolveOnce("drive:"+strings.TrimSpace(id), func() (map[string]any, error) {
            return a.resolveStockAssetOnce(ctx, id)
        })
    }
    
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolveStockAssetOnce(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        defer a.resolverClock()()
        started := time.Now()
        defer func() {
            log.Printf("final_job resolve kind=drive id=%s ms=%d", id, time.Since(started).Milliseconds())
        }()
        if a == nil || a.stock == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job stock Drive reader is not configured")
        }
        id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
        if id == "" || strings.ContainsAny(id, "/\\\x00\r\n") {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job stock Drive id is invalid")
        }
        meta, err := a.stock.GetFileMeta(ctx, id)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("read stock Drive metadata %q: %w", id, err)
        }
        if meta == nil || meta.Size <= 0 {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("stock Drive file %q has no positive byte size", id)
        }
    
        path, cleanup, err := a.stagedStockPath(ctx, id, meta.Size)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        defer cleanup()
        // A staged stock file is written once, by us, from the Drive bytes of that
        // exact id and size — the same identity the staging cache already trusts to
        // serve the file without downloading it again. Hashing, probing and signing
        // those same bytes on every later handoff is therefore repeated work, not
        // verification: the receipt written next to the file answers all three.
        // Fail-closed: a receipt that does not describe exactly this file is dropped
        // and the bytes are re-derived.
        if receipt, ok := readFinalJobStockReceipt(path, meta.Size); ok {
            ref, publishErr := scriptgen.PublishFinalJobLocalObjectVerified(ctx, "stock-sha256-"+receipt.SHA256[:24], path, receipt.SHA256, receipt.SizeBytes)
            if publishErr == nil {
                ref["duration_ms"] = receipt.DurationMS
                return ref, nil
            }
        }
        hash, size, err := digest.SHA256File(path)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("hash stock Drive file %q: %w", id, err)
        }
        if a.probe == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("canonical media probe is not configured")
        }
        info, probeErr := a.probe.Probe(ctx, path)
        if info == nil || !info.HasVideo {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("probe stock Drive video %q: video stream is missing", id)
        }
        resolved := asset.ResolveAssetDuration(info.Duration.Microseconds(), probeErr, 0, false)
        if !resolved.Known() {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("probe stock Drive video %q: duration is unknown: %w", id, probeErr)
        }
        durationMS := resolved.DurationUS / 1000
        assetID := "stock-sha256-" + hash[:24]
        ref, err := scriptgen.PublishFinalJobLocalObject(ctx, assetID, path, hash, size)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("publish stock Drive file %q to HTTPS Objectstore: %w", id, err)
        }
        ref["duration_ms"] = durationMS
        writeFinalJobStockReceipt(path, finalJobStockReceipt{SHA256: hash, SizeBytes: size, DurationMS: durationMS})
        return ref, nil
    }
    
    // finalJobStockReceipt is what resolving a staged stock file produced: its
    // content address and the duration the probe reported. It is bound to the exact
    // staged file (size) so a re-downloaded or replaced file can never be served
    // from a stale receipt.
    type finalJobStockReceipt struct {
        SHA256     string `json:"sha256"`
    package scriptgeneration
    
    import (
        "context"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "math"
        "strings"
        "sync"
    
        "github.com/Marcuss-ops/PipelineGen/internal/kernel/digest"
        kernelmedia "github.com/Marcuss-ops/PipelineGen/internal/kernel/media"
    )
    
    // prepareFinalJobVideoSegments replaces source-video references with verified
    // assembly-ready fragments. It keeps audio as a single copy asset and drops
    // every unused source video from FINALIZE, so the remote worker's work is only
    // packet-copy placement plus final audio mux.
    func prepareFinalJobVideoSegments(ctx context.Context, rawPlan string, runtimeAssets []any, preparer FinalJobVideoSegmentPreparer) (string, []any, error) {
        if preparer == nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job requires a local video-segment preparer; refusing to send unprepared sources")
        }
        var plan finalJobCompiledPlan
        if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rawPlan), &plan); err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("decode final_job compiled plan before segment preparation: %w", err)
        }
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) == 0 {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment preparation requires one non-empty video track")
        }
        refs := make(map[string]map[string]any, len(runtimeAssets))
        for index, raw := range runtimeAssets {
            asset, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
            if !ok {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %d has an invalid shape", index)
            }
            id := finalJobStringValue(asset["asset_id"])
            if id == "" {
                continue
            }
            if prior := refs[id]; prior != nil && !sameFinalJobAssetIdentity(prior, asset) {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %q has conflicting source references", id)
            }
            refs[id] = asset
        }
    
        preparedAssets := make(map[string]finalJobPlanAsset, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments)+1)
        preparedRefs := make([]any, 0, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments)+1)
        // Phase 1 — validate every binding and describe the work. This is cheap and
        // sequential, and it fails before any expensive preparation starts.
        work := make([]finalJobSegmentWork, 0, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments))
        for index := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            segment := &plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[index]
            source := refs[segment.AssetID]
            if source == nil {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q has no runtime source asset %q", segment.SegmentID, segment.AssetID)
            }
            if !strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(source["sha256"]), segment.SHA256) {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q source SHA-256 does not match the compiled plan", segment.SegmentID)
            }
            work = append(work, finalJobSegmentWork{
                index:  index,
                source: source,
                request: FinalJobVideoSegmentRequest{
                    SegmentID: segment.SegmentID, SourceAssetID: segment.AssetID, SourceSHA256: segment.SHA256,
                    SourceInUS: segment.SourceInUS, SourceDurationUS: segment.SourceDurationUS,
                    TimelineStartFrame: segment.TimelineStartFrame, FrameCount: segment.FrameCount,
                    TimelineRevision: plan.TimelineRevision, TimelineSHA256: plan.TimelineSHA256,
                },
            })
        }
        // Phase 2 — prepare the fragments. They are independent, so they run on the
        // preparer's lanes; the result is indexed by plan position, which keeps the
        // binding deterministic whatever the completion order is.
        prepared, err := finalJobPrepareSegments(ctx, preparer, work)
        if err != nil {
            return "", nil, err
        }
        // Phase 3 — bind in plan order, ONE asset per placement. The assembler
        // certifies each placement against the manifest of its OWN asset
        // (`segment "…" manifest binding is not exact` — r66), so two placements can
        // never share one object even when their pixels are identical. The
        // collision is resolved on the OBJECT, never on the binding: the later
        // placement is re-prepared with a placement tag (same pictures, different
        // container, different bytes), which satisfies both the plan's unique
        // canonical identity and the assembler's per-placement certificate.
        usedSHA := make(map[string]string, len(work))
        usedURI := make(map[string]string, len(work))
        for _, item := range work {
            segment := &plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[item.index]
            source := item.source
            asset, ref, err := finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(prepared[item.index], item.request)
            if err != nil {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared final_job segment %q: %w", segment.SegmentID, err)
            }
            if _, exists := usedSHA[asset.SHA256]; exists {
                // Identical bytes for a second placement. Derive THIS placement from
                // the certified object already produced above: the same bitstream in
                // a distinct container is a naming problem, and re-encoding the same
                // window would pay for pixels that already exist. The tag stays in
                // the work identity, so the tagged object can never be answered with
                // the untagged bytes.
                item.request.PlacementTag = segment.SegmentID
                item.request.ReuseFromSHA256 = asset.SHA256
                item.request.ReuseFromURI = usedURI[asset.SHA256]
                tagged, tagErr := preparer.PrepareFinalJobVideoSegment(ctx, source, item.request)
                if tagErr != nil {
                    return "", nil, finalJobSegmentPrepareError(item, tagErr)
                }
                asset, ref, err = finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(tagged, item.request)
                if err != nil {
                    return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared final_job segment %q: %w", segment.SegmentID, err)
                }
                if other, stillShared := usedSHA[asset.SHA256]; stillShared {
                    return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q still certifies the bytes of another placement (%q); refusing to send a plan the assembler must reject", segment.SegmentID, other)
                }
            }
            usedSHA[asset.SHA256] = segment.SegmentID
            usedURI[asset.SHA256] = finalJobStringValue(ref["source_uri"])
            preparedAssets[asset.AssetID] = asset
            if strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(source["role"]), "overlay_timeline") {
                ref["role"] = "overlay"
            }
            // One runtime reference per asset: every placement owns its own object,
            // so FINALIZE receives unique ids without duplicating work.
            preparedRefs = append(preparedRefs, ref)
            segment.AssetID = asset.AssetID
            segment.SHA256 = asset.SHA256
            segment.SourceInUS = 0
            segment.SourceDurationUS = asset.DurationUS
        }
    
        // Preserve the one final audio asset, then add only the fragments referenced
        // by the executable plan. Original stock, clip, and overlay sources no
        // longer cross the FINALIZE boundary.
        var audioAsset *finalJobPlanAsset
        for index := range plan.Assets {
            if plan.Assets[index].AssetID == plan.FinalAudio.AssetID {
                asset := plan.Assets[index]
                audioAsset = &asset
                break
            }
        }
        if audioAsset == nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job compiled plan has no final audio asset")
        }
        // The producer re-binds the plan through the SAME asset registry the
        // payload builder filled: one identity rule, one dedupe rule, one order.
        assets := &finalJobPlanAssets{}
        if err := assets.set([]finalJobPlanAsset{*audioAsset}); err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job compiled plan final audio: %w", err)
        }
        for _, asset := range preparedAssets {
            if err := assets.add(asset); err != nil {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared final_job asset: %w", err)
            }
        }
        plan.Assets = assets.sorted()
        // Every video reference in the plan must now bind to one of the freshly
        // prepared fragments with the exact frame identity. The timeline position
        // belongs to the segment (and may be shared by several placements of one
        // asset), so it is not compared against the asset.
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            asset, ok := preparedAssets[segment.AssetID]
            if !ok || asset.SHA256 != segment.SHA256 || asset.FrameCount != segment.FrameCount {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job prepared segment %q lost its exact manifest binding", segment.SegmentID)
            }
        }
    
        // Keep FINALIZE minimal: prepared video fragments and the certified master
        // audio. Timeline/overlay placement is represented by the compiled plan.
        for _, raw := range runtimeAssets {
            asset, _ := raw.(map[string]any)
            if asset == nil || !strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(asset["role"]), "final_audio") {
                continue
            }
            preparedRefs = append(preparedRefs, asset)
        }
        // The video role is preserved from its source (stock/clip/overlay) because
        // Master validates that vocabulary while the immutable compiled plan uses
        // kind=video. Final audio remains the last role-tagged asset above.
    
        // The remote applies these exact rules; running them here means a plan that
        // cannot be accepted dies in this process, not in a live run.
        if err := validateFinalJobPlanBindingRules(plan); err != nil {
            return "", nil, err
        }
        canonicalPlan, err := json.Marshal(plan)
        if err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("marshal prepared final_job compiled plan: %w", err)
        }
        return string(canonicalPlan), preparedRefs, nil
    }
    
    func finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(raw map[string]any, request FinalJobVideoSegmentRequest) (finalJobPlanAsset, map[string]any, error) {
        if raw == nil {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("preparer returned an empty reference")
        }
        id := finalJobStringValue(raw["asset_id"])
        sha := strings.ToLower(finalJobStringValue(raw["sha256"]))
        source := strings.TrimSpace(finalJobStringValue(raw["source_uri"]))
        if source == "" {
            source = strings.TrimSpace(finalJobStringValue(raw["url"]))
        }
        size := finalJobInt64(raw["size_bytes"])
        durationUS := finalJobInt64(raw["duration_us"])
        if durationUS <= 0 {
            durationUS = finalJobInt64(raw["duration_ms"]) * 1000
        }
        frameCount := finalJobInt64(raw["frame_count"])
        if id == "" || len(sha) != 64 || size <= 0 || !strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(source), "https://") {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("preparer must return an asset id, SHA-256, positive size, and HTTPS source_uri")
        }
        if finalJobStringValue(raw["profile_id"]) != kernelmedia.AssemblyMediaContractID || !boolValue(raw["copy_eligible"]) || !boolValue(raw["first_frame_keyframe"]) || !boolValue(raw["closed_gop"]) {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("preparer did not certify the assembly-ready V1 stream")
        }
        if frameCount != request.FrameCount || finalJobInt64(raw["timeline_revision"]) != request.TimelineRevision ||
            !strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(raw["timeline_sha256"]), request.TimelineSHA256) ||
            finalJobInt64(raw["timeline_start_frame"]) != request.TimelineStartFrame {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("preparer returned frame/timeline metadata that does not match the requested segment")
        }
        // Frame math and geometry come from the assembly contract, not from a
        // second copy of 24/1 and 1920x1080 in the client plan builder.
        delivery := kernelmedia.DefaultAssemblyMediaContract()
        expectedDurationUS := finalJobFrameDurationUS(request.FrameCount, int64(delivery.FPS.Num), int64(delivery.FPS.Den))
        if durationUS != expectedDurationUS {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared duration is %dus, expected %dus for %d frames", durationUS, expectedDurationUS, request.FrameCount)
        }
        ref := make(map[string]any, len(raw)+1)
        for key, value := range raw {
            if key == "url" || key == "drive_file_id" {
                continue
            }
            ref[key] = value
        }
        ref["asset_id"], ref["sha256"], ref["size_bytes"], ref["source_uri"] = id, sha, size, source
        delete(ref, "local_path")
        asset := finalJobPlanAsset{
            AssetID: id, AssetKey: "sha256:" + sha, SHA256: sha, SizeBytes: size,
            Kind: "video", MIME: "video/mp4", DurationUS: durationUS, Width: delivery.Width, Height: delivery.Height, ProfileID: delivery.ID, FrameCount: frameCount,
            TimelineRevision: request.TimelineRevision, TimelineSHA256: strings.ToLower(request.TimelineSHA256),
            TimelineStartFrame: request.TimelineStartFrame, FirstFrameKeyframe: true, ClosedGOP: true,
        }
        return asset, ref, nil
    }
    
    func finalJobFrameDurationUS(frameCount, fpsNum, fpsDen int64) int64 {
        if frameCount <= 0 || fpsNum <= 0 || fpsDen <= 0 {
            return 0
        }
        numerator := frameCount * 1_000_000 * fpsDen
        return (numerator + fpsNum/2) / fpsNum
    }
    
    func sameFinalJobAssetIdentity(a, b map[string]any) bool {
        return strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(a["sha256"]), finalJobStringValue(b["sha256"])) &&
            finalJobStringValue(a["source_uri"]) == finalJobStringValue(b["source_uri"]) &&
            finalJobInt64(a["size_bytes"]) == finalJobInt64(b["size_bytes"])
    }
    
    func boolValue(value any) bool {
        b, _ := value.(bool)
        return b
    }
    
    func validateFinalJobHTTPSRuntimeAssets(assets []any) error {
        for i, raw := range assets {
            asset, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
            if !ok {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %d has an invalid shape", i)
            }
            source := strings.TrimSpace(finalJobStringValue(asset["source_uri"]))
            if source == "" {
                source = strings.TrimSpace(finalJobStringValue(asset["url"]))
            }
            if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(source), "https://") {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %q has no HTTPS source_uri", finalJobStringValue(asset["asset_id"]))
            }
            assetID := strings.TrimSpace(finalJobStringValue(asset["asset_id"]))
            if assetID == "" {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %d has no immutable asset_id", i)
            }
            delete(asset, "drive_file_id")
            // The Master uses `source_uri` to construct the signed HTTPS future-asset
            // plan, while the worker's runtime asset resolver requires `url` to stay
            // an internal asset reference. Sending the raw signed URL in `url` fails
            // closed in that resolver before the worker can consume the HTTPS plan.
            asset["source_uri"] = source
            asset["url"] = "velox-asset://" + assetID
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    func finalJobSceneDurationMS(scenes []map[string]any) int64 {
        var total int64
        for _, scene := range scenes {
            seconds, ok := scene["duration_seconds"].(float64)
            if ok && !math.IsNaN(seconds) && !math.IsInf(seconds, 0) && seconds > 0 {
                total += int64(math.Round(seconds * 1000))
            }
        }
        return total
    }
    
    // trimFinalJobSceneTail removes a small rounding surplus from the end of the
    // video timeline while preserving the minimum duration of every scene. The
    // packet-copy renderer requires its video timeline not to exceed final audio.
    func trimFinalJobSceneTail(scenes []map[string]any, surplusMS, minimumMS int64) error {
        if surplusMS <= 0 {
            return nil
        }
        for i := len(scenes) - 1; i >= 0 && surplusMS > 0; i-- {
            seconds, ok := scenes[i]["duration_seconds"].(float64)
            if !ok || math.IsNaN(seconds) || math.IsInf(seconds, 0) {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d has an invalid duration while aligning audio", i)
            }
            durationMS := int64(math.Round(seconds * 1000))
            available := durationMS - minimumMS
            if available <= 0 {
                continue
            }
            trim := min(available, surplusMS)
            scenes[i]["duration_seconds"] = float64(durationMS-trim) / 1000
            surplusMS -= trim
        }
        if surplusMS > 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("final_job cannot trim %dms to fit the certified audio without violating minimum scene duration", surplusMS)
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    // finalJobIdempotencyKey stays stable when the same submitted request is
    // retried under a new local run id. The remote Master uses this key to return
    // the already-prepared render instead of starting a duplicate video job.
    // Older/internal callers without a request key retain the run-id behavior.
    func finalJobIdempotencyKey(requestKey, runID string) string {
        requestKey = strings.TrimSpace(requestKey)
        if requestKey == "" {
            return "creator-77-" + strings.TrimSpace(runID)
        }
        // 2026-09-28: the digest SSOT (godlike/06) owns the algorithm. This call
        // used to import crypto/sha256 directly, which the archcheck
        // digest_sha256_import_outside_ssot gate rejects; SHA256String returns the
        // same lowercase hex, so the first 32 characters are the exact 16 bytes the
        // previous hex.EncodeToString(sum[:16]) produced.
        return "creator-77-request-" + digest.SHA256String(requestKey)[:32]
    }
    
    // finalJobAttemptIdempotencyKey is stable while reconciling one PREPARE
    // attempt, and distinct after Master reports a terminal lease.
    func finalJobAttemptIdempotencyKey(requestKey, runID string, attempt int) string {
        if attempt < 1 {
            attempt = 1
        }
        return finalJobIdempotencyKey(requestKey, runID) + fmt.Sprintf("-attempt-%d", attempt)
    }
    
    // compositeVideoScene preserves source identity in the remote contract. Stock
    // footage and caller-provided clips both carry silent video in the `stock`
    // media slot, but `kind` determines which pipeline policy owns that video.
    // Keep it explicit so stock can never inherit clip subtitle/transcript work.
    func compositeVideoScene(id string, index int, kind string, asset map[string]any, durationMS int64, text string) map[string]any {
        ref := make(map[string]any, len(asset))
        for k, v := range asset {
            // Materialized local paths are only for the Creator-side compositor. The
            // worker fetches the certified source_uri over HTTPS.
            if k == "local_path" {
                continue
            }
            ref[k] = v
        }
        if driveID := finalJobStringValue(ref["drive_file_id"]); driveID != "" {
            ref["url"] = driveFileWebLink(driveID)
        }
        scene := map[string]any{"scene_id": id, "index": index, "kind": kind, "duration_seconds": float64(durationMS) / 1000, "stock": ref}
        // PREPARE requires non-empty text on every scene, but stock scene text is
        // rendered as subtitles. Stock footage is intentionally caption-free, so
        // discard any narration/title and satisfy the schema with an invisible
        // separator. Clip scenes retain their real caption when provided.
        if kind == "stock" || strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
            text = "\u200b"
        }
        scene["text"] = text
        return scene
    }
    
    // The remote renderer requires each scene to be at least 100 ms. Audio and
    // source timing can leave a short final remainder (for example, 16 ms) after
    // millisecond rounding. Borrow that remainder from preceding scenes while
    // keeping every scene above the limit and preserving the total runtime.
    func enforceFinalJobMinimumSceneDuration(scenes []map[string]any, minimumMS int64) error {
        if minimumMS <= 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("final_job minimum scene duration must be positive")
        }
        for i, scene := range scenes {
            seconds, ok := scene["duration_seconds"].(float64)
            if !ok || math.IsNaN(seconds) || math.IsInf(seconds, 0) || seconds < 0 {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d has an invalid duration", i)
            }
            durationMS := int64(math.Round(seconds * 1000))
            if durationMS >= minimumMS {
                continue
            }
            deficit := minimumMS - durationMS
            for previous := i - 1; previous >= 0 && deficit > 0; previous-- {
                previousSeconds, valid := scenes[previous]["duration_seconds"].(float64)
                if !valid || math.IsNaN(previousSeconds) || math.IsInf(previousSeconds, 0) {
                    return fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d has an invalid duration", previous)
                }
                previousMS := int64(math.Round(previousSeconds * 1000))
                available := previousMS - minimumMS
                if available <= 0 {
                    continue
                }
                take := min(available, deficit)
                scenes[previous]["duration_seconds"] = float64(previousMS-take) / 1000
                deficit -= take
            }
            if deficit > 0 {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d is shorter than %dms with no preceding duration to borrow", i, minimumMS)
            }
            scene["duration_seconds"] = float64(minimumMS) / 1000
        }
        return nil
    }

    type finalJobSegmentWork struct {

    type FinalJobSegmentParallelism interface {

    func finalJobSegmentPrepareError(item finalJobSegmentWork, err error) error {
        return fmt.Errorf(
            "prepare final_job segment %q from asset %q role %q at %dus for %dus: %w",
            item.request.SegmentID,
            finalJobStringValue(item.source["asset_id"]),
            finalJobStringValue(item.source["role"]),
            item.request.SourceInUS,
            item.request.SourceDurationUS,
            err,
        )
    }
    
    // finalJobPrepareSegments prepares the fragments concurrently and returns them
    // indexed by plan position, so the binding stays deterministic whatever order
    // they complete in. Fail-closed: a failure cancels the remaining work and is
    // reported by plan position, never by scheduling luck, and a mere cancellation
    // is not reported over a real cause.
    func finalJobPrepareSegments(ctx context.Context, preparer FinalJobVideoSegmentPreparer, work []finalJobSegmentWork) ([]map[string]any, error) {
        prepared := make([]map[string]any, len(work))
        if len(work) == 0 {
            return prepared, nil
        }
        lanes := 1
        if declared, ok := preparer.(FinalJobSegmentParallelism); ok {
            if lanes = declared.Parallelism(); lanes < 1 {
                lanes = 1
            }
        }
        if lanes > len(work) {
            lanes = len(work)
        }
        if lanes == 1 {
            for _, item := range work {
                result, err := preparer.PrepareFinalJobVideoSegment(ctx, item.source, item.request)
                if err != nil {
                    return nil, finalJobSegmentPrepareError(item, err)
                }
                prepared[item.index] = result
            }
            return prepared, nil
        }
        runCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
        defer cancel()
        failures := make([]error, len(work))
        gates := make(chan struct{}, lanes)
        var wg sync.WaitGroup
        for _, item := range work {
            wg.Add(1)
            go func(item finalJobSegmentWork) {
                defer wg.Done()
                select {
                case gates <- struct{}{}:
                    defer func() { <-gates }()
                case <-runCtx.Done():
                    return
                }
                if runCtx.Err() != nil {
                    return
                }
                result, err := preparer.PrepareFinalJobVideoSegment(runCtx, item.source, item.request)
                if err != nil {
                    failures[item.index] = finalJobSegmentPrepareError(item, err)
                    cancel()
                    return
                }
                prepared[item.index] = result
            }(item)
        }
        wg.Wait()
        var cancelled error
        for _, err := range failures {
            if err == nil {
                continue
            }
            if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
                if cancelled == nil {
                    cancelled = err
                }
                continue
            }
            return nil, err
        }
        if cancelled != nil {
            return nil, cancelled
        }
        if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        return prepared, nil
    }

    // Runtime-asset resolution for the remote final job: the identity cache, the
    // stock staging and its receipts, and the prefetch lanes that keep handoff
    // from re-resolving one source per fragment.
    
    // resolverClock accumulates the runtime-asset resolution time of one handoff.
    // It answers the only question the receipt could not: how much of handoff_ms is
    // spent finding and publishing sources rather than encoding fragments.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolverClock() func() {
        started := time.Now()
        return func() {
            if a != nil {
                a.resolverNS.Add(time.Since(started).Nanoseconds())
            }
        }
    }
    
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) ResolveFinalJobAsset(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        return a.resolveOnce("objectstore:"+strings.TrimSpace(id), func() (map[string]any, error) {
            defer a.resolverClock()()
            started := time.Now()
            ref, err := a.ResolveFinalJobObjectStoreAsset(ctx, id)
            log.Printf("final_job resolve kind=objectstore id=%s bytes=%v ms=%d err=%v",
                id, ref["size_bytes"], time.Since(started).Milliseconds(), err != nil)
            return ref, err
        })
    }
    
    // resolveOnce answers a repeated resolution from the handoff's own cache. The
    // cached reference is copied on the way out so a caller cannot mutate the entry
    // (the payload builder stamps roles and durations onto the map it receives).
    //
    // Concurrent callers of the SAME identity share one resolution (single flight):
    // the prefetch warms a folder while the walk asks for the file it needs, and
    // without this the prefetch would be duplicated work instead of saved work.
    // An error is never cached — a failed warm-up must not poison the walk.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolveOnce(key string, build func() (map[string]any, error)) (map[string]any, error) {
        if a == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job adapter is not configured")
        }
        a.resolvedMu.Lock()
        if cached, ok := a.resolved[key]; ok {
            a.hits++
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
            return copyFinalJobRef(cached), nil
        }
        a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
    
        a.inflightMu.Lock()
        if call, ok := a.inflight[key]; ok {
            a.inflightMu.Unlock()
            <-call.done
            if call.err != nil {
                return nil, call.err
            }
            a.resolvedMu.Lock()
            a.hits++
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
            return copyFinalJobRef(call.ref), nil
        }
        if a.inflight == nil {
            a.inflight = make(map[string]*finalJobResolveCall, 16)
        }
        call := &finalJobResolveCall{done: make(chan struct{})}
        a.inflight[key] = call
        a.inflightMu.Unlock()
    
        func() {
            defer close(call.done)
            defer func() {
                a.inflightMu.Lock()
                delete(a.inflight, key)
                a.inflightMu.Unlock()
            }()
            call.ref, call.err = build()
            if call.err != nil {
                return
            }
            a.resolvedMu.Lock()
            if a.resolved == nil {
                a.resolved = make(map[string]map[string]any, 16)
            }
            a.resolved[key] = copyFinalJobRef(call.ref)
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        }()
        if call.err != nil {
            return nil, call.err
        }
        return copyFinalJobRef(call.ref), nil
    }
    
    const (
        // defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency is how many Drive sources one handoff
        // resolves at a time. It is 1 because concurrency was MEASURED and it loses
        // on this stack: serial r69/r73 cost ~190 ms per source (61 sources = 10,9 s
        // of the handoff), while a 64-file warm-up at 6 workers paid 576 ms per
        // source on average (max 2.068 ms) and turned the same handoff into 49,5 s.
        // The per-call cost triples under load — the path is throughput bound, not
        // latency bound — so parallelising it multiplies work instead of hiding it.
        // The knob stays so a future stack fix can be measured against this table.
        defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency = 1
        // maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency bounds the operator knob: beyond this the
        // handoff is no longer latency bound and a folder listing becomes a spike.
        maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency = 16
        // finalJobPrefetchPerFolder caps how many of one folder's files a prefetch
        // warms. It is a WINDOW, not a sample: the folder cursor consumes the list
        // in order, so warming the head of the list is exactly what the walk asks
        // for next (r73: a 240-file folder, 61 of them consumed, 12 warmed → 10,9 s
        // still spent on the critical path). 64 covers a long timeline at ~5 s per
        // source while costing ceil(64/6)·190 ms ≈ 2 s of wall instead of 64·190 ms.
        // A folder of hundreds is never resolved wholesale.
        finalJobPrefetchPerFolder = 64
    )
    
    // finalJobResolveConcurrency reads VELOX_FINAL_JOB_RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY. Absent
    // means the measured default, 1 means the pre-2026-11-01 serial handoff, and a
    // malformed value degrades to serial rather than inventing parallelism.
    func finalJobResolveConcurrency() int {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency
        }
        value, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || value < 1 {
            return 1
        }
        if value > maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency {
            return maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency
        }
        return value
    }

        a.resolvedRunID = runID
        a.resolved = nil
        a.hits = 0
    }
    
    // PrefetchFinalJobStockAssets warms the handoff cache for the Drive sources one
    // stock folder is about to offer. It returns when every requested identity has
    // been attempted (or the context ended), and it never reports an error: a
    // source that cannot be warmed is resolved — and reported — by the walk.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) PrefetchFinalJobStockAssets(ctx context.Context, ids []string) {
        a.prefetchFinalJobSources(ctx, ids, a.ResolveFinalJobStockAsset)
    }
    
    // prefetchFinalJobSources is the scheduling half of the prefetch: dedupe, skip
    // what the cache already holds, then resolve with a bounded pool. The resolver
    // is a parameter so the scheduling is testable without a Drive or an object
    // store.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) prefetchFinalJobSources(ctx context.Context, ids []string, resolve func(context.Context, string) (map[string]any, error)) {
        if a == nil || resolve == nil {
            return
        }
        workers := finalJobResolveConcurrency()
        if workers <= 1 {
            return
        }
        unique := make([]string, 0, len(ids))
        seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(ids))
        for _, raw := range ids {
            id := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
            if id == "" {
                continue
            }
            if _, ok := seen[id]; ok {
                continue
            }
            seen[id] = struct{}{}
            a.resolvedMu.Lock()
            _, cached := a.resolved["drive:"+id]
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        }
        if readerErr != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("close stock Drive response %q: %w", id, readerErr)
        }
        if fileErr != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("close staged stock file %q: %w", id, fileErr)
        }
        if written != size {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("stock Drive file %q downloaded %d bytes, expected %d", id, written, size)
        }
        if err := os.Rename(tmpPath, cached); err != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("commit stock cache entry %q: %w", cached, err)
        }
        return cached, func() {}, nil
    }
    
    // ResolveFinalJobStockAsset retains the explicitly allowed Drive path for
    // selected stock-folder videos. Every other final-job asset goes through the
    // HTTPS Objectstore resolver above.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) ResolveFinalJobStockAsset(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        return a.resolveOnce("drive:"+strings.TrimSpace(id), func() (map[string]any, error) {
            return a.resolveStockAssetOnce(ctx, id)
        })
    }
    
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolveStockAssetOnce(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        defer a.resolverClock()()
        started := time.Now()
        defer func() {
            log.Printf("final_job resolve kind=drive id=%s ms=%d", id, time.Since(started).Milliseconds())
        }()
        if a == nil || a.stock == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job stock Drive reader is not configured")
        }
        id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
        if id == "" || strings.ContainsAny(id, "/\\\x00\r\n") {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job stock Drive id is invalid")
        }
        meta, err := a.stock.GetFileMeta(ctx, id)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("read stock Drive metadata %q: %w", id, err)
        }
        if meta == nil || meta.Size <= 0 {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("stock Drive file %q has no positive byte size", id)
        }
    
        path, cleanup, err := a.stagedStockPath(ctx, id, meta.Size)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        defer cleanup()
        // A staged stock file is written once, by us, from the Drive bytes of that
        // exact id and size — the same identity the staging cache already trusts to
        // serve the file without downloading it again. Hashing, probing and signing
        // those same bytes on every later handoff is therefore repeated work, not
        // verification: the receipt written next to the file answers all three.
        // Fail-closed: a receipt that does not describe exactly this file is dropped
        // and the bytes are re-derived.
        if receipt, ok := readFinalJobStockReceipt(path, meta.Size); ok {
            ref, publishErr := scriptgen.PublishFinalJobLocalObjectVerified(ctx, "stock-sha256-"+receipt.SHA256[:24], path, receipt.SHA256, receipt.SizeBytes)
            if publishErr == nil {
                ref["duration_ms"] = receipt.DurationMS
                return ref, nil
            }
        }
        hash, size, err := digest.SHA256File(path)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("hash stock Drive file %q: %w", id, err)
        }
        if a.probe == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("canonical media probe is not configured")
        }
        info, probeErr := a.probe.Probe(ctx, path)
        if info == nil || !info.HasVideo {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("probe stock Drive video %q: video stream is missing", id)
        }
        resolved := asset.ResolveAssetDuration(info.Duration.Microseconds(), probeErr, 0, false)
        if !resolved.Known() {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("probe stock Drive video %q: duration is unknown: %w", id, probeErr)
        }
        durationMS := resolved.DurationUS / 1000
        assetID := "stock-sha256-" + hash[:24]

    // prepareFinalJobVideoSegments replaces source-video references with verified
    // assembly-ready fragments. It keeps audio as a single copy asset and drops
    // every unused source video from FINALIZE, so the remote worker's work is only
    // packet-copy placement plus final audio mux.
    func prepareFinalJobVideoSegments(ctx context.Context, rawPlan string, runtimeAssets []any, preparer FinalJobVideoSegmentPreparer) (string, []any, error) {
        if preparer == nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job requires a local video-segment preparer; refusing to send unprepared sources")
        }
        var plan finalJobCompiledPlan
        if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rawPlan), &plan); err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("decode final_job compiled plan before segment preparation: %w", err)
        }
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) == 0 {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment preparation requires one non-empty video track")
        }
        refs := make(map[string]map[string]any, len(runtimeAssets))
        for index, raw := range runtimeAssets {
            asset, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
            if !ok {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %d has an invalid shape", index)
            }
            id := finalJobStringValue(asset["asset_id"])
            if id == "" {
                continue
            }
            if prior := refs[id]; prior != nil && !sameFinalJobAssetIdentity(prior, asset) {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %q has conflicting source references", id)
            }
            refs[id] = asset
        }
    
        preparedAssets := make(map[string]finalJobPlanAsset, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments)+1)
        preparedRefs := make([]any, 0, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments)+1)
        // Phase 1 — validate every binding and describe the work. This is cheap and
        // sequential, and it fails before any expensive preparation starts.
        work := make([]finalJobSegmentWork, 0, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments))
        for index := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            segment := &plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[index]
            source := refs[segment.AssetID]
            if source == nil {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q has no runtime source asset %q", segment.SegmentID, segment.AssetID)
            }
            if !strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(source["sha256"]), segment.SHA256) {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q source SHA-256 does not match the compiled plan", segment.SegmentID)
            }
            work = append(work, finalJobSegmentWork{
                index:  index,
                source: source,
                request: FinalJobVideoSegmentRequest{
                    SegmentID: segment.SegmentID, SourceAssetID: segment.AssetID, SourceSHA256: segment.SHA256,
                    SourceInUS: segment.SourceInUS, SourceDurationUS: segment.SourceDurationUS,
                    TimelineStartFrame: segment.TimelineStartFrame, FrameCount: segment.FrameCount,
                    TimelineRevision: plan.TimelineRevision, TimelineSHA256: plan.TimelineSHA256,
                },
            })
        }
        // Phase 2 — prepare the fragments. They are independent, so they run on the
        // preparer's lanes; the result is indexed by plan position, which keeps the
        // binding deterministic whatever the completion order is.
        prepared, err := finalJobPrepareSegments(ctx, preparer, work)
        if err != nil {
            return "", nil, err
        }
        // Phase 3 — bind in plan order, ONE asset per placement. The assembler
        // certifies each placement against the manifest of its OWN asset
        // (`segment "…" manifest binding is not exact` — r66), so two placements can
        // never share one object even when their pixels are identical. The
        // collision is resolved on the OBJECT, never on the binding: the later
        // placement is re-prepared with a placement tag (same pictures, different
        // container, different bytes), which satisfies both the plan's unique
        // canonical identity and the assembler's per-placement certificate.
        usedSHA := make(map[string]string, len(work))
        usedURI := make(map[string]string, len(work))
        for _, item := range work {
            segment := &plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[item.index]
            source := item.source
            asset, ref, err := finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(prepared[item.index], item.request)
            if err != nil {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared final_job segment %q: %w", segment.SegmentID, err)
            }
            if _, exists := usedSHA[asset.SHA256]; exists {
                // Identical bytes for a second placement. Derive THIS placement from
                // the certified object already produced above: the same bitstream in
                // a distinct container is a naming problem, and re-encoding the same
                // window would pay for pixels that already exist. The tag stays in
                // the work identity, so the tagged object can never be answered with
                // the untagged bytes.
                item.request.PlacementTag = segment.SegmentID
                item.request.ReuseFromSHA256 = asset.SHA256
                item.request.ReuseFromURI = usedURI[asset.SHA256]
                tagged, tagErr := preparer.PrepareFinalJobVideoSegment(ctx, source, item.request)
                if tagErr != nil {
                    return "", nil, finalJobSegmentPrepareError(item, tagErr)
                }
                asset, ref, err = finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(tagged, item.request)
                if err != nil {
                    return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared final_job segment %q: %w", segment.SegmentID, err)
                }
                if other, stillShared := usedSHA[asset.SHA256]; stillShared {
                    return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q still certifies the bytes of another placement (%q); refusing to send a plan the assembler must reject", segment.SegmentID, other)
                }
            }
            usedSHA[asset.SHA256] = segment.SegmentID
            usedURI[asset.SHA256] = finalJobStringValue(ref["source_uri"])
            preparedAssets[asset.AssetID] = asset
            if strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(source["role"]), "overlay_timeline") {
                ref["role"] = "overlay"
            }
            // One runtime reference per asset: every placement owns its own object,
            // so FINALIZE receives unique ids without duplicating work.
            preparedRefs = append(preparedRefs, ref)
            segment.AssetID = asset.AssetID
            segment.SHA256 = asset.SHA256
            segment.SourceInUS = 0
            segment.SourceDurationUS = asset.DurationUS
        }
    
        // Preserve the one final audio asset, then add only the fragments referenced
        // by the executable plan. Original stock, clip, and overlay sources no
        // longer cross the FINALIZE boundary.
        var audioAsset *finalJobPlanAsset
        for index := range plan.Assets {
            if plan.Assets[index].AssetID == plan.FinalAudio.AssetID {
                asset := plan.Assets[index]
                audioAsset = &asset
                break
            }
        }
        if audioAsset == nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job compiled plan has no final audio asset")
        }
        // The producer re-binds the plan through the SAME asset registry the
        // payload builder filled: one identity rule, one dedupe rule, one order.
        assets := &finalJobPlanAssets{}
        if err := assets.set([]finalJobPlanAsset{*audioAsset}); err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job compiled plan final audio: %w", err)
        }
        for _, asset := range preparedAssets {
            if err := assets.add(asset); err != nil {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared final_job asset: %w", err)
            }
        }
        plan.Assets = assets.sorted()
        // Every video reference in the plan must now bind to one of the freshly
        // prepared fragments with the exact frame identity. The timeline position
        // belongs to the segment (and may be shared by several placements of one
        // asset), so it is not compared against the asset.
        for _, segment := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            asset, ok := preparedAssets[segment.AssetID]
            if !ok || asset.SHA256 != segment.SHA256 || asset.FrameCount != segment.FrameCount {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job prepared segment %q lost its exact manifest binding", segment.SegmentID)
            }
        }
    
        // Keep FINALIZE minimal: prepared video fragments and the certified master
        // audio. Timeline/overlay placement is represented by the compiled plan.
        for _, raw := range runtimeAssets {
            asset, _ := raw.(map[string]any)
            if asset == nil || !strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(asset["role"]), "final_audio") {
                continue
            }
            preparedRefs = append(preparedRefs, asset)
        }
        // The video role is preserved from its source (stock/clip/overlay) because
        // Master validates that vocabulary while the immutable compiled plan uses
        // kind=video. Final audio remains the last role-tagged asset above.
    
        // The remote applies these exact rules; running them here means a plan that
        // cannot be accepted dies in this process, not in a live run.
        if err := validateFinalJobPlanBindingRules(plan); err != nil {
            return "", nil, err
        }
        canonicalPlan, err := json.Marshal(plan)
        if err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("marshal prepared final_job compiled plan: %w", err)
        }
        return string(canonicalPlan), preparedRefs, nil
    }
    
    func finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(raw map[string]any, request FinalJobVideoSegmentRequest) (finalJobPlanAsset, map[string]any, error) {
        if raw == nil {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("preparer returned an empty reference")
        }
        id := finalJobStringValue(raw["asset_id"])
        sha := strings.ToLower(finalJobStringValue(raw["sha256"]))
        source := strings.TrimSpace(finalJobStringValue(raw["source_uri"]))
        if source == "" {
            source = strings.TrimSpace(finalJobStringValue(raw["url"]))
        }
        size := finalJobInt64(raw["size_bytes"])
        durationUS := finalJobInt64(raw["duration_us"])
        if durationUS <= 0 {
            durationUS = finalJobInt64(raw["duration_ms"]) * 1000
        }
        frameCount := finalJobInt64(raw["frame_count"])
        if id == "" || len(sha) != 64 || size <= 0 || !strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(source), "https://") {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("preparer must return an asset id, SHA-256, positive size, and HTTPS source_uri")
        }
        if finalJobStringValue(raw["profile_id"]) != kernelmedia.AssemblyMediaContractID || !boolValue(raw["copy_eligible"]) || !boolValue(raw["first_frame_keyframe"]) || !boolValue(raw["closed_gop"]) {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("preparer did not certify the assembly-ready V1 stream")
        }
        if frameCount != request.FrameCount || finalJobInt64(raw["timeline_revision"]) != request.TimelineRevision ||
            !strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(raw["timeline_sha256"]), request.TimelineSHA256) ||
            finalJobInt64(raw["timeline_start_frame"]) != request.TimelineStartFrame {
            return finalJobPlanAsset{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("preparer returned frame/timeline metadata that does not match the requested segment")

        1. Esegui il test del package modificato, es. `go test ./internal/capabilities/audio/... -count=1` (oppure `-run TestNome` per un singolo test).

        7. Non scartare modifiche locali non correlate.
        Esempi concreti del loop rapido (punti 1-2), `-count=1` evita risultati in cache:

    func finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(raw map[string]any, request FinalJobVideoSegmentRequest) (finalJobPlanAsset, map[string]any, error) {
        // The per-call cost triples under load — the path is throughput bound, not
        // latency bound — so parallelising it multiplies work instead of hiding it.
        // The knob stays so a future stack fix can be measured against this table.
        defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency = 1
        // maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency bounds the operator knob: beyond this the
        // handoff is no longer latency bound and a folder listing becomes a spike.
        maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency = 16
        // finalJobPrefetchPerFolder caps how many of one folder's files a prefetch
        // warms. It is a WINDOW, not a sample: the folder cursor consumes the list
        // in order, so warming the head of the list is exactly what the walk asks
        // for next (r73: a 240-file folder, 61 of them consumed, 12 warmed → 10,9 s
        // still spent on the critical path). 64 covers a long timeline at ~5 s per
        // source while costing ceil(64/6)·190 ms ≈ 2 s of wall instead of 64·190 ms.
        // A folder of hundreds is never resolved wholesale.
        finalJobPrefetchPerFolder = 64
    )
    
    // finalJobResolveConcurrency reads VELOX_FINAL_JOB_RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY. Absent
    // means the measured default, 1 means the pre-2026-11-01 serial handoff, and a
    // malformed value degrades to serial rather than inventing parallelism.
    func finalJobResolveConcurrency() int {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency
        }
        value, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || value < 1 {
            return 1
        }
        if value > maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency {
            return maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency
        }
        return value
    }

    // re-walks the same selection and reports its own error.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx context.Context, runID string, req scriptgen.GenerateRequest, result *scriptgen.GenerateResult) error {
        if a == nil || result == nil {

        // The prewarm owns the cache of THIS run; StartFinalJob keeps it because it

        a.beginHandoffCache(runID)

        a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        log.Printf("final_job prewarm kind=stock windows=%d unique_resolved=%d wall_ms=%d err=%v",
            windows, unique, time.Since(started).Milliseconds(), err)
        return err
    }

            return "", "", fmt.Errorf("final_job V2 render plan requires a positive canonical duration")

        if delta := audio.DurationUS - timelineDurationUS; delta < -40_000 || delta > 40_000 {

        }

        baseEnd := base[len(base)-1].endUS

    package scriptgeneration
    
    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "strings"
    )
    
    // final_job_stock_planner.go owns WHICH stock source a final job consumes.
    //
    // The selection used to exist only inside BuildFinalJobPayloads, intertwined
    // with building scenes, runtime assets and script text. That made the selection
    // unavailable to anything that wanted to resolve the same sources EARLIER than
    // the handoff: r75 measured 9,8 s of serial Drive resolution inside `handoff`
    // (576 ms per source, concurrency does not help because each source publishes
    // its own bytes) while the overlay render was occupying 13,4 s of the critical
    // path with no work queued behind it.
    //
    // A prewarm that re-derived the selection would be a second implementation of
    // the same rule, and two implementations of "which source does scene N get"
    // drift: the prewarm would warm the wrong file and the walk would still pay the
    // full price, silently. So the rule lives here, once, and both the payload
    // build and the prewarm walk through it.
    //
    // The walk is DEPENDENT ON RESOLVED DURATIONS: which file a scene consumes next
    // depends on how long the previous chunk filled the scene, and durations come
    // from the resolver. A prewarm therefore cannot know the set without resolving
    // it — but resolving is exactly the expensive work, and the resolver's cache
    // (plus its single-flight index) makes the later walk answer from what the
    // prewarm already paid for. That is why sharing the walk is sufficient and a
    // separate "predict the set" heuristic is not needed.
    
    // finalJobStockClip is one stock window the remote assembler will place: the
    // resolved asset (Drive identity in, immutable HTTPS reference out) and the
    // exact duration the scene consumes from it.
    type finalJobStockClip struct {
        Asset   map[string]any
        ChunkMS int64
    }
    
    // finalJobStockPlanner carries the per-handoff stock bookkeeping: the eligible
    // file list per folder, the resolved asset cache, and the rotation cursor. The
    // cursor is per FOLDER and advances across scenes, so one scene's consumption
    // decides what the next scene in the same folder gets — the planner must be
    // shared by every scene of a handoff, never recreated per scene.
    type finalJobStockPlanner struct {
        files   map[string][]FinalJobStockFile
        assets  map[string]map[string]any
        cursors map[string]int
    }
    
    func newFinalJobStockPlanner() *finalJobStockPlanner {
        return &finalJobStockPlanner{
            files:   make(map[string][]FinalJobStockFile),
            assets:  make(map[string]map[string]any),
            cursors: make(map[string]int),
        }
    }
    
    // folder returns the video files of one stock folder, listing it once per
    // handoff and warming the sources it will offer. The final-job preparer
    // normalizes sources that do not qualify for packet copy before publishing
    // them to the remote assembler.
    func (p *finalJobStockPlanner) folder(ctx context.Context, resolver FinalJobAssetResolver, folderID string) ([]FinalJobStockFile, error) {
        if files, ok := p.files[folderID]; ok {
            return files, nil
        }
        listed, err := resolver.ListFinalJobStockFolder(ctx, folderID)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("list selected stock folder %s: %w", folderID, err)
        }
        if len(listed) == 0 {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("selected stock folder %s contains no video files", folderID)
        }
        p.files[folderID] = listed
        // Warm the sources this folder can offer BEFORE the walk asks for them. A
        // scene at 10-14 s spends 195 ms per uncached Drive source (metadata,
        // staged bytes, publish, signature) and r69's handoff paid 56 of those
        // serially: 10,9 s of its 14,4 s. The set is known here and the identities
        // are independent, so the only reason to stay serial was that nobody had
        // asked for them concurrently.
        prefetchFinalJobStockAssets(ctx, resolver, listed)
        return listed, nil
    }
    
    // sceneClips consumes one scene's canonical duration from its stock folder and
    // returns the exact chunks the assembler will place.
    //
    // It reproduces the stock walk of the final-job payload byte for byte: rotate
    // through the folder, consume one chunk per file, and take the scene's
    // remaining duration from the last one. The cursor is stored after the file has
    // been claimed, so a failure half way through a scene leaves the folder
    // advanced exactly as the successful walk would have.
    func (p *finalJobStockPlanner) sceneClips(ctx context.Context, resolver FinalJobAssetResolver, folderID string, durationUS int64) ([]finalJobStockClip, error) {
        files, err := p.folder(ctx, resolver, folderID)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        remainingMS := (durationUS + 999) / 1000
        if remainingMS <= 0 {
            return nil, nil
        }
        clips := make([]finalJobStockClip, 0, 1)
        folderIndex := p.cursors[folderID]
        for remainingMS > 0 {
            file := files[folderIndex%len(files)]
            folderIndex++
            p.cursors[folderID] = folderIndex
            asset, ok := p.assets[file.ID]
            if !ok {
                asset, err = resolveFinalJobStockAsset(ctx, resolver, file.ID)
                if err != nil {
                    return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve stock file %s (%s): %w", file.Name, file.ID, err)
                }
                p.assets[file.ID] = asset
            }
            durationMS, _ := asset["duration_ms"].(int64)
            if durationMS <= 0 {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("stock file %s has no canonical duration", file.Name)
            }
            chunkMS := durationMS
            if chunkMS > remainingMS {
                chunkMS = remainingMS
            }
            clips = append(clips, finalJobStockClip{Asset: asset, ChunkMS: chunkMS})
            remainingMS -= chunkMS
            folderIndex++
        }
        return clips, nil
    }
    
    // PrewarmFinalJobStockSources resolves every stock source the final job WILL
    // consume, during a window the run is already spending elsewhere, and reports
    // how many windows it planned.
    //
    // It is deliberately the same walk the handoff uses (see finalJobStockPlanner):
    // a source is only warmable if the walk would ask for it, and the walk only
    // asks for it once it has resolved the previous chunk's duration. Running the
    // walk early therefore resolves the exact identities the handoff would have
    // resolved serially, and the handoff's own cache answers them.
    //
    // Failure is not fatal and not silent: the error is returned to the caller (the
    // runner logs it) while the handoff re-walks and reports its own error, so a
    // prewarm miss can only ever cost the time it tried to save.
    func PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx context.Context, result *GenerateResult, resolver FinalJobAssetResolver) (int, error) {
        if result == nil || result.CanonicalTimeline == nil || resolver == nil {
            return 0, nil
        }
        scenesByID := make(map[string]Scene, len(result.Scenes))
        for _, scene := range result.Scenes {
            scenesByID[scene.ID] = scene
        }
        planner := newFinalJobStockPlanner()
        planned := 0
        for _, segment := range result.CanonicalTimeline.Segments {
            localScene, ok := scenesByID[segment.ID]
            if !ok {
                continue
            }
            // Fixed-media scenes place protected intro clips and clip-only scenes
            // place the pipeline's own certified render: neither touches a stock
            // folder, so neither advances the cursor this walk reproduces.
            if segment.FixedMedia || localScene.ExecutionMode.IsFixedMedia() {
                continue
            }
            if localScene.Stock == nil {
                continue
            }
            folderID := strings.TrimSpace(localScene.Stock.FolderID)
            if folderID == "" {
                continue
            }
            clips, err := planner.sceneClips(ctx, resolver, folderID, segment.DurationUS)
            if err != nil {
                return planned, err
            }
            planned += len(clips)
        }
        return planned, nil
    }

        if err != nil {

        }

        timelineMaterial := map[string]any{
            "duration_us":             timelineDurationUS,
            "audio_plan_sha256":       strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(audio.PlanSHA256)),
            "overlay_timeline_sha256": "",
        }
        if len(manifests) == 1 {
            if asset, ok := manifests[0]["asset"].(map[string]any); ok {
