            }
        } else if len(manifests) > 1 {
            hashes := make([]string, 0, len(manifests))
            for _, manifest := range manifests {
                asset := manifest["asset"].(map[string]any)
                hashes = append(hashes, strings.ToLower(finalJobStringValue(asset["sha256"])))
            }
            timelineMaterial["overlay_timeline_sha256"] = digest.SHA256String(strings.Join(hashes, "\x00"))
        }
        timelineBytes, err := json.Marshal(timelineMaterial)
        if err != nil {
            return "", "", fmt.Errorf("marshal final_job V2 timeline identity: %w", err)
        }
        timelineSHA := digest.SHA256String(string(timelineBytes))
        plan := finalJobCompiledPlan{
            PlanVersion: 2, TimelineRevision: timelineRevision, TimelineSHA256: timelineSHA,
            DurationUS: timelineDurationUS,
            Output:     finalJobPlanOutputBlock(),
            FinalAudio: finalJobPlanAudio{
                Mode: "FINAL_AUDIO_COPY", AssetID: finalJobStringValue(audioRef["asset_id"]),
                SHA256: strings.ToLower(finalJobStringValue(audioRef["sha256"])), SizeBytes: finalJobInt64(audioRef["size_bytes"]),
                Codec: delivery.AudioCodec, SampleRateHz: delivery.AudioSampleRate, Channels: delivery.AudioChannels,
                DurationUS:       audio.DurationUS,
                TimelineRevision: timelineRevision, TimelineSHA256: timelineSHA,
            },
            VideoTracks: []finalJobPlanVideoTrack{{TrackID: "main-video", Segments: segments}},
            Assets:      assets.sorted(),
        }
        canonical, err := json.Marshal(plan)
        if err != nil {
            return "", "", fmt.Errorf("marshal final_job canonical V2 render plan: %w", err)
        }
        return string(canonical), digest.SHA256String(string(canonical)), nil
    }
    
    // finalJobPlanBaseSegments describes one source segment per scene and types
    // every stock asset INTO the shared registry the caller already owns.
    func finalJobPlanBaseSegments(scenes []map[string]any, assets *finalJobPlanAssets) ([]finalJobBaseSegment, error) {
        base := make([]finalJobBaseSegment, 0, len(scenes))
        var cursorUS int64
        for i, scene := range scenes {
            asset, ok := scene["stock"].(map[string]any)
            if !ok {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d has no video asset", i)
            }
            durationSeconds, ok := scene["duration_seconds"].(float64)
            if !ok || math.IsNaN(durationSeconds) || math.IsInf(durationSeconds, 0) || durationSeconds <= 0 {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d has an invalid duration", i)
            }
            durationUS := int64(math.Round(durationSeconds * 1_000_000))
            assetDurationUS := finalJobInt64(asset["duration_ms"]) * 1000
            if err := assets.addRaw(asset, "video", assetDurationUS, finalJobInt(asset["width"]), finalJobInt(asset["height"]), finalJobInt64(asset["frame_count"])); err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d: %w", i, err)
            }
            sourceInUS := finalJobInt64(asset["start_ms"]) * 1000
            assetID := finalJobStringValue(asset["asset_id"])
            sha := strings.ToLower(finalJobStringValue(asset["sha256"]))
            base = append(base, finalJobBaseSegment{startUS: cursorUS, endUS: cursorUS + durationUS, sourceInUS: sourceInUS, assetID: assetID, sha256: sha})
            cursorUS += durationUS
        }
        return base, nil
    }
    
    func finalJobMergeOverlayWindows(input []finalJobOverlayWindow) ([]finalJobOverlayWindow, error) {
        sort.SliceStable(input, func(i, j int) bool {
            if input[i].startUS != input[j].startUS {
                return input[i].startUS < input[j].startUS
            }
            return input[i].endUS < input[j].endUS
        })
        merged := make([]finalJobOverlayWindow, 0, len(input))
        for _, current := range input {
            if current.endUS <= current.startUS || current.assetID == "" || len(current.sha256) != 64 {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job overlay timeline contains an invalid replacement window")
            }
            if len(merged) > 0 && current.startUS < merged[len(merged)-1].endUS {
                prior := &merged[len(merged)-1]
                if prior.assetID != current.assetID || prior.sha256 != current.sha256 || prior.artifactInUS-prior.startUS != current.artifactInUS-current.startUS {
                    return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job overlay replacement windows overlap with different artifact timing")
                }
                if current.endUS > prior.endUS {
                    prior.endUS = current.endUS
                }
                continue
            }
            // Adjacent windows of the SAME artifact that are also contiguous inside
            // it are one continuous take: keeping them apart would pay two fragment
            // encodes (and two verifications, two uploads) for one piece of video.
            if len(merged) > 0 {
                prior := &merged[len(merged)-1]
                if prior.assetID == current.assetID && prior.sha256 == current.sha256 &&
                    prior.endUS == current.startUS &&
                    prior.artifactInUS+(prior.endUS-prior.startUS) == current.artifactInUS {
                    prior.endUS = current.endUS
                    continue
                }
            }

    func finalJobComposePlanSegments(base []finalJobBaseSegment, overlays []finalJobOverlayWindow, durationUS, fpsNum, fpsDen int64) ([]finalJobPlanSegment, error) {
        segments := make([]finalJobPlanSegment, 0, len(base)+2*len(overlays))
        cursorUS := int64(0)
        appendBase := func(startUS, endUS int64) error {
            if endUS <= startUS {
                return nil
            }
            for _, source := range base {
                inUS, outUS := max(startUS, source.startUS), min(endUS, source.endUS)
                if outUS <= inUS {
                    continue
                }
                startFrame := finalJobFrameAtUS(inUS, fpsNum, fpsDen)
                endFrame := finalJobFrameAtUS(outUS, fpsNum, fpsDen)
                // The compiled timeline is frame-quantized. A positive microsecond
                // interval shorter than half a frame can round to no output frame;
                // omit it instead of emitting an invalid zero-frame worker segment.
                if endFrame <= startFrame {
                    continue
                }
                segments = append(segments, finalJobPlanSegment{
                    SegmentID: fmt.Sprintf("segment-%04d", len(segments)), AssetID: source.assetID, SHA256: source.sha256,
                    TimelineStartFrame: startFrame,
                    FrameCount:         endFrame - startFrame,
                    SourceInUS:         source.sourceInUS + (inUS - source.startUS), SourceDurationUS: outUS - inUS,
                })
            }
            return nil
        }
        for _, overlay := range overlays {
            if overlay.startUS < cursorUS || overlay.endUS > durationUS {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job overlay windows are not ordered within the output timeline")
            }
            if err := appendBase(cursorUS, overlay.startUS); err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
            startFrame := finalJobFrameAtUS(overlay.startUS, fpsNum, fpsDen)
            endFrame := finalJobFrameAtUS(overlay.endUS, fpsNum, fpsDen)
            if endFrame > startFrame {
                segments = append(segments, finalJobPlanSegment{
                    SegmentID: fmt.Sprintf("segment-%04d", len(segments)), AssetID: overlay.assetID, SHA256: overlay.sha256,
                    TimelineStartFrame: startFrame, FrameCount: endFrame - startFrame,
                    SourceInUS: overlay.artifactInUS, SourceDurationUS: overlay.endUS - overlay.startUS,
                })
            }
            cursorUS = overlay.endUS
        }
        if err := appendBase(cursorUS, durationUS); err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        segments = finalJobMergeContiguousSegments(segments)
        for i, segment := range segments {
            if segment.FrameCount <= 0 || segment.SourceDurationUS <= 0 {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job V2 segment %d has an empty frame or source window (frames=%d source_duration_us=%d asset=%q)", i, segment.FrameCount, segment.SourceDurationUS, segment.AssetID)
            }
        }
        return segments, nil
    }

    // FinalJobSubmitter hands a completed local media plan to the configured
    // remote render master. It is intentionally absent from runs with

    //

    // owns the first two phases and the FIRST bounded wait; a wait that outlives
    // that budget is reported with ErrFinalJobPending, and the durable receipt it
    // returns carries the Master's job id so a later attempt resumes from it (see
    // FinalJobAttacher) instead of asking the Master for a second render.

        SubmitFinalJob(context.Context, string, GenerateRequest, *GenerateResult) (RemoteFinalJobResult, error)
    }
    
    // FinalJobSourcePrewarmer is the OPTIONAL capability that resolves the stock
    // sources a final job will consume BEFORE the handoff asks for them.

    // own bytes), so on a 10-scene run it pays ~10 s inside `remote_final_job`
    // while the overlay render holds 13 s of the critical path with nothing queued
    // behind it. Warming the same sources during that render moves the cost into a
    // window that was already paid for; it does not make the resolution faster.
    //

    // prewarm keeps the serial handoff byte for byte, and the returned error is
    // logged by the runner — the handoff still walks and still reports its own
    // failure, so a prewarm miss can only cost the time it tried to save.

        PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx context.Context, runID string, req GenerateRequest, result *GenerateResult) error

    // The runner checkpoints the returned job ID before it starts polling, so a

    }

    // branch on it without importing the transport package, and it always travels
    // with the receipt that carries the job id — the handle an attempt must persist
    // before handing the wait back.
    var ErrFinalJobPending = errors.New("remote final job is still rendering")

    // receipt state could not be saved safely.
    var ErrFinalJobReceiptCheckpoint = errors.New("remote final job receipt checkpoint failed")

    // job that a PREVIOUS attempt already submitted, with no second PREPARE. A
    // submitter that cannot resume one is still valid (it is what every non-final
    // run wires), but a run that already has a pending receipt fails closed rather
    // than submit a duplicate render.

        // waitToCompletion=false waits only up to the submitter's attach budget and
        // reports ErrFinalJobPending when it expires; true waits with the
        // submitter's full poll timeout, which is the pre-split blocking contract.
        AttachFinalJob(ctx context.Context, jobID string, waitToCompletion bool) (RemoteFinalJobResult, error)
    }

        // retries of PREPARE_INTENT keep it stable for idempotent reconciliation.

    func finalJobPlanBaseSegments(scenes []map[string]any, assets *finalJobPlanAssets) ([]finalJobBaseSegment, error) {
        base := make([]finalJobBaseSegment, 0, len(scenes))

                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d has no video asset", i)
            }
            durationSeconds, ok := scene["duration_seconds"].(float64)
            if !ok || math.IsNaN(durationSeconds) || math.IsInf(durationSeconds, 0) || durationSeconds <= 0 {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job scene %d has an invalid duration", i)

            durationUS := int64(math.Round(durationSeconds * 1_000_000))
            assetDurationUS := finalJobInt64(asset["duration_ms"]) * 1000
            if err := assets.addRaw(asset, "video", assetDurationUS, finalJobInt(asset["width"]), finalJobInt(asset["height"]), finalJobInt64(asset["frame_count"])); err != nil {

            sourceInUS := finalJobInt64(asset["start_ms"]) * 1000
            assetID := finalJobStringValue(asset["asset_id"])

            base = append(base, finalJobBaseSegment{startUS: cursorUS, endUS: cursorUS + durationUS, sourceInUS: sourceInUS, assetID: assetID, sha256: sha})

        return base, nil

    func finalJobMergeOverlayWindows(input []finalJobOverlayWindow) ([]finalJobOverlayWindow, error) {
        sort.SliceStable(input, func(i, j int) bool {
            if input[i].startUS != input[j].startUS {
                return input[i].startUS < input[j].startUS
            }
            return input[i].endUS < input[j].endUS
        })

        for _, current := range input {
            if current.endUS <= current.startUS || current.assetID == "" || len(current.sha256) != 64 {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job overlay timeline contains an invalid replacement window")
            }
            if len(merged) > 0 && current.startUS < merged[len(merged)-1].endUS {
                prior := &merged[len(merged)-1]
                if prior.assetID != current.assetID || prior.sha256 != current.sha256 || prior.artifactInUS-prior.startUS != current.artifactInUS-current.startUS {
                    return nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job overlay replacement windows overlap with different artifact timing")
                }
                if current.endUS > prior.endUS {
                    prior.endUS = current.endUS
                }
                continue
            }
            // Adjacent windows of the SAME artifact that are also contiguous inside
            // it are one continuous take: keeping them apart would pay two fragment
            // encodes (and two verifications, two uploads) for one piece of video.
            if len(merged) > 0 {
                prior := &merged[len(merged)-1]
                if prior.assetID == current.assetID && prior.sha256 == current.sha256 &&
                    prior.endUS == current.startUS &&
                    prior.artifactInUS+(prior.endUS-prior.startUS) == current.artifactInUS {
                    prior.endUS = current.endUS
                    continue
                }
            }
            merged = append(merged, current)
        }
        return merged, nil
    }

    func finalJobMergeContiguousSegments(segments []finalJobPlanSegment) []finalJobPlanSegment {

            return segments

    func finalJobFrameAtUS(us, fpsNum, fpsDen int64) int64 {

        denominator := int64(1_000_000) * fpsDen
        return (numerator + denominator/2) / denominator

    func finalJobInt64(value any) int64 {
        switch n := value.(type) {
        case int:
            return int64(n)
        case int64:
            return n
        case float64:
            return int64(n)
        case json.Number:
            i, _ := n.Int64()
            return i
        case string:
            var i int64
            _, _ = fmt.Sscan(strings.TrimSpace(n), &i)
            return i
        default:
            return 0
        }
    }

        return int(finalJobInt64(value))

            }
            if err := enforceFinalJobPreflight(remoteScenes, result.FinalAudio.DurationMS); err != nil {
                return nil, nil, err

    // prepareFinalJobVideoSegments replaces source-video references with verified
    // assembly-ready fragments. It keeps audio as a single copy asset and drops
    // every unused source video from FINALIZE, so the remote worker's work is only
    // packet-copy placement plus final audio mux.
    func prepareFinalJobVideoSegments(ctx context.Context, rawPlan string, runtimeAssets []any, preparer FinalJobVideoSegmentPreparer) (string, []any, error) {
        if preparer == nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job requires a local video-segment preparer; refusing to send unprepared sources")
        }
        var plan finalJobCompiledPlan
        if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rawPlan), &plan); err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("decode final_job compiled plan before segment preparation: %w", err)
        }
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) == 0 {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment preparation requires one non-empty video track")
        }
        refs := make(map[string]map[string]any, len(runtimeAssets))
        for index, raw := range runtimeAssets {
            asset, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
            if !ok {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %d has an invalid shape", index)
            }
            id := finalJobStringValue(asset["asset_id"])
            if id == "" {
                continue
            }
            if prior := refs[id]; prior != nil && !sameFinalJobAssetIdentity(prior, asset) {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job runtime asset %q has conflicting source references", id)
            }
            refs[id] = asset
        }
    
        preparedAssets := make(map[string]finalJobPlanAsset, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments)+1)
        preparedRefs := make([]any, 0, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments)+1)
        // Phase 1 — validate every binding and describe the work. This is cheap and
        // sequential, and it fails before any expensive preparation starts.
        work := make([]finalJobSegmentWork, 0, len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments))
        for index := range plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments {
            segment := &plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[index]
            source := refs[segment.AssetID]
            if source == nil {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q has no runtime source asset %q", segment.SegmentID, segment.AssetID)
            }
            if !strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(source["sha256"]), segment.SHA256) {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q source SHA-256 does not match the compiled plan", segment.SegmentID)
            }
            work = append(work, finalJobSegmentWork{
                index:  index,
                source: source,
                request: FinalJobVideoSegmentRequest{
                    SegmentID: segment.SegmentID, SourceAssetID: segment.AssetID, SourceSHA256: segment.SHA256,
                    SourceInUS: segment.SourceInUS, SourceDurationUS: segment.SourceDurationUS,
                    TimelineStartFrame: segment.TimelineStartFrame, FrameCount: segment.FrameCount,
                    TimelineRevision: plan.TimelineRevision, TimelineSHA256: plan.TimelineSHA256,
                },
            })
        }
        // Phase 2 — prepare the fragments. They are independent, so they run on the
        // preparer's lanes; the result is indexed by plan position, which keeps the
        // binding deterministic whatever the completion order is.
        prepared, err := finalJobPrepareSegments(ctx, preparer, work)
        if err != nil {
            return "", nil, err
        }
        // Phase 3 — bind in plan order, ONE asset per placement. The assembler
        // certifies each placement against the manifest of its OWN asset
        // (`segment "…" manifest binding is not exact` — r66), so two placements can
        // never share one object even when their pixels are identical. The
        // collision is resolved on the OBJECT, never on the binding: the later
        // placement is re-prepared with a placement tag (same pictures, different
        // container, different bytes), which satisfies both the plan's unique
        // canonical identity and the assembler's per-placement certificate.
        usedSHA := make(map[string]string, len(work))
        usedURI := make(map[string]string, len(work))
        for _, item := range work {
            segment := &plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[item.index]
            source := item.source
            asset, ref, err := finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(prepared[item.index], item.request)
            if err != nil {
                return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared final_job segment %q: %w", segment.SegmentID, err)
            }
            if _, exists := usedSHA[asset.SHA256]; exists {
                // Identical bytes for a second placement. Derive THIS placement from
                // the certified object already produced above: the same bitstream in
                // a distinct container is a naming problem, and re-encoding the same
                // window would pay for pixels that already exist. The tag stays in
                // the work identity, so the tagged object can never be answered with
                // the untagged bytes.
                item.request.PlacementTag = segment.SegmentID
                item.request.ReuseFromSHA256 = asset.SHA256
                item.request.ReuseFromURI = usedURI[asset.SHA256]
                tagged, tagErr := preparer.PrepareFinalJobVideoSegment(ctx, source, item.request)
                if tagErr != nil {
                    return "", nil, finalJobSegmentPrepareError(item, tagErr)
                }
                asset, ref, err = finalJobPreparedSegmentAsset(tagged, item.request)
                if err != nil {
                    return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("prepared final_job segment %q: %w", segment.SegmentID, err)
                }
                if other, stillShared := usedSHA[asset.SHA256]; stillShared {
                    return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("final_job segment %q still certifies the bytes of another placement (%q); refusing to send a plan the assembler must reject", segment.SegmentID, other)
                }
            }
            usedSHA[asset.SHA256] = segment.SegmentID
            usedURI[asset.SHA256] = finalJobStringValue(ref["source_uri"])
            preparedAssets[asset.AssetID] = asset
            if strings.EqualFold(finalJobStringValue(source["role"]), "overlay_timeline") {
                ref["role"] = "overlay"
            }
            // One runtime reference per asset: every placement owns its own object,
            // so FINALIZE receives unique ids without duplicating work.
        attempt := 1
        if result.RemoteFinalJob != nil && result.RemoteFinalJob.Attempt > 0 {
            attempt = result.RemoteFinalJob.Attempt
        }
        key := finalJobAttemptIdempotencyKey(req.IdempotencyKey, runID, attempt)
        pre := map[string]any{
            "idempotency_key":             key,
            "job_type":                    "video.render.v2",
            "render_only":                 true,
            "video_name":                  finalJobVideoName(req, runID),
            "script_text":                 strings.TrimSpace(scriptText.String()),
            "compiled_render_plan_json":   compiledPlan,
            "compiled_render_plan_sha256": compiledPlanSHA,

            "script_text": strings.TrimSpace(scriptText.String()),
            "overlays":    remoteOverlays,

                "voiceover_volume":           1.0,
                "voiceover_duration_seconds": float64(result.FinalAudio.DurationMS) / 1000,
            }
        }
        finalize["runtime_payload"] = runtimePayload

            if err != nil {
                return nil, nil, err
            }
            compiledPlanSHA = digest.SHA256String(compiledPlan)

    import (
        capmodel "github.com/Marcuss-ops/PipelineGen/internal/capabilities/overlays/model"
    
        "context"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "math"

    )
    
    // Source preparation for the final job: the local preflight, the timestamp and
    // pixel-format normalisation of the composition source, and the publication
    // of the final receipt the runner reads back.
    
    // enforceFinalJobPreflight is the deterministic pre-enqueue gate: predictable
    // remote scene rejection classes fail locally before the Master PREPARE exists.
    func enforceFinalJobPreflight(scenes []map[string]any, certifiedAudioMS int64) error {
        if certifiedAudioMS <= 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("final_job preflight: certified audio duration must be positive")
        }
        for i, scene := range scenes {
            seconds, ok := scene["duration_seconds"].(float64)
            if !ok || math.IsNaN(seconds) || math.IsInf(seconds, 0) || seconds <= 0 {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job preflight: scene %d has an invalid duration %v", i, seconds)
            }
            if finalJobSceneMediaLocator(scene) == "" {
                id, _ := scene["scene_id"].(string)
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job preflight: scene %q carries no resolvable media locator (predicted remote prefetch rejection)", id)
            }
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    // finalJobSceneMediaLocator extracts the resolvable Drive locator from a
    // remote scene's media slot ("stock" for both stock and caller-clip kinds).
    func finalJobSceneMediaLocator(scene map[string]any) string {
        slot, ok := scene["stock"].(map[string]any)
        if !ok {
            return ""
        }
        if link := strings.TrimSpace(fmt.Sprint(slot["url"])); link != "" && link != "<nil>" {
            return link
        }
        if driveID := strings.TrimSpace(fmt.Sprint(slot["drive_file_id"])); driveID != "" && driveID != "<nil>" {
            return driveID
        }
        return ""
    }
    
    // restoreFinalJobFixedMedia keeps the canonical media-kind marker from the
    // original generated scenes after the audio-only projection rewrites fixed
    // intro/outro audio to silence or narration. The remote payload still needs to
    // resolve those clips from Drive as fixed media, not as generated body clips.
    func restoreFinalJobFixedMedia(result *GenerateResult, timeline *capabilityaudio.CanonicalTimeline) {
        if result == nil || timeline == nil {
            return
        }
        fixed := make(map[string]bool, len(result.Scenes))
        for _, scene := range result.Scenes {
            fixed[scene.ID] = scene.ExecutionMode.IsFixedMedia()
        }
        for i := range timeline.Segments {
            if isFixed, ok := fixed[timeline.Segments[i].ID]; ok {
                timeline.Segments[i].FixedMedia = isFixed
            }
        }
    }
    
    // normalizeFinalJobVideoBackground makes producer-local stock inputs safe for
    // Chronon's native frame-zero decoder. Drive clips can have their first video
    // sample at a small positive PTS (for example 21 ms); a composite starts at
    // zero and the native decoder correctly rejects a request before that sample.
    // The remote final job still receives the certified composite and its original
    // separately compiled final audio.
    //
    // The timestamp fix is done with a stream-copy remux first: `-copyts
    // -start_at_zero` shifts the first timestamp to 0 without decoding or
    // re-encoding, so a 3-minute 1080p source costs seconds instead of the 30-60s a
    // full libx264 pass costs on the critical path. The copy is only
    // attempted when the source video is already H.264/yuv420p (the intermediate
    // composite's expected format) AND the remuxed first packet actually lands on
    // zero; every other case falls back to the pre-existing re-encode, so the
    // correctness contract is unchanged.
    func normalizeFinalJobVideoBackground(ctx context.Context, plan capmodel.OverlayPlan) (capmodel.OverlayPlan, func(), error) {
        if plan.Source == nil {
            return plan, nil, nil
        }
        source := *plan.Source
        ffmpeg, err := exec.LookPath("ffmpeg")
        if err != nil {
            return plan, nil, fmt.Errorf("ffmpeg is required to normalize stock timestamps: %w", err)
        }
        workDir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "pipelinegen-final-composite-")
        if err != nil {
            return plan, nil, fmt.Errorf("create normalization workspace: %w", err)
        }
        cleanup := func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(workDir) }
        input := strings.TrimSpace(source.LocalPath)
        if input == "" {
            cleanup()
            return plan, nil, fmt.Errorf("source asset %q has no materialized local path", source.AssetID)
        }
        output := filepath.Join(workDir, "source.mp4")
        // Fast path: stream-copy remux. It is taken only when the source video is
        // already H.264/yuv420p (so the copy stays byte-compatible with the
        // intermediate composite) and the remuxed first packet lands on zero; any
        // doubt falls through to the re-encode below.
        if ffprobe, probeErr := exec.LookPath("ffprobe"); probeErr == nil {
            if sourceVideoIsH264YUV420P(ctx, ffprobe, input) {
                if copyErr := remuxFinalJobSourceTimestamps(ctx, ffmpeg, input, output); copyErr == nil {
                    if firstVideoPTSIsZero(ctx, ffprobe, output) {
                        return commitNormalizedFinalJobSource(plan, source.AssetID, output, cleanup)
                    }
                }
                _ = os.Remove(output)
            }
        }
        // Fallback: full re-encode (pre-existing behaviour) for a source that is
        // not already H.264/yuv420p, or whose stream-copied first timestamp did not
        // land on zero.
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, ffmpeg,
            "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-fflags", "+genpts",
            "-i", input, "-map", "0:v:0", "-an", "-vf", "setpts=PTS-STARTPTS",
            "-vsync", "0", "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "ultrafast", "-crf", "20",
            "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-avoid_negative_ts", "make_zero", "-movflags", "+faststart", output,
        )
        if combined, runErr := cmd.CombinedOutput(); runErr != nil {
            cleanup()
            return plan, nil, fmt.Errorf("normalize source asset %q: %w: %s", source.AssetID, runErr, strings.TrimSpace(string(combined)))
        }
        return commitNormalizedFinalJobSource(plan, source.AssetID, output, cleanup)
    }
    
    // commitNormalizedFinalJobSource hashes the normalized artifact, rejects an
    // empty result, and rewrites the plan's source to point at it. Both the remux
    // fast path and the re-encode fallback end here so the two cannot drift.
    func commitNormalizedFinalJobSource(plan capmodel.OverlayPlan, sourceAssetID, output string, cleanup func()) (capmodel.OverlayPlan, func(), error) {
        hash, size, hashErr := digest.SHA256File(output)
        if hashErr != nil {
            cleanup()
            return plan, nil, fmt.Errorf("hash normalized source asset %q: %w", sourceAssetID, hashErr)
        }
        if size == 0 {
            cleanup()
            return plan, nil, fmt.Errorf("normalized source asset %q is empty", sourceAssetID)
        }
        plan.Source = &capmodel.OverlaySource{
            AssetID:   "finaljob-video-" + hash[:16],
            Path:      "assets/semantic/finaljob-video-" + hash + ".mp4",
            LocalPath: output, SHA256: hash,
        }
        return plan, cleanup, nil
    }
    
    // remuxFinalJobSourceTimestamps stream-copies the source video into a
    // faststart MP4 whose first timestamp is shifted to zero. `-copyts` preserves
    // the input timestamps and `-start_at_zero` shifts the output so the first one
    // lands on zero — the only stream-copy combination that zeroes a POSITIVE first
    // PTS (`-avoid_negative_ts make_zero` fixes negative timestamps only and leaves
    // a positive start untouched). No frame is decoded or re-encoded.
    func remuxFinalJobSourceTimestamps(ctx context.Context, ffmpeg, input, output string) error {
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, ffmpeg,
            "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-fflags", "+genpts",
            "-i", input, "-map", "0:v:0", "-an",
            "-c", "copy", "-copyts", "-start_at_zero", "-movflags", "+faststart", output,
        )
        if combined, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(combined)))
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    // sourceVideoIsH264YUV420P reports whether the source's first video stream is
    // already the format the intermediate composite expects, so a stream copy is
    // byte-compatible and no re-encode is needed.
    func sourceVideoIsH264YUV420P(ctx context.Context, ffprobe, input string) bool {
        fields := ffprobeKeyValues(ctx, ffprobe,
            "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries", "stream=codec_name,pix_fmt", "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1", input)
        return strings.EqualFold(fields["codec_name"], "h264") &&
            strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(fields["pix_fmt"]), "yuv420p")
    }
    
    // firstVideoPTSIsZero reports whether the output's first video packet starts at
    // (or essentially at) timestamp zero. A non-zero first PTS is exactly the bug
    // this normalization exists to prevent, so the remux is rejected when it does
    // not hold and the caller falls back to the re-encode.
    func firstVideoPTSIsZero(ctx context.Context, ffprobe, path string) bool {
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, ffprobe, "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0",
            "-show_entries", "packet=pts_time", "-of", "csv=p=0", "-read_intervals", "%+#1", path)
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
            return false
        }
        for _, line := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
            line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
            if line == "" || line == "N/A" {
                continue
            }
            value, convErr := strconv.ParseFloat(line, 64)
            if convErr != nil {
                continue
            }
            return value >= -0.001 && value <= 0.001
        }
        return false
    }
    
    // ffprobeKeyValues runs ffprobe with the given arguments and returns its
    // `<key>=<value>` output lines as a map. A probe failure yields an empty map,
    // which every caller treats as "cannot prove the copy is safe".
    func ffprobeKeyValues(ctx context.Context, ffprobe string, args ...string) map[string]string {
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, ffprobe, append([]string{"-v", "error"}, args...)...)
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
            return map[string]string{}
        }
        fields := make(map[string]string)
        for _, line := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
            key, value, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(line), "=")
            if !ok {
                continue
            }
            fields[strings.TrimSpace(key)] = strings.TrimSpace(value)
        }
        return fields
    }
    
    // finalJobReceiptSucceeded reports whether the durable receipt already records
    // a COMPLETED remote render.
    func finalJobReceiptSucceeded(receipt *RemoteFinalJobResult) bool {
        return receipt != nil && strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(receipt.Status), "SUCCEEDED")
    }
    
    func finalJobReceiptTerminal(receipt *RemoteFinalJobResult) bool {
        if receipt == nil {
            return false
        }
        switch strings.ToUpper(strings.TrimSpace(receipt.Status)) {
        case "FAILED", "CANCELLED", "CANCELED", "REJECTED":
            return true
        default:
            return false
        }
    }
    
    // finalJobPendingID returns the Master job id a previous attempt left in
    // flight, or "" when there is nothing to resume.
    func finalJobPendingID(receipt *RemoteFinalJobResult) string {
        if receipt == nil || finalJobReceiptSucceeded(receipt) || finalJobReceiptTerminal(receipt) {
            return ""
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(receipt.JobID)
    }
    
    // finalJobDurableReceipt reads the receipt the RUN has persisted, which is the
    // authoritative record of a remote render this run already started. The
    // in-memory result only carries it when the attempt ADOPTED the checkpoint (see
    // executionRun.start); a replay that rebuilt the result — or a fresh process
    // resuming the run — must not lose the handle, because losing it means asking
    // the Master for a second render of work it is already doing.
    func (r *Runner) finalJobDurableReceipt(ctx context.Context, runID string) *RemoteFinalJobResult {
        if r.repo == nil {
            return nil
        }
        run, err := r.repo.Get(ctx, runID)
        if err != nil || run == nil || run.Result == nil {
            return nil
        }
        return run.Result.RemoteFinalJob
    }
    
    // submitFinalJob drives the optional remote render handoff. It is attach-first
    // on purpose: an attempt that finds a pending receipt resumes THAT job, because
    // a second PREPARE asks the Master for a second render of work it is already
    // doing. Only a run with no receipt submits, and a run whose receipt is already
    // SUCCEEDED is skipped entirely (a later phase failed the run after the render
    // finished).
    func (r *Runner) submitFinalJob(ctx context.Context, runID string, req GenerateRequest, result *GenerateResult) bool {

            r.failRunWithRetry(ctx, runID, StagePublishingDocuments, fmt.Errorf("final_job=true but remote final-job submitter is not configured"))
            return false
        }
        r.auditFinalJobArtifactReuse(runID, result)
        receipt := (*RemoteFinalJobResult)(nil)
        if result != nil {
            receipt = result.RemoteFinalJob
        }
        if receipt == nil {
            receipt = r.finalJobDurableReceipt(ctx, runID)
            if receipt != nil && result != nil {
                result.RemoteFinalJob = receipt
            }
        }
        if finalJobReceiptSucceeded(receipt) {
            if r.log != nil {
                r.log.Info("remote final job already completed by an earlier attempt; reusing its receipt",
                    zap.String("run_id", runID), zap.String("remote_job_id", receipt.JobID))
            }
            return true
        }
        attempt := 1
        if receipt != nil {
            attempt = receipt.Attempt
            if attempt < 1 {
                attempt = 1

                if result != nil {
                    result.RemoteFinalJobHistory = append(result.RemoteFinalJobHistory, *receipt)
                }
                attempt++
            }
            // A receipt without a job id is a durable PREPARE intent. Reuse its
            // attempt key so a lost PREPARE response reconciles to the same lease.
        }
        if jobID := finalJobPendingID(receipt); jobID != "" {
            attacher, ok := r.finalJobSubmitter.(FinalJobAttacher)
            if !ok {
                // Fail closed: the wired submitter cannot wait on the job this run
                // already started, and submitting again would duplicate a render the
                // Master is already performing.
                r.failRunWithRetry(ctx, runID, StagePublishingDocuments, fmt.Errorf(
                    "remote final job %s is still in flight but the wired submitter cannot resume it (%T does not implement FinalJobAttacher)", jobID, r.finalJobSubmitter))
                return false
            }
            if r.log != nil {
                r.log.Info("resuming remote final job",
                    zap.String("run_id", runID), zap.String("remote_job_id", jobID),
                    zap.Int("yields", receipt.Yields), zap.Bool("wait_to_completion", receipt.Yields > 0))
            }
            remote, err := attacher.AttachFinalJob(ctx, jobID, receipt.Yields > 0)
            remote.Attempt = receipt.Attempt
            // The durable receipt already carries the locally measured handoff (and,
            // on a resumed job, possibly earlier Master phases); keep them when the
            // attach result only reports its own side.
            remote.Timing = receipt.Timing.Merge(remote.Timing)
            return r.settleFinalJob(ctx, runID, result, remote, receipt.Yields, err)
        }
        if starter, ok := r.finalJobSubmitter.(FinalJobStarter); ok {
            if result == nil {
                return r.settleFinalJob(ctx, runID, result, RemoteFinalJobResult{}, 0, fmt.Errorf("remote final job has no result to checkpoint before PREPARE"))
            }
            intent := RemoteFinalJobResult{Status: "PREPARE_INTENT", Attempt: attempt}
            result.RemoteFinalJob = &intent
            if err := r.repo.SavePartialResult(ctx, runID, result); err != nil {
                return r.settleFinalJob(ctx, runID, result, intent, 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint PREPARE intent: %w", ErrFinalJobReceiptCheckpoint, err))
            }
            remote, err := starter.StartFinalJob(ctx, runID, req, result)
            remote.Attempt = attempt
            if err != nil {
                return r.settleFinalJob(ctx, runID, result, remote, 0, err)
            }
            if strings.TrimSpace(remote.JobID) == "" {
                return r.settleFinalJob(ctx, runID, result, remote, 0, fmt.Errorf("remote final job starter returned no job id"))
            }
            remote.Yields = 0
            result.RemoteFinalJob = &remote
            if err := r.repo.SavePartialResult(ctx, runID, result); err != nil {
                return r.settleFinalJob(ctx, runID, result, remote, 0, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint remote final job %s before attach: %w", remote.JobID, err))
            }
            attacher, ok := r.finalJobSubmitter.(FinalJobAttacher)
            if !ok {
                return r.settleFinalJob(ctx, runID, result, remote, 0, fmt.Errorf("remote final job starter cannot attach to job %s", remote.JobID))
            }
            attached, err := attacher.AttachFinalJob(ctx, remote.JobID, false)
            attached.Attempt = attempt
            // StartFinalJob measured the local handoff; the attach result knows the
            // Master phases. The persisted receipt must carry both.
            attached.Timing = remote.Timing.Merge(attached.Timing)
            return r.settleFinalJob(ctx, runID, result, attached, 0, err)
        }

    // validateFinalJobPlanBindingRules mirrors the admission surface the remote
    // assembler applies to a compiled V2 plan, so a plan the worker would reject is
    // rejected in this process instead. The rules were confirmed against the worker
    // contract on 2026-11-01:
    //
    //   - assets[] must carry unique ids, and two assets may not share one
    //     asset_key: the resolver rejects a second id for the same content;
    //   - two assets may not certify the same bytes, because the plan refuses two
    //     assets with one canonical identity;
    //   - several segments MAY reference one asset. The placement lives on the
    //     segment — unique segment_id, own timeline_start_frame and frame_count —
    //     so a repeated window is one artifact referenced twice.
    //
    // The last rule is why identical work is canonicalised by sha256 before this
    // check runs: the plan is only correct when every distinct byte-set has exactly
    // one asset, whatever number of placements point at it.
    func validateFinalJobPlanBindingRules(plan finalJobCompiledPlan) error {
        byID := make(map[string]finalJobPlanAsset, len(plan.Assets))
        byKey := make(map[string]string, len(plan.Assets))
        bySHA := make(map[string]string, len(plan.Assets))
        for _, asset := range plan.Assets {
            id := strings.TrimSpace(asset.AssetID)
            if id == "" {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan asset without an id")
            }
            if _, exists := byID[id]; exists {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan assets repeat id %q", id)
            }
            byID[id] = asset
            key := strings.TrimSpace(asset.AssetKey)
            if key == "" {
                key = "sha256:" + strings.ToLower(asset.SHA256)
            }
            if owner, exists := byKey[key]; exists {
                return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan assets %q and %q share one asset key %q", owner, id, key)
            }
            byKey[key] = id
            if sha := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(asset.SHA256)); sha != "" {
                if owner, exists := bySHA[sha]; exists {
                    return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan assets %q and %q certify the same bytes %s", owner, id, sha)
                }
                bySHA[sha] = id
            }
        }
        seenSegment := make(map[string]struct{}, len(plan.Assets))
        for _, track := range plan.VideoTracks {
            for _, segment := range track.Segments {
                id := strings.TrimSpace(segment.SegmentID)
                if id == "" {
                    return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan segment without an id")
                }
                if _, exists := seenSegment[id]; exists {
                    return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan segments repeat id %q", id)
                }
                seenSegment[id] = struct{}{}
                asset, ok := byID[segment.AssetID]
                if !ok {
                    return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan segment %q references unknown asset %q", id, segment.AssetID)
                }
                if !strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(asset.SHA256), strings.TrimSpace(segment.SHA256)) {
                    return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan segment %q does not certify its asset %q", id, asset.AssetID)
                }
                if segment.FrameCount <= 0 {
                    return fmt.Errorf("final_job plan segment %q has no frame span", id)
                }
            }
        }
        return nil
    }

    func TestBuildFinalJobPayloadsUsesPublishedPhraseVideoForPhraseOnlyScene(t *testing.T) {
        result := phraseOnlyFinalJobResult("scene-phrase")
        pre, finalize, err := BuildFinalJobPayloads(context.Background(), "run-phrase", GenerateRequest{Title: "Garlasco", SourceLanguage: "it"}, result, finalJobPayloadResolver{})
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("BuildFinalJobPayloads: %v", err)
        }
        plan := decodeFinalJobPlanForTest(t, pre)
        if len(plan.VideoTracks) != 1 || len(plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments) != 1 {
            t.Fatalf("compiled phrase plan tracks = %#v, want one phrase-video segment", plan.VideoTracks)
        }
        segment := plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[0]
        if segment.AssetID != "phrase-video" || segment.FrameCount != 120 || segment.SourceInUS != 0 {
            t.Fatalf("compiled phrase segment = %+v, want the certified 5s timeline video", segment)
        }
        var phraseAsset *finalJobPlanAsset
        for i := range plan.Assets {
            if plan.Assets[i].AssetID == "phrase-video" {
                phraseAsset = &plan.Assets[i]
                break
            }
        }
        if phraseAsset == nil || phraseAsset.SHA256 != strings.Repeat("c", 64) {
            t.Fatalf("compiled phrase assets = %+v, want certified phrase-video identity", plan.Assets)
        }
        assets := finalize["runtime_assets"].([]any)
        roles := map[string]int{}
        for _, raw := range assets {
            roles[raw.(map[string]any)["role"].(string)]++
        }
        if roles["clip"] != 1 || roles["final_audio"] != 1 || roles["overlay_timeline"] != 1 {
            t.Fatalf("runtime_assets = %#v, want phrase video, final audio, and its timeline reference", assets)
        }
        runtimePayload := finalize["runtime_payload"].(map[string]any)
        overlays := runtimePayload["overlays"].([]any)
        if len(overlays) != 0 {
            t.Fatalf("finalize overlays = %#v, want consumed phrase video omitted to avoid rendering its animation twice", overlays)
        }
        manifest, ok := runtimePayload["overlay_manifest"].(map[string]any)
        if !ok {
            t.Fatalf("finalize overlay_manifest = %#v, want the typed manifest document", runtimePayload["overlay_manifest"])
        }
        if entries := manifest["entries"].([]any); len(entries) != 0 {
            t.Fatalf("manifest entries = %#v, want the consumed phrase omitted from placement", entries)
        }
    }

    func TestVideoAssembleSlice_CopiesDriveSourceWindowsWithoutReencoding(t *testing.T) {
        plan := driveSlicePlan()
        canonical, err := plan.CanonicalJSON()
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        videoPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "stock.mp4")
        audioPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "audio.m4a")
        if err := os.WriteFile(videoPath, []byte("stock"), 0o640); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(audioPath, []byte("audio"), 0o640); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
        }
        renderer := &sliceNativeRenderer{}
        runner := pipeline.NewRunner(nil, renderer, nil)
        exec := &videoAssembleSliceExecutor{runner: runner, prober: sliceMediaProbeStub{}, outputRoot: t.TempDir()}
        spec := executorTaskSpec(VideoAssembleSliceID, "job-drive-slice", canonical, plan)
        result, err := exec.Execute(runtimeassets.WithBindings(context.Background(), runtimeassets.Bindings{
            "drive:stock-01": {AssetID: "drive:stock-01", Path: videoPath, SHA256: strings.Repeat("b", 64), Size: 5, Verified: true},
            "audio":          {AssetID: "audio", Path: audioPath, SHA256: copyOnlySHA([]byte("audio")), Size: 5, Verified: true},
        }), nil, spec)
        if err != nil || result.Status != "succeeded" {
            t.Fatalf("slice execution result=%+v err=%v", result, err)
        }
        if len(result.Outputs) != 1 || result.RawMetrics == nil || result.RawMetrics.ConcatMode != "packet_copy" || result.RawMetrics.EncodePasses != 0 || !result.RawMetrics.FinalConcatStreamCopy {
            t.Fatalf("slice result did not report copy-only remote assembly: %+v", result)
        }
        if renderer.calls != 1 {
            t.Fatalf("native packet renderer call count = %d, want one", renderer.calls)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(string(renderer.wire), `"bindings"`) || !strings.Contains(string(renderer.wire), `"output_path"`) {
            t.Fatalf("native render did not receive the bound compiled plan: %s", renderer.wire)
        }
    }
    
    func TestVideoAssembleSlice_RejectsNonKeyframeOffsetBeforeFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
        plan := driveSlicePlan()
        plan.VideoTracks[0].Segments[0].SourceInUS = 14_000_000
        canonical, err := plan.CanonicalJSON()

            t.Fatalf("invalid copy plan result=%+v err=%v, want immediate failure", result, err)
        }
        if result.ErrorCode != "DRIVE_SLICE_PLAN_INVALID" || renderer.calls != 0 {
            t.Fatalf("invalid cut was not rejected before native mux: result=%+v native_calls=%d", result, renderer.calls)
        }
    }

    // startFinalJobStockPrewarm overlaps the final-job stock resolution with the
    // overlay render. It never blocks the phase and never fails the run: the
    // prewarm goroutine only fills the submitter's per-handoff cache, and the
    // handoff re-walks the same selection through the same planner.
    //
    // The goroutine gets a SNAPSHOT of the result, not the live one: the overlay
    // phase writes result.OverlayRender / result.LocalizedOverlayRenders when it
    // joins, while the walk only reads the canonical timeline and the scenes — a
    // copy keeps those reads in one memory location the phase never writes.
    func (r *Runner) startFinalJobStockPrewarm(ctx context.Context, runID string, req GenerateRequest, result *GenerateResult) {
        if !req.FinalJob || result == nil || r.finalJobSubmitter == nil {
            return
        }
        prewarmer, ok := r.finalJobSubmitter.(FinalJobSourcePrewarmer)
        if !ok {
            return
        }
        // Once per run: the join branch and the serial phase are exclusive, but a
        // resumed attempt or a re-entered phase must not walk twice.
        r.prewarmMu.Lock()
        already := r.prewarmRunID == runID
        if !already {
            r.prewarmRunID = runID
        }
        r.prewarmMu.Unlock()
        if already {
            return
        }
        snapshot := *result
        workRes := &snapshot
        startedAt := time.Now()
        go func() {
            err := prewarmer.PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx, runID, req, workRes)
            if r.log == nil {
                return
            }
            fields := []zap.Field{zap.String("run_id", runID), zap.Duration("wall", time.Since(startedAt))}
            if err != nil {
                r.log.Warn("final-job stock prewarm stopped early; the handoff resolves the rest serially", append(fields, zap.Error(err))...)
                return
            }
            r.log.Info("final-job stock prewarm finished", fields...)
        }()
    }
    
    // renderOverlayPlanAtBoundary is the ONLY place that chooses the submission
    // shape for one language plan (TICKET-OVERLAY-RENDER-PER-SCENE-2026-10-29).
    //
    // The per-scene split (one composition per scene window, N independent GPU
    // round-trips instead of one whole-timeline pass) is opt-in via
    // OVERLAY_RENDER_PER_SCENE and now applies to final jobs too: the worker's
    // final manifest carries artifacts[] and the V2 plan binds one asset per
    // distinct byte-set, so several certified overlay artifacts are a supported
    // shape (the wire becomes pipelinegen.overlay-manifest-set.v1, one manifest per
    // batch). Single-scene plans never split (degenerate case of the same shape),
    // and enqueuers without the Split capability keep the single path — including
    // every test mock, so flag OFF and capability-missing both reproduce the
    // single-timeline behaviour byte for byte.
    //
    // Fail-closed fallback: a SPLIT ERROR falls back to the single-timeline
    // submission, so a flag-ON run can only ever end up with more GPU work, never
    // a different failure surface than the certified path. A split that RENDERS but
    // whose batch set cannot be certified is a different class: it is a defective
        // audioAssetSource turns the run's BGM/SFX asset_ids into verified
        // local paths + certified durations before the audio plan is compiled.
        // Nil means the audio intent block is not resolvable — a run that
        // carries BGM/SFX intents fails closed in the audio-compile phase.
        audioAssetSource        AudioAssetSource

    const deprecatedFinalJobWorker51ID = "velox-worker-523925eb"
    
    // finalJobWorkerPin is the placement pin for a handoff, or "" when the Master
    // must place the job itself. There is deliberately no default: an operator pin
    // is a deployment fact (which worker is healthy), not something this binary can
    // know. The retired worker-51 default is rejected loudly instead of silently
    // resurrected by a stale environment file.
    func finalJobWorkerPin() (string, error) {
        pin := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_WORKER_ID"))
        if pin == "" {
            return "", nil
        }
        if pin == deprecatedFinalJobWorker51ID {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_WORKER_ID pins the retired worker %s; unset it to let the Master place the job", pin)
        }
        return pin, nil
    }
    
    // finalJobQueueBudget reads VELOX_FINAL_JOB_QUEUE_SECONDS: how long a handoff
    // may wait for the Master to lease and START the job before the wait is handed
    // back. It bounds the failure mode r9 exposed (46 minutes in PENDING, then a
    // cancellation): a queued job cannot finish, so holding the local worker for
    // the whole render budget buys nothing. 0 disables the queue budget. A
    // malformed value is a configuration error, not a silent default.
    func finalJobQueueBudget() (time.Duration, error) {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_QUEUE_SECONDS"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobQueueBudget, nil
        }
        seconds, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || seconds < 0 {
            return 0, fmt.Errorf("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_QUEUE_SECONDS must be a non-negative integer number of seconds, got %q", raw)
        }
        return time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second, nil
    }
    
    // defaultFinalJobQueueBudget is generous for a healthy Master (r101 leased in
    // 0 s, r103 in 58 s) and far below the 46-minute stall that motivated it.
    const defaultFinalJobQueueBudget = 3 * time.Minute

    // A malformed value is a configuration error, not a silent default.
    func finalJobAttachBudget() (time.Duration, error) {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_ATTACH_SECONDS"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobAttachBudget, nil
        }
        seconds, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || seconds < 0 {

        }
        return time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second, nil
    }

    // resolveHits reports the resolutions answered from the handoff cache, so a
    // receipt can tell deduplicated work from work that never happened.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolveHits() int {
        if a == nil {
            return 0
        }
        a.resolvedMu.Lock()
        defer a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        return a.hits
    }
    
    // finalJobStockCacheDir is where a Drive stock file is kept between runs. The
    // handoff publishes every source it sends, and publishing needs the bytes; the
    // same file id with the same byte size is the same bytes, so the next run must
    // not pay the network again. VELOX_FINAL_JOB_STOCK_CACHE_DIR relocates it.
    func finalJobStockCacheDir() string {
        if dir := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_STOCK_CACHE_DIR")); dir != "" {
            return dir
        }
        return filepath.Join("data", "cache", "final_job_stock")
    }
    
    // stagedStockPath returns a local copy of one Drive stock file, downloading it
    // only when the cache does not already hold exactly that many bytes. The size is
    // part of the cache key: a file that changed identity cannot be served stale.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) stagedStockPath(ctx context.Context, id string, size int64) (string, func(), error) {
        dir := finalJobStockCacheDir()
        cached := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d.bin", id, size))
        if info, err := os.Stat(cached); err == nil && info.Size() == size {
            return cached, func() {}, nil
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("create stock cache %q: %w", dir, err)
        }
        tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".stock-*")
        if err != nil {
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("stage stock file in %q: %w", dir, err)
        }
        tmpPath := tmp.Name()
        discard := func() { _ = os.Remove(tmpPath) }
        reader, _, err := a.stock.DownloadFile(ctx, id)
        if err != nil {
            _ = tmp.Close()
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("download stock Drive file %q: %w", id, err)
        }
        written, copyErr := io.Copy(tmp, reader)
        readerErr := reader.Close()
        fileErr := tmp.Close()
        if copyErr != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("copy stock Drive file %q: %w", id, copyErr)
        }
        if readerErr != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("close stock Drive response %q: %w", id, readerErr)
        }
        if fileErr != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("close staged stock file %q: %w", id, fileErr)
        }
        if written != size {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("stock Drive file %q downloaded %d bytes, expected %d", id, written, size)
        }
        if err := os.Rename(tmpPath, cached); err != nil {
            discard()
            return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("commit stock cache entry %q: %w", cached, err)
        }
        return cached, func() {}, nil
    }
    
    // ResolveFinalJobStockAsset retains the explicitly allowed Drive path for
    // selected stock-folder videos. Every other final-job asset goes through the
    // HTTPS Objectstore resolver above.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) ResolveFinalJobStockAsset(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        return a.resolveOnce("drive:"+strings.TrimSpace(id), func() (map[string]any, error) {
            return a.resolveStockAssetOnce(ctx, id)
        })
    }
    
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) resolveStockAssetOnce(ctx context.Context, id string) (map[string]any, error) {
        defer a.resolverClock()()
        started := time.Now()
        defer func() {
            log.Printf("final_job resolve kind=drive id=%s ms=%d", id, time.Since(started).Milliseconds())
        }()
        if a == nil || a.stock == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job stock Drive reader is not configured")
        }
        id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
        if id == "" || strings.ContainsAny(id, "/\\\x00\r\n") {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("final-job stock Drive id is invalid")
        }
        meta, err := a.stock.GetFileMeta(ctx, id)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("read stock Drive metadata %q: %w", id, err)
        }
        if meta == nil || meta.Size <= 0 {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("stock Drive file %q has no positive byte size", id)
        }
    
        path, cleanup, err := a.stagedStockPath(ctx, id, meta.Size)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        defer cleanup()
        // A staged stock file is written once, by us, from the Drive bytes of that
        // exact id and size — the same identity the staging cache already trusts to
        // serve the file without downloading it again. Hashing, probing and signing
        // those same bytes on every later handoff is therefore repeated work, not
        // verification: the receipt written next to the file answers all three.
        // Fail-closed: a receipt that does not describe exactly this file is dropped
        // and the bytes are re-derived.
        if receipt, ok := readFinalJobStockReceipt(path, meta.Size); ok {
            ref, publishErr := scriptgen.PublishFinalJobLocalObjectVerified(ctx, "stock-sha256-"+receipt.SHA256[:24], path, receipt.SHA256, receipt.SizeBytes)
            if publishErr == nil {
                ref["duration_ms"] = receipt.DurationMS
                return ref, nil
            }
        }
        hash, size, err := digest.SHA256File(path)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("hash stock Drive file %q: %w", id, err)
        }
        if a.probe == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("canonical media probe is not configured")
        }
        info, probeErr := a.probe.Probe(ctx, path)
        if info == nil || !info.HasVideo {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("probe stock Drive video %q: video stream is missing", id)
        }
        resolved := asset.ResolveAssetDuration(info.Duration.Microseconds(), probeErr, 0, false)
        if !resolved.Known() {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("probe stock Drive video %q: duration is unknown: %w", id, probeErr)
        }
        durationMS := resolved.DurationUS / 1000
        assetID := "stock-sha256-" + hash[:24]
        ref, err := scriptgen.PublishFinalJobLocalObject(ctx, assetID, path, hash, size)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("publish stock Drive file %q to HTTPS Objectstore: %w", id, err)
        }
        ref["duration_ms"] = durationMS
        writeFinalJobStockReceipt(path, finalJobStockReceipt{SHA256: hash, SizeBytes: size, DurationMS: durationMS})
        return ref, nil
    }
    
    // finalJobStockReceipt is what resolving a staged stock file produced: its
    // content address and the duration the probe reported. It is bound to the exact
    // staged file (size) so a re-downloaded or replaced file can never be served
    // from a stale receipt.
    type finalJobStockReceipt struct {
        SHA256     string `json:"sha256"`
        SizeBytes  int64  `json:"size_bytes"`
        DurationMS int64  `json:"duration_ms"`
    }
    
    func finalJobStockReceiptPath(staged string) string { return staged + ".resolve.json" }
    
    func readFinalJobStockReceipt(staged string, size int64) (finalJobStockReceipt, bool) {
        payload, err := os.ReadFile(finalJobStockReceiptPath(staged))
        if err != nil {
            return finalJobStockReceipt{}, false
        }
        var receipt finalJobStockReceipt
        if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &receipt); err != nil {
            return finalJobStockReceipt{}, false
        }
        if len(receipt.SHA256) != 64 || receipt.SizeBytes != size || receipt.DurationMS <= 0 {
            return finalJobStockReceipt{}, false
        }
        return receipt, true
    }
    
    // writeFinalJobStockReceipt is best-effort: a handoff that cannot persist the
    // receipt is slower next time, never wrong.
    func writeFinalJobStockReceipt(staged string, receipt finalJobStockReceipt) {
        payload, err := json.Marshal(receipt)

    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) ListFinalJobStockFolder(ctx context.Context, folderID string) ([]scriptgen.FinalJobStockFile, error) {
        defer a.resolverClock()()
        if a == nil || a.stock == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("remote final-job stock Drive reader is not configured")
        }
        listed, err := a.stock.ListFiles(ctx, folderID)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        files := make([]scriptgen.FinalJobStockFile, 0, len(listed))
        for _, f := range listed {
            if strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(f.MimeType), "video/") || strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(f.Name), ".mp4") {
                files = append(files, scriptgen.FinalJobStockFile{ID: f.ID, Name: f.Name})
            }
        }
        sort.Slice(files, func(i, j int) bool { return files[i].Name < files[j].Name })
        return files, nil
    }

        }
        base := ""
        if v := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_MASTER_URL")); v != "" {
            base = v

        if base == "" {
            base = defaultFinalJobMasterURL
        }
        masterURL, err := url.Parse(base)
        if err != nil || masterURL == nil || masterURL.Scheme != "https" || masterURL.Host == "" {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("remote final-job master URL must use HTTPS")
        }
        budget, err := finalJobAttachBudget()
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        queueBudget, err := finalJobQueueBudget()
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        client := remotejob.New(base, token)
        client.QueueTimeout = queueBudget
        return &remoteFinalJobAdapter{media: pgmedia.NewMediaSearcher(root.MediaPostgres), stock: root.Drive.Reader, client: client, attachBudget: budget, queueBudget: queueBudget}, nil
    }
    
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) SubmitFinalJob(ctx context.Context, runID string, req scriptgen.GenerateRequest, result *scriptgen.GenerateResult) (scriptgen.RemoteFinalJobResult, error) {
        started, err := a.StartFinalJob(ctx, runID, req, result)
        if err != nil {
            return started, err
        }
        remote, waitErr := a.client.Attach(ctx, started.JobID, a.attachBudget)
        receipt := finalJobResult(started.JobID, remote)
        // The attach result only knows Master-clock phases; the locally measured
        // handoff belongs to the receipt the submission produced.
        receipt.Timing = mergeFinalJobTiming(started.Timing, receipt.Timing)
        return receipt, finalJobWaitError(waitErr)
    }

    func TestPrepareFinalJobSegmentsRunsLanesAndKeepsPlanOrder(t *testing.T) {
        timelineSHA := strings.Repeat("a", 64)
        work := make([]finalJobSegmentWork, 0, 6)
        for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
            work = append(work, finalJobSegmentWork{
                index:  i,
                source: map[string]any{"asset_id": "stock-raw", "sha256": strings.Repeat("d", 64)},
                request: FinalJobVideoSegmentRequest{
                    SegmentID: fmt.Sprintf("segment-%04d", i), SourceSHA256: strings.Repeat("d", 64),
                    SourceDurationUS: 1_000_000, FrameCount: 24,
                    TimelineRevision: 1, TimelineSHA256: timelineSHA,
                },
            })
        }
        stub := &concurrentSegmentStub{lanes: 3, failIndex: -1}
        prepared, err := finalJobPrepareSegments(context.Background(), stub, work)
        if err != nil {
            t.Fatalf("finalJobPrepareSegments: %v", err)
        }
        if len(prepared) != len(work) {
            t.Fatalf("prepared %d segments, want %d", len(prepared), len(work))
        }
        for i, raw := range prepared {
            if got, want := raw["asset_id"], fmt.Sprintf("fragment-segment-%04d", i); got != want {
                t.Fatalf("prepared[%d] = %v, want %v (results must stay in plan order)", i, got, want)
            }
        }
        if peak := atomic.LoadInt32(&stub.peak); peak < 2 {
            t.Fatalf("peak concurrency = %d, want the lanes to actually overlap", peak)
        }
        if peak := atomic.LoadInt32(&stub.peak); peak > int32(stub.lanes) {
            t.Fatalf("peak concurrency = %d, want it bounded by %d lanes", peak, stub.lanes)
        }
    }
    
    func TestPrepareFinalJobSegmentsReportsTheFirstPlanFailure(t *testing.T) {
        timelineSHA := strings.Repeat("a", 64)
        work := make([]finalJobSegmentWork, 0, 4)
        for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
            work = append(work, finalJobSegmentWork{
                index:  i,
                source: map[string]any{"asset_id": "stock-raw", "sha256": strings.Repeat("d", 64)},
                request: FinalJobVideoSegmentRequest{
                    SegmentID: fmt.Sprintf("segment-%04d", i), SourceSHA256: strings.Repeat("d", 64),
                    SourceDurationUS: 1_000_000, FrameCount: 24,
                    TimelineRevision: 1, TimelineSHA256: timelineSHA,
                },
            })
        }
        stub := &concurrentSegmentStub{lanes: 2, failIndex: 1}
        _, err := finalJobPrepareSegments(context.Background(), stub, work)
        if err == nil {
            t.Fatal("finalJobPrepareSegments = nil error, want the rejected segment")
        }
        if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "segment-0001") {
            t.Fatalf("error = %v, want it to name the first failing plan position", err)
        }
        if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "context canceled") {
            t.Fatalf("error = %v, want the real cause, not the cancellation", err)
        }
    }

    // Runtime-asset resolution for the remote final job: the identity cache, the
    // stock staging and its receipts, and the prefetch lanes that keep handoff
        // for next (r73: a 240-file folder, 61 of them consumed, 12 warmed → 10,9 s
        // still spent on the critical path). 64 covers a long timeline at ~5 s per
        // source while costing ceil(64/6)·190 ms ≈ 2 s of wall instead of 64·190 ms.
        // A folder of hundreds is never resolved wholesale.
        finalJobPrefetchPerFolder = 64
    )
    
    // finalJobResolveConcurrency reads VELOX_FINAL_JOB_RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY. Absent
    // means the measured default, 1 means the pre-2026-11-01 serial handoff, and a
    // malformed value degrades to serial rather than inventing parallelism.
    func finalJobResolveConcurrency() int {
        raw := strings.TrimSpace(knobs.String("VELOX_FINAL_JOB_RESOLVE_CONCURRENCY"))
        if raw == "" {
            return defaultFinalJobResolveConcurrency
        }
        value, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
        if err != nil || value < 1 {
            return 1
        }
        if value > maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency {
            return maxFinalJobResolveConcurrency
        }
        return value
    }
    
    // PrewarmFinalJobStockSources is the capability the scripts runner calls while
    // the overlay render is still running (FinalJobSourcePrewarmer). It walks the
    // FINAL JOB's own stock selection through the same planner the payload build
    // uses, so the identities it resolves are exactly the ones the handoff would
    // have resolved serially, and the handoff then answers them from this cache.
    //
    // It never fails the run: the error is returned for the log, and the handoff
    // re-walks the same selection and reports its own error.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx context.Context, runID string, req scriptgen.GenerateRequest, result *scriptgen.GenerateResult) error {
        if a == nil || result == nil {
            return nil
        }
        // The prewarm owns the cache of THIS run; StartFinalJob keeps it because it
        // sees the same run id.
        a.beginHandoffCache(runID)
        started := time.Now()
        windows, err := scriptgen.PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx, result, a)
        a.resolvedMu.Lock()
        unique := len(a.resolved)
        a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        log.Printf("final_job prewarm kind=stock windows=%d unique_resolved=%d wall_ms=%d err=%v",
            windows, unique, time.Since(started).Milliseconds(), err)
        return err
    }
    
    // beginHandoffCache scopes the per-handoff resolution cache to ONE run without
    // throwing away what a prewarm of the SAME run already resolved.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) beginHandoffCache(runID string) {
        if a == nil {
            return
        }
        runID = strings.TrimSpace(runID)
        a.resolvedMu.Lock()
        defer a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
        if a.resolvedRunID == runID && a.resolved != nil {
            return
        }
        a.resolvedRunID = runID
        a.resolved = nil
        a.hits = 0
    }
    
    // PrefetchFinalJobStockAssets warms the handoff cache for the Drive sources one
    // stock folder is about to offer. It returns when every requested identity has
    // been attempted (or the context ended), and it never reports an error: a
    // source that cannot be warmed is resolved — and reported — by the walk.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) PrefetchFinalJobStockAssets(ctx context.Context, ids []string) {
        a.prefetchFinalJobSources(ctx, ids, a.ResolveFinalJobStockAsset)
    }
    
    // prefetchFinalJobSources is the scheduling half of the prefetch: dedupe, skip
    // what the cache already holds, then resolve with a bounded pool. The resolver
    // is a parameter so the scheduling is testable without a Drive or an object
    // store.
    func (a *remoteFinalJobAdapter) prefetchFinalJobSources(ctx context.Context, ids []string, resolve func(context.Context, string) (map[string]any, error)) {
        if a == nil || resolve == nil {
            return
        }
        workers := finalJobResolveConcurrency()
        if workers <= 1 {
            return
        }
        unique := make([]string, 0, len(ids))
        seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(ids))
        for _, raw := range ids {
            id := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
            if id == "" {
                continue
            }
            if _, ok := seen[id]; ok {
                continue
            }
            seen[id] = struct{}{}
            a.resolvedMu.Lock()
            _, cached := a.resolved["drive:"+id]
            a.resolvedMu.Unlock()
            if cached {
                continue
            }
            unique = append(unique, id)
            if len(unique) == finalJobPrefetchPerFolder {
                break
            }
        }
        if len(unique) == 0 {
            return
        }
        if len(unique) < workers {
            workers = len(unique)
        }
        started := time.Now()
        log.Printf("final_job prefetch kind=drive requested=%d warm=%d workers=%d", len(ids), len(unique), workers)
        queue := make(chan string)
        var wg sync.WaitGroup
        for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
            wg.Add(1)
            go func() {
                defer wg.Done()
                for id := range queue {
                    if ctx.Err() != nil {
                        return
                    }
                    if _, err := resolve(ctx, id); err != nil {
                        log.Printf("final_job prefetch kind=drive id=%s err=%v", id, err)
                    }
                }
            }()
        }
        for _, id := range unique {
            select {
            case queue <- id:
            case <-ctx.Done():
                close(queue)
                wg.Wait()
                return
            }
        }
        close(queue)
        wg.Wait()
        log.Printf("final_job prefetch kind=drive warm=%d wall_ms=%d", len(unique), time.Since(started).Milliseconds())
    }
    
    func copyFinalJobRef(ref map[string]any) map[string]any {
        if ref == nil {
            return nil
        }
        out := make(map[string]any, len(ref))
        for key, value := range ref {
            out[key] = value
        }
        return out
    }

    func (r *Runner) runOverlayRenderPhase(ctx context.Context, runID string, req GenerateRequest, exec ExecutionContext, resumeIdx int, state audioCompileState, result *GenerateResult) bool {

        r.applyOverlayRenderOutcomes(runID, result, outcomes)
        return true
    }

    // startFinalJobStockPrewarm overlaps the final-job stock resolution with the
    // overlay render. It never blocks the phase and never fails the run: the
    // prewarm goroutine only fills the submitter's per-handoff cache, and the
    // handoff re-walks the same selection through the same planner.
    //
    // The goroutine gets a SNAPSHOT of the result, not the live one: the overlay
    // phase writes result.OverlayRender / result.LocalizedOverlayRenders when it
    // joins, while the walk only reads the canonical timeline and the scenes — a
    // copy keeps those reads in one memory location the phase never writes.
    func (r *Runner) startFinalJobStockPrewarm(ctx context.Context, runID string, req GenerateRequest, result *GenerateResult) {
        if !req.FinalJob || result == nil || r.finalJobSubmitter == nil {
            return
        }
        prewarmer, ok := r.finalJobSubmitter.(FinalJobSourcePrewarmer)
        if !ok {
            return
        }
        // Once per run: the join branch and the serial phase are exclusive, but a
        // resumed attempt or a re-entered phase must not walk twice.
        r.prewarmMu.Lock()
        already := r.prewarmRunID == runID
        if !already {
            r.prewarmRunID = runID
        }
        r.prewarmMu.Unlock()
        if already {
            return
        }
        snapshot := *result
        workRes := &snapshot
        startedAt := time.Now()
        go func() {
            err := prewarmer.PrewarmFinalJobStockSources(ctx, runID, req, workRes)
            if r.log == nil {
                return
            }
            fields := []zap.Field{zap.String("run_id", runID), zap.Duration("wall", time.Since(startedAt))}
            if err != nil {
                r.log.Warn("final-job stock prewarm stopped early; the handoff resolves the rest serially", append(fields, zap.Error(err))...)
                return
            }
            r.log.Info("final-job stock prewarm finished", fields...)
        }()
    }
